mdcat-b10-chem-4.qHtml: What is the volume occupied by 4.4 grams of carbon dioxide (CO2) gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP, 273.15 K and 1 atm)? (Molar mass of CO2 = 44 g/mol; molar volume at STP = 22.414 L)
optionsHtml: 2.24 dm3 (or L)
mdcat-b10-chem-4.explainHtml: Moles of CO2 = mass / molar mass = 4.4 g / 44 g/mol = 0.10 mol. At STP, 1 mole of any ideal gas occupies 22.414 dm3. Volume = 0.10 mol × 22.414 dm3/mol = 2.24 dm3 (or liters).

mdcat-b10-chem-5.qHtml: According to Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity, how are the three 2p electrons distributed in the ground-state electronic configuration of a neutral nitrogen atom (Z = 7)?
optionsHtml: One electron resides in each of the three degenerate 2p orbitals (2px1, 2py1, 2pz1) with parallel spins
Two electrons pair in 2px2, one in 2py1, and 2pz remains vacant
All three electrons pair up in 2px^{3}
Two electrons reside in 2px with opposite spins and one is promoted to 3s
mdcat-b10-chem-5.explainHtml: Hund's rule states that when electrons occupy degenerate orbitals of equal energy, electrons remain unpaired with parallel spins before any orbital is doubly occupied. Nitrogen (1s22s22p3) has one unpaired electron with parallel spin in each of 2px, 2py, and 2pz.

mdcat-b10-chem-6.qHtml: What is the de Broglie wavelength (λ) associated with an electron of rest mass m = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg moving with a velocity of 2.0 × 10⁶ m/s? (Planck's constant h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s)

mdcat-b10-chem-7.qHtml: In the hydrogen atomic emission spectrum, electronic transitions ending at the principal quantum level n1 = 2 originate the Balmer series. In which region of the electromagnetic spectrum do Balmer spectral lines appear?
optionsHtml: Visible region (with the highest energy transitions extending into near-UV)
mdcat-b10-chem-7.explainHtml: The Lyman series (n1 = 1) falls in the ultraviolet region. The Balmer series (n1 = 2) falls in the visible region (approx. 400 nm to 700 nm, e.g., H-α at 656 nm is red, H-β at 486 nm is blue-green). The Paschen, Brackett, and Pfund series fall in the infrared region.

mdcat-b10-chem-8.qHtml: Which set of four quantum numbers (n, l, ml, ms) is physically impossible according to quantum mechanical selection rules and the Pauli exclusion principle?
mdcat-b10-chem-8.explainHtml: For any principal quantum number n, the azimuthal (orbital) quantum number l can only take integer values from 0 up to (n - 1). Therefore, when n = 3, l can only be 0, 1, or 2 (s, p, or d subshell). An orbital with l = 3 (an f-subshell) cannot exist in the third shell (n = 3).

mdcat-b10-chem-9.qHtml: In the van der Waals equation of state for real gases: [P + (n2a / V2)] (V - nb) = nRT, what physical molecular property does the constant "a" correct for?
optionsHtml: Intermolecular attractive forces between gas molecules that reduce pressure exerted on container walls
The finite excluded volume occupied by the gas molecules themselves
Inelastic collisions between gas molecules and container walls
Thermal dissociation of gas molecules at elevated pressures
mdcat-b10-chem-9.explainHtml: In the van der Waals equation, (n2a / V2) is the internal pressure correction accounting for intermolecular attractive forces (dispersion, dipole-dipole) that pull molecules inward and lessen wall impact pressure. The constant "b" accounts for the co-volume (excluded finite volume).

mdcat-b10-chem-10.qHtml: According to Graham's law of gaseous effusion, the rate of effusion of methane (CH4, molar mass = 16 g/mol) is how many times faster than that of sulfur dioxide (SO2, molar mass = 64 g/mol) under identical conditions of temperature and pressure?
mdcat-b10-chem-10.explainHtml: Graham's law states: Rate1 / Rate2 = {M2 / M1}. For CH4 vs SO2: Rate(CH4) / Rate(SO2) = {64 / 16} = {4} = 2.0. Therefore, methane effuses exactly twice as fast as sulfur dioxide.

mdcat-b10-chem-11.qHtml: A real gas approaches ideal gas behavior most closely under which combination of thermodynamic conditions?
mdcat-b10-chem-11.explainHtml: At low pressure, gas molecules are far apart, making their excluded volume negligible relative to the container volume. At high temperature, high kinetic energy overcomes attractive intermolecular forces. Thus, real gases behave most ideally at low pressure and high temperature.

mdcat-b10-chem-12.qHtml: The root-mean-square speed (v_rms) of gas molecules in Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution is directly proportional to:
optionsHtml: The square root of absolute temperature ({T})
The absolute temperature squared (T2)
The molar mass of the gas (M)
The ambient pressure independent of temperature
mdcat-b10-chem-12.explainHtml: From kinetic theory, v_rms = {3RT / M}. Hence, root-mean-square velocity is directly proportional to the square root of absolute temperature ({T}) and inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass (1/{M}).

mdcat-b10-chem-13.qHtml: Why does water (H2O) exhibit an anomalously higher normal boiling point (100°C) compared to hydrogen fluoride (HF, 19.5°C), even though fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen?
optionsHtml: Each H2O molecule can form an average of four hydrogen bonds forming a 3D network, whereas HF forms an average of only two hydrogen bonds per molecule
HF undergoes complete ionic dissociation in the gas phase
H2O has a much smaller molar mass than HF
The O-H covalent bond is shorter and weaker than the F-H bond
mdcat-b10-chem-13.explainHtml: Although the H-F bond dipole is stronger, an HF molecule has only one hydrogen atom (and three lone pairs), limiting it to an average of two hydrogen bonds per molecule (linear chains). An H2O molecule has two hydrogens and two lone pairs, forming an extensive tetrahedral network of four hydrogen bonds per molecule.

mdcat-b10-chem-14.qHtml: In the face-centered cubic (FCC) unit cell lattice of crystalline copper, what is the total effective number of copper atoms contained within a single unit cell?
mdcat-b10-chem-14.explainHtml: An FCC unit cell contains atoms at 8 corners and 6 faces: (8 corners × 1/8 share) + (6 face centers × 1/2 share) = 1 + 3 = 4 net atoms per unit cell. (Its atomic packing factor is 74%).

mdcat-b10-chem-15.qHtml: Isomorphism in crystallography refers to the phenomenon where two distinct chemical substances:
optionsHtml: Possess identical crystal forms and unit cell geometry because they have similar chemical formulas and atomic radius ratios
Exist in two or more distinct crystalline forms depending on crystallization temperature
Have identical empirical formulas but different molecular weights
Exhibit identical optical rotation of plane-polarized l
mdcat-b10-chem-15.explainHtml: Isomorphous substances (e.g., NaF and MgO, or K2SO4 and K2SeO4) have the same crystalline form because their constituent ions have identical stoichiometry and comparable ionic radius ratios. Polymorphism refers to a single chemical entity adopting multiple crystal structures.

mdcat-b10-chem-16.qHtml: The vapor pressure of a pure liquid in a closed container depends exclusively on which of the following variables?
optionsHtml: The temperature of the liquid and the nature of intermolecular forces
The surface area of the liquid exposed to the vapor space
The volume of empty headspace above the liquid
The total atmospheric pressure of the surrounding room
mdcat-b10-chem-16.explainHtml: Equilibrium vapor pressure is an intensive property defined by the Clausius-Clapeyron equation: ln(P) = -ΔH_vap / (RT) + C. It depends solely on temperature and the intrinsic strength of intermolecular attractive forces, and is independent of liquid surface area, volume, or ambient external pressure.

mdcat-b10-chem-17.qHtml: In the Born-Haber cycle for the formation of crystalline sodium chloride: Na(s) + 1/2 Cl2(g) → NaCl(s), which of the component thermodynamic steps is strongly exothermic?
optionsHtml: Lattice energy (condensation of gaseous Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions into crystalline lattice) and electron affinity of chlorine
Enthalpy of atomization of solid metallic sodium
First ionization energy of gaseous sodium atoms
Bond dissociation enthalpy of diatomic Cl2 gas
mdcat-b10-chem-17.explainHtml: In the Born-Haber cycle, atomization of Na(s), ionization of Na(g), and dissociation of Cl2(g) are endothermic (ΔH > 0). The electron affinity of Cl(g) (ΔH = -349 kJ/mol) and the crystal lattice energy (ΔH_latt = -787 kJ/mol) are strongly exothermic (ΔH < 0).

mdcat-b10-chem-18.qHtml: For a chemical reaction occurring at constant temperature and pressure, which condition guarantees that the reaction is thermodynamically spontaneous in the forward direction?
optionsHtml: The change in Gibbs free energy is negative (ΔG < 0)
The standard enthalpy change is positive (ΔH > 0)
The entropy change of the system is zero (ΔS = 0)
The activation energy (Ea) is exactly zero
mdcat-b10-chem-18.explainHtml: According to the second law of thermodynamics, at constant temperature and pressure, the criterion for spontaneity is ΔG = ΔH - TΔS < 0. When ΔG is negative, the reaction is exergonic and spontaneous.

mdcat-b10-chem-19.qHtml: When 100 mL of 1.0 M HCl is completely neutralized by 100 mL of 1.0 M NaOH in a constant-pressure coffee-cup calorimeter, the measured standard enthalpy of neutralization (ΔH_neut°) is approximately:
optionsHtml: -57.3 kJ per mole of H2O formed
-285.8 kJ per mole of H2O formed
+57.3 kJ per mole of H2O formed
-114.6 kJ per mole of H2O formed
mdcat-b10-chem-19.explainHtml: The neutralization of any strong acid by a strong base represents the reaction: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H2O(l). Because strong acids and bases are fully dissociated, the enthalpy of neutralization is a constant value of approximately -57.3 kJ/mol (-13.7 kcal/mol) of water formed.

mdcat-b10-chem-20.qHtml: If the bond dissociation energy of H-H is 436 kJ/mol, Cl-Cl is 242 kJ/mol, and H-Cl is 431 kJ/mol, what is the enthalpy change (ΔH) for the gas-phase synthesis reaction: H2(g) + Cl2(g) → 2HCl(g)?
mdcat-b10-chem-20.explainHtml: ΔH = Σ(Bond energy of bonds broken) - Σ(Bond energy of bonds formed) = [BE(H-H) + BE(Cl-Cl)] - [2 × BE(H-Cl)] = [436 + 242] - [2 × 431] = 678 - 862 = -184 kJ.

mdcat-b10-chem-21.qHtml: For the exothermic synthesis of ammonia in the Haber-Bosch process: N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) (ΔH = -92 kJ/mol), which change in conditions will shift the equilibrium position toward higher yield of NH3 according to Le Chatelier's principle?
optionsHtml: Increasing total system pressure and lowering temperature
Decreasing total system pressure and raising temperature
Adding an iron catalyst at constant volume
Continuously removing N2 gas from the reactor
mdcat-b10-chem-21.explainHtml: The forward reaction involves a decrease in gas moles (4 moles of reactants → 2 moles of product) and is exothermic (ΔH < 0). By Le Chatelier's principle, increasing pressure favors the side with fewer gas moles (NH3), and decreasing temperature shifts equilibrium in the exothermic forward direction.

mdcat-b10-chem-22.qHtml: How are the equilibrium constants Kp and Kc mathematically related for the reversible thermal dissociation of dinitrogen tetroxide: N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g)?
mdcat-b10-chem-22.explainHtml: The general relation is Kp = Kc (RT)^Δn, where Δn = (moles of gaseous products) - (moles of gaseous reactants). For N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g), Δn = 2 - 1 = 1. Hence, Kp = Kc (RT)^{1}.

mdcat-b10-chem-23.qHtml: If the solubility product constant (Ksp) of silver chromate (Ag2CrO4) at 25°C is 1.1 × 10^{-1}², what is its molar solubility (S) in pure water?
optionsHtml: S = ³{Ksp / 4} ≈ 6.5 × 10⁻⁵ mol/L
S = {Ksp} ≈ 1.05 × 10⁻⁶ mol/L
S = ⁴{Ksp / 27} ≈ 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ mol/L
mdcat-b10-chem-23.explainHtml: Dissociation: Ag2CrO4(s) ⇌ 2Ag⁺(aq) + CrO42⁻(aq). If solubility is S mol/L, then [Ag⁺] = 2S and [CrO42⁻] = S. Ksp = [Ag⁺]² [CrO42⁻] = (2S)^{2} (S) = 4S3. Therefore, S = ³{Ksp / 4} = ³√((1.1 × 10^{-1}²) / 4) ≈ 6.5 × 10⁻⁵ mol/L.

mdcat-b10-chem-24.qHtml: What happens to the numerical value of the chemical equilibrium constant Kc of an endothermic reaction when the reaction temperature is increased?
optionsHtml: Kc increases because heat acts as an effective reactant, driving product formation
Kc decreases because products decompose faster
Kc remains strictly unchanged because only a catalyst alters Kc
Kc drops to zero as activation energy is exceeded
mdcat-b10-chem-24.explainHtml: By the van 't Hoff equation (d ln Kc / dT = ΔH° / RT2), for an endothermic reaction (ΔH° > 0), raising temperature increases the value of Kc. Temperature is the only thermodynamic variable that changes the numerical value of Kc.

mdcat-b10-chem-25.qHtml: In the standard Daniell voltaic cell: Zn(s) | Zn2⁺(1 M) || Cu2⁺(1 M) | Cu(s), if E°(Zn2⁺/Zn) = -0.76 V and E°(Cu2⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V, what is the standard cell potential (E°_cell)?
mdcat-b10-chem-25.explainHtml: E°_cell = E°_cathode (reduction) - E°_anode (oxidation) = E°(Cu2⁺/Cu) - E°(Zn2⁺/Zn) = (+0.34 V) - (-0.76 V) = +0.34 V + 0.76 V = +1.10 V.

mdcat-b10-chem-26.qHtml: According to Faraday's first law of electrolysis, how much electrical charge (in Coulombs) is required to deposit exactly 1.0 mole of copper metal from an aqueous solution of copper(II) sulfate (CuSO4)? (1 Faraday F ≈ 96,500 C)
mdcat-b10-chem-26.explainHtml: The reduction cathode half-reaction is: Cu2⁺(aq) + 2 e⁻ → Cu(s). To reduce 1 mole of Cu2⁺ ions requires 2 moles of electrons. Total electrical charge Q = n × F = 2 mol × 96,500 C/mol = 193,000 Coulombs (2 F).

mdcat-b10-chem-27.qHtml: In the commercial lead-acid storage battery, what chemical transformations occur at the positive and negative plates during electrical discharge?
optionsHtml: Both the spongy lead anode (Pb) and lead dioxide cathode (PbO2) are converted into lead(II) sulfate (PbSO4), consuming sulfuric acid
Pb is oxidized to PbO at the anode while PbO2 is reduced to metallic Pb at the cathode
Lead sulfate is converted into lead metal and sulfuric acid is generated
Water is electrolyzed into hydrogen and oxygen gases at both electrodes
mdcat-b10-chem-27.explainHtml: During discharge: Anode: Pb(s) + HSO4⁻ → PbSO4(s) + H⁺ + 2e⁻. Cathode: PbO2(s) + HSO4⁻ + 3H⁺ + 2e⁻ → PbSO4(s) + 2H2O. Both plates convert to insoluble PbSO4(s), while H2SO4 is consumed, lowering the electrolyte density.

mdcat-b10-chem-28.qHtml: In the standard hydrogen electrode (SHE), assigned an arbitrary standard reduction potential of 0.00 V at all temperatures, the platinum electrode is coated with platinum black to:
optionsHtml: Provide a catalytic high-surface-area interface for the equilibrium: 2H⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ ⇌ H2(g)
Prevent acidic protons from reacting with water molecules
Generate an irreversible electrical resistance across the half-cell
Act as a sacrificial anode that oxidizes before hydrogen
mdcat-b10-chem-28.explainHtml: Platinum is chemically inert and does not take part in the redox reaction. Coating it with finely divided platinum black increases its effective surface area and catalytically adsorbs H2 gas at 1 atm in contact with 1.0 M H⁺(aq) to establish rapid reversible thermodynamic equilibrium: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ ⇌ H2.

mdcat-b10-chem-29.qHtml: For a first-order chemical reaction with rate constant k = 0.0693 min^{-1}, what is the half-life (t_1/2) of the reaction?
mdcat-b10-chem-29.explainHtml: For a first-order reaction, half-life is independent of initial substrate concentration: t_1/2 = ln(2) / k = 0.693 / k. Substituting k = 0.0693 min^{-1}: t_1/2 = 0.693 / 0.0693 = 10 minutes.

mdcat-b10-chem-30.qHtml: Experimental kinetic measurements for the reaction A + 2B → C show that doubling [A] while keeping [B] constant quadruples the rate, while doubling [B] while keeping [A] constant doubles the rate. What is the differential rate law and overall order?
mdcat-b10-chem-30.explainHtml: Rate ∝ [A]^m [B]^n. Doubling [A] quadruples the rate (2m = 4 → m = 2, second order in A). Doubling [B] doubles the rate (2n = 2 → n = 1, first order in B). Rate = k [A]² [B]¹. Overall reaction order = 2 + 1 = 3 (third order).

mdcat-b10-chem-31.qHtml: According to the Arrhenius equation: k = A e^{-Ea / RT}, a plot of ln(k) versus 1/T yields a stra line with what slope?
mdcat-b10-chem-31.explainHtml: Taking natural logarithms: ln(k) = ln(A) - (Ea / R)(1/T). This matches the linear form y = mx + c where y = ln(k), x = 1/T, intercept c = ln(A), and slope m = -Ea / R. (If plotted with log10, slope is -Ea / (2.303 R)).

mdcat-b10-chem-32.qHtml: How does the addition of a positive catalyst accelerate a chemical reaction without being consumed?
optionsHtml: It provides an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy (Ea)
It increases the average kinetic energy of the reacting molecules
It makes the overall enthalpy change (ΔH) significantly more negative
It increases the collision frequency between reactant molecules by a factor of 10⁶
mdcat-b10-chem-32.explainHtml: A catalyst offers an alternate mechanistic pathway involving a different transition state with lower activation energy (Ea). Consequently, a much larger fraction of colliding molecules possesses kinetic energy greater than or equal to Ea, dramatically increasing reaction rate without changing ΔH or equilibrium position.

mdcat-b10-chem-33.qHtml: According to Raoult's law for an ideal binary liquid solution of two volatile components A and B, the total vapor pressure (P_total) above the solution is given by:
mdcat-b10-chem-33.explainHtml: Raoult's law states that the partial vapor pressure of each volatile component in an ideal solution is equal to the vapor pressure of the pure component multiplied by its mole fraction in liquid: P_A = P°_A X_A and P_B = P°_B X_B. By Dalton's law of partial pressures: P_total = P_A + P_B = P°_A X_A + P°_B X_B.

mdcat-b10-chem-34.qHtml: What is the van 't Hoff factor (i) for an ideal, completely dissociated aqueous solution of calcium chloride (CaCl2)?
mdcat-b10-chem-34.explainHtml: CaCl2 dissociates completely in water: CaCl2(s) → Ca2⁺(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq). One mole of calcium chloride produces 1 mole of Ca2⁺ and 2 moles of Cl⁻, yielding a total of 3 moles of solute particles per mole of formula units. Thus, the theoretical van 't Hoff factor i = 3.

mdcat-b10-chem-35.qHtml: A 0.10 molal aqueous solution of which of the following non-volatile solutes will exhibit the lowest freezing point?
mdcat-b10-chem-35.explainHtml: Freezing point depression ΔTf = i × Kf × m. For equal molality (0.10 m): Glucose has i = 1 (ΔTf ∝ 0.10); NaCl has i = 2 (ΔTf ∝ 0.20); CaCl2 has i = 3 (ΔTf ∝ 0.30); AlCl3 dissociates into 1 Al3⁺ + 3 Cl⁻ giving i = 4 (ΔTf ∝ 0.40). Highest ΔTf produces the lowest actual freezing point.

mdcat-b10-chem-36.qHtml: The osmotic pressure (π) of a dilute solution containing n moles of non-volatile solute in volume V at temperature T is mathematically described by the van 't Hoff equation as:
optionsHtml: π = C R T (where C = n / V)
π = (n2 R T) / V^{2}
mdcat-b10-chem-36.explainHtml: Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff demonstrated that dilute solutions obey an equation analogous to the ideal gas law: π V = n R T, or π = (n / V) R T = C R T, where C is the molarity (mol/L), R is the gas constant (0.0821 L·atm/mol·K), and T is absolute temperature in Kelvin.

mdcat-b10-chem-37.qHtml: According to the Bronsted-Lowry acid-base theory, what are the conjugate acid-base pairs in the forward aqueous equilibrium: NH3 + H2O ⇌ NH4⁺ + OH⁻?
optionsHtml: H2O is an acid and OH⁻ is its conjugate base; NH3 is a base and NH4⁺ is its conjugate acid
NH3 is an acid and OH⁻ is its conjugate base; H2O is a base and NH4⁺ is its conjugate acid
NH4⁺ and OH⁻ are conjugate acid-base pairs
NH3 and H2O are conjugate acid-base pairs
mdcat-b10-chem-37.explainHtml: An acid donates H⁺ and a base accepts H⁺. H2O donates a proton to form OH⁻ (Pair 1: H2O acid / OH⁻ conjugate base). NH3 accepts a proton to form NH4⁺ (Pair 2: NH3 base / NH4⁺ conjugate acid).

mdcat-b10-chem-38.qHtml: What is the pH of a 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ M aqueous solution of hydrochloric acid (HCl) at 25°C?
mdcat-b10-chem-38.explainHtml: In ultra-dilute acid (10⁻⁸ M HCl), autoionization of water cannot be neglected. Total [H⁺] = [H⁺]_HCl + [H⁺]_H2O = 10⁻⁸ + x. From Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻] = (10⁻⁸ + x)(x) = 1.0 × 10^{-1}⁴. Solving gives x ≈ 9.5 × 10⁻⁸ M, so total [H⁺] ≈ 1.05 × 10⁻⁷ M, yielding pH = -log(1.05 × 10⁻⁷) ≈ 6.98. Acidic solutions can never have pH > 7 at 25°C.

mdcat-b10-chem-39.qHtml: According to the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, what is the pH of an acidic buffer solution containing 0.1 M acetic acid (CH3COOH) and 0.1 M sodium acetate (CH3COONa), given that pKa of acetic acid is 4.74?
mdcat-b10-chem-39.explainHtml: Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = pKa + log([Conjugate Base] / [Acid]). When [Salt] = [Acid] (0.1 M / 0.1 M = 1), log(1) = 0. Therefore, pH = pKa + 0 = 4.74. An equimolar buffer operates at maximum buffer capacity with pH = pKa.

mdcat-b10-chem-40.qHtml: Which of the following salts undergoes cationic hydrolysis in aqueous solution, resulting in an acidic solution with a pH less than 7 at 25°C?
mdcat-b10-chem-40.explainHtml: NH4Cl is the salt of a weak base (NH3) and a strong acid (HCl). The ammonium cation hydrolyzes in water: NH4⁺(aq) + H2O(l) ⇌ NH3(aq) + H3O⁺(aq). The accumulation of hydronium ions yields an acidic solution (pH < 7). Cl⁻ does not hydrolyze.

mdcat-b10-chem-41.qHtml: Why does beryllium (Be) exhibit anomalous chemical properties compared to the other Group 2 alkaline earth metals, including forming predominantly covalent rather than ionic compounds?
optionsHtml: Extremely small ionic radius and high charge density leading to strong polarizing power (Fajans' rules)
Presence of vacant d-orbitals in its valence shell
Very low first and second ionization energies
Ability to form stable trivalent cations (Be3⁺)
mdcat-b10-chem-41.explainHtml: Beryllium has an exceptionally small atomic and ionic radius (Be2⁺ ionic radius ~31 pm). This generates an enormous charge density and polarizing power. According to Fajans' rules, high polarizing power severely distorts anion electron clouds, conferring high covalent character to beryllium halides (e.g., BeCl2 is covalent and polymeric).

mdcat-b10-chem-42.qHtml: In the contact process for industrial manufacture of sulfuric acid (H2SO4), what solid heterogeneous catalyst is employed to oxidize SO2 to SO3 at 450°C?
mdcat-b10-chem-42.explainHtml: In the Contact Process, sulfur dioxide is converted to sulfur trioxide: 2SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g) (ΔH = -196 kJ/mol). Vanadium pentoxide (V2O5) supported on silica is used as the commercial catalyst at ~450°C and 1-2 atm.

mdcat-b10-chem-43.qHtml: What is the molecular geometry and hybridization of the central sulfur atom in sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) according to VSEPR theory?
optionsHtml: Octahedral geometry with sp3d2 hybridization
Trigonal bipyramidal geometry with sp3d hybridization
Square planar geometry with dsp2 hybridization
Tetrahedral geometry with sp3 hybridization
mdcat-b10-chem-43.explainHtml: In SF6, the central sulfur atom has 6 valence electrons and forms 6 single covalent bonds with fluorine atoms with 0 lone pairs (Steric Number = 6). VSEPR predicts sp3d2 hybridization with regular octahedral geometry and 90∘ F-S-F bond angles.

mdcat-b10-chem-44.qHtml: Why are aqueous solutions of scandium(III) salts [Sc3⁺(aq)] and zinc(II) salts [Zn2⁺(aq)] completely colorless?
optionsHtml: Sc3⁺ has an empty d-subshell (3d0) and Zn2⁺ has a completely filled d-subshell (3d10), so neither can undergo d-d electronic transitions in the visible spectrum
Both cations form giant ionic polymers that scatter all visible l
Their d-orbitals are degenerate and cannot be split by water ligands
They absorb only monochromatic gamma radiation
mdcat-b10-chem-44.explainHtml: The characteristic colors of transition metal complexes arise from d-d transitions when degenerate d-orbitals split in a crystal field. Sc3⁺ has a 3d0 configuration (no d-electrons to promote), and Zn2⁺ has a 3d10 configuration (all d-orbitals completely filled; no vacant d-level). Hence, both are colorless.

mdcat-b10-chem-45.qHtml: What is the coordination number and oxidation state of the central iron atom in the coordination complex potassium hexacyanoferrate(II): K4[Fe(CN)6]?
mdcat-b10-chem-45.explainHtml: In K4[Fe(CN)6], the complex anion is [Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻. Six monodentate cyanide ligands (CN⁻) are directly bonded to iron, so Coordination Number = 6. Let x be the oxidation state of Fe: x + 6(-1) = -4 → x - 6 = -4 → x = +2.

mdcat-b10-chem-46.qHtml: According to Crystal Field Theory (CFT), an octahedral coordination complex of Cr3⁺ (electronic configuration 3d3) in an aqueous medium has what ground-state d-electron configuration?
mdcat-b10-chem-46.explainHtml: In an octahedral crystal field, the 5 degenerate d-orbitals split into a lower-energy triply degenerate set (t2g: dxy, dyz, dxz) and a higher-energy doubly degenerate set (eg: dx2−y2, dz2). For a 3d3 ion like Cr3⁺, Hund's rule places one electron in each of the three t2g orbitals with parallel spins, giving t2g3eg0.

mdcat-b10-chem-47.qHtml: In the molecule ethyne (acetylene, H-C≡C-H), what is the hybridization of the carbon atoms and the composition of the carbon-carbon triple bond?
optionsHtml: sp hybridization; the triple bond consists of one σ (sp-sp) bond and two mutually perpendicular π (2py-2py and 2pz-2pz) bonds
sp2 hybridization; one σ bond and two π bonds
sp3 hybridization; three σ bonds
sp hybridization; three π bonds without a σ bond
mdcat-b10-chem-47.explainHtml: Each carbon in ethyne forms two linear σ bonds (one with H via sp-1s, one with C via sp-sp) with 180∘ bond angles (sp hybridization). The two unhybridized p-orbitals (2py and 2pz) on each carbon overlap sideways to form two mutually perpendicular π-bonds (cylindrical π electron cloud).

mdcat-b10-chem-48.qHtml: Which of the following pairs of organic molecules illustrates tautomerism (a dynamic functional isomerism involving proton relocation)?
optionsHtml: Diethyl ether and Methyl propyl ether
mdcat-b10-chem-48.explainHtml: Tautomerism is a special form of functional group isomerism where two constitutional isomers interconvert rapidly through the migration of a mobile proton accompanied by a shift in a double bond. Acetaldehyde (keto form) and vinyl alcohol / ethenol (enol form) represent classic keto-enol tautomers.

mdcat-b10-chem-49.qHtml: Which of the following organic structures contains a chiral (asymmetric) carbon center and can therefore exist as a pair of non-superimposable optical enantiomers?
mdcat-b10-chem-49.explainHtml: A chiral carbon is bonded to four distinctly different atoms or groups. In 2-chlorobutane, C2 is bonded to: (1) -H, (2) -Cl, (3) -CH3, and (4) -CH2CH3 (ethyl). Having four distinct substituents, C2 is a stereocenter capable of rotating plane-polarized l.

mdcat-b10-chem-50.qHtml: According to Markovnikov's rule, what is the major organic product obtained when propene (CH3-CH=CH2) reacts with gaseous hydrogen bromide (HBr) in the absence of peroxides?
mdcat-b10-chem-50.explainHtml: Electrophilic addition proceeds through the more stable carbocation intermediate. Protonation of propene at C1 yields a secondary carbocation (CH3-C⁺H-CH3), which is more stable than the primary carbocation (CH3-CH2-C⁺H2) due to hyperconjugation. Attack by Br⁻ on the secondary carbocation gives 2-bromopropane as the major product.

mdcat-b10-chem-51.qHtml: Why does benzene (C6H6) undergo electrophilic aromatic substitution rather than electrophilic addition reactions typical of aliphatic alkenes?
optionsHtml: Substitution preserves the cyclic delocalized 6 π-electron sextet conferring thermodynamic aromatic resonance stabilization (150 kJ/mol)
Benzene lacks double bonds entirely and is an alkane
Aromatic C-H bonds are ionic and easily dissociated
The ring is sterically blocked from nucleophilic attack
mdcat-b10-chem-51.explainHtml: Benzene possesses extraordinary thermodynamic stability (resonance energy of ~150 kJ/mol or 36 kcal/mol) due to complete cyclic conjugation of 6 π-electrons (Hückel's 4n+2 rule). Addition reactions would permanently destroy this aromatic stabilization, whereas electrophilic substitution regenerates the intact aromatic ring.

mdcat-b10-chem-52.qHtml: In the free-radical chlorination of methane in the presence of ultraviolet l, what chemical reaction represents a termination step?
optionsHtml: Two methyl radicals recombining to form ethane: •CH3 + •CH3 → CH3-CH3
A chlorine radical reacting with methane: Cl• + CH4 → •CH3 + HCl
A methyl radical reacting with Cl2: •CH3 + Cl2 → CH3Cl + Cl•
Photodissociation of chlorine: Cl2 + hν → 2 Cl•
mdcat-b10-chem-52.explainHtml: Initiation creates free radicals (Cl2 + hν → 2 Cl•). Propagation steps consume one radical and produce another. Termination occurs whenever any two free radicals collide and combine to form a stable covalent molecule without generating new radicals (e.g., •CH3 + •CH3 → C2H6).

mdcat-b10-chem-53.qHtml: Which mechanism correctly describes the nucleophilic substitution reaction of primary alkyl halides (e.g., 1-bromobutane) with aqueous sodium hydroxide?
optionsHtml: SN2 mechanism: a single-step concerted process involving backside nucleophilic attack, a pentacoordinate transition state, and complete inversion of stereochemical configuration (Walden inversion)
SN1 mechanism: a two-step process via a planar carbocation intermediate producing racemization
E1cB mechanism: involving an intermediate carbanion
Electrophilic aromatic substitution via a sigma complex
mdcat-b10-chem-53.explainHtml: Primary alkyl halides possess minimal steric hindrance around the electrophilic α-carbon. Nucleophiles attack from the opposite side of the leaving group in a single concerted bimolecular step (Rate = k [R-X] [Nu⁻]), passing through a trigonal bipyramidal transition state that produces 100% inversion of configuration (Walden inversion).

mdcat-b10-chem-54.qHtml: When preparing an alkylmagnesium halide (Grignard reagent, R-Mg-X), why must the reaction be conducted in anhydrous ether strictly free from all traces of moisture and water?
optionsHtml: Grignard reagents are extremely strong carbanion bases that react violently with water to produce alkanes: R-MgX + H2O → R-H + Mg(OH)X
Water oxidizes metallic magnesium into unreactive magnesium peroxide
Ether reacts with water to form explosive peroxides
Alkyl halides decompose into alkenes in the presence of water
mdcat-b10-chem-54.explainHtml: The carbon-magnesium bond in Grignard reagents is strongly polarized (R^δ- — Mg^δ+), giving the alkyl carbon pronounced nucleophilic and basic carbanion character. Grignard reagents react quantitatively and rapidly with active proton donors like water: R-MgX + H2O → R-H + Mg(OH)X, destroying the reagent.

mdcat-b10-chem-55.qHtml: According to Zaitsev's (Saytzeff's) rule for the base-induced dehydrohalogenation of secondary and tertiary alkyl halides, what is the major alkene formed?
optionsHtml: The most highly substituted, thermodynamically stable alkene having the greatest number of alkyl substituents attached to the double-bond carbons
The cis-alkene exclusively due to steric hindrance
A cyclic cycloalkane without a double bond
mdcat-b10-chem-55.explainHtml: Zaitsev's rule states that in β-elimination (E2/E1) reactions of alkyl halides with non-bulky bases, base removes a proton preferentially from the β-carbon with fewer hydrogen atoms, yielding the most substituted, hyperconjugated, thermodynamically stable alkene as the major product.

mdcat-b10-chem-56.qHtml: In the Lucas test for differentiating alcohols, anhydrous ZnCl2 in concentrated HCl is added to an unknown alcohol at room temperature. A cloudy precipitate forms immediately within seconds. What class of alcohol is present?
optionsHtml: Tertiary alcohol (3∘ alcohol)
Primary alcohol (1∘ alcohol)
Secondary alcohol (2∘ alcohol)
mdcat-b10-chem-56.explainHtml: The Lucas reagent converts alcohols to insoluble alkyl chlorides via an SN1 carbocation mechanism. Tertiary alcohols form very stable 3∘ carbocations and react immediately (cloudiness in seconds). Secondary alcohols react within 5-10 minutes, while primary alcohols do not react at room temperature without heating.

mdcat-b10-chem-57.qHtml: Why is phenol (C6H5OH, pKa ≈ 10) substantially more acidic than aliphatic alcohols like ethanol (C2H5OH, pKa ≈ 16)?
optionsHtml: The phenoxide conjugate base is stabilized by resonance delocalization of its negative charge into the aromatic π-electron ring
The hydroxyl oxygen in phenol is sp3 hybridized and cannot donate electrons
Aliphatic alcohols form stable carbocations upon losing a proton
Phenol contains a carboxylic acid functional group
mdcat-b10-chem-57.explainHtml: Loss of H⁺ from phenol yields the phenoxide ion (C6H5O⁻). The negative charge on oxygen is resonance-delocalized over the ortho- and para-positions of the aromatic benzene ring across four contributing resonance structures. In ethoxide (C2H5O⁻), the negative charge is localized on oxygen, and the ethyl group destabilizes it by electron-donating induction (+I).

mdcat-b10-chem-58.qHtml: When phenol is treated with excess aqueous bromine water at room temperature without a Lewis acid catalyst, what characteristic precipitate is formed?
optionsHtml: A brown liquid of o-bromophenol only
mdcat-b10-chem-58.explainHtml: The -OH group in phenol is strongly activating and ortho/para-directing due to +M resonance donation into the ring. In aqueous solution, ionization to phenoxide increases activation even further. Reaction with bromine water yields rapid polybromination, depositing a diagnostic white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

mdcat-b10-chem-59.qHtml: Controlled oxidation of a secondary alcohol (such as 2-propanol) with acidified potassium dichromate (K2Cr2O7 / H2SO4) yields which carbonyl compound as the final oxidation product?
mdcat-b10-chem-59.explainHtml: Primary alcohols oxidize first to aldehydes and subsequently to carboxylic acids. Secondary alcohols possess only one α-hydrogen and oxidize exclusively to ketones (e.g., 2-propanol oxidizes to acetone), which resist further oxidation under non-destructive conditions. Tertiary alcohols lack α-hydrogens and resist oxidation.

mdcat-b10-chem-60.qHtml: Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate, [Ag(NH3)2]⁺) is reduced to deposit an elemental silver mirror on the inner walls of a test tube by which class of organic compounds?
mdcat-b10-chem-60.explainHtml: Aldehydes possess an oxidizable hydrogen atom directly attached to the carbonyl carbon, allowing them to be readily oxidized to carboxylate ions by mild oxidizing agents like Tollens' reagent: R-CHO + 2[Ag(NH3)2]⁺ + 3OH⁻ → R-COO⁻ + 2Ag(s) + 4NH3 + 2H2O. Ketones lack this hydrogen and give a negative Tollens' test.

mdcat-b10-chem-61.qHtml: The iodoform test (reaction with I2 in aqueous NaOH) produces a diagnostic br yellow crystalline precipitate of triiodomethane (CHI3) when reacted with which structural motif?
optionsHtml: Methyl ketones (CH3-C=O) and secondary methyl carbinols (CH3-CH(OH)-R, including ethanol)
mdcat-b10-chem-61.explainHtml: The haloform reaction requires a methyl group adjacent to a carbonyl (CH3-CO-) or a group oxidizable to it (CH3-CH(OH)-). Halogenation in base converts the methyl to a trihalomethyl group (-CI3), which acts as a leaving group upon nucleophilic attack by OH⁻, precipitating yellow CHI3 (melting point 119°C).

mdcat-b10-chem-62.qHtml: Which of the following aldehydes lacks α-hydrogen atoms and therefore undergoes the Cannizzaro disproportionation reaction when heated with concentrated alkali (50% NaOH)?
mdcat-b10-chem-62.explainHtml: Aldehydes possessing α-hydrogens undergo aldol condensation in base. Aldehydes lacking α-hydrogens (such as HCHO and C6H5CHO) cannot form enolate ions; instead, they undergo Cannizzaro self-redox disproportionation, where one molecule is reduced to an alcohol and another is oxidized to a carboxylic acid salt.

mdcat-b10-chem-63.qHtml: In the nucleophilic addition of hydrogen cyanide (HCN) to acetaldehyde, what species acts as the attacking nucleophile in the rate-determining step?
mdcat-b10-chem-63.explainHtml: HCN is a weak acid and dissociates poorly on its own. A base catalyst generates cyanide ions (:CN⁻). The nucleophilic :CN⁻ attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon in the slow, rate-determining step, forming a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate that随后 picks up a proton from HCN to yield the cyanohydrin.

mdcat-b10-chem-64.qHtml: Why do carboxylic acids (e.g., acetic acid) have significantly higher boiling points than alcohols of comparable molecular we?
optionsHtml: Carboxylic acid molecules form stable cyclic intermolecular hydrogen-bonded dimers in both liquid and vapor phases
Carboxylic acids have higher covalent bond energies in their hydrocarbon tails
Carboxylic acids contain basic nitrogen atoms
The carboxyl group undergoes spontaneous free-radical polymerization
mdcat-b10-chem-64.explainHtml: Carboxylic acids contain both a hydrogen-bond donor (-OH) and an exceptional acceptor (C=O). Two acid molecules form a cyclic e-membered ring dimer held together by two strong complementary hydrogen bonds. This doubles their effective molecular mass and elevates boiling points above corresponding alcohols.

mdcat-b10-chem-65.qHtml: In Fischer esterification, a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst (concentrated H2SO4) to form an ester and water. Isotopic labeling with oxygen-18 (¹⁸O) in the alcohol demonstrates that:
optionsHtml: The ester oxygen originates from the alcohol, and water is formed from the carboxylic acid -OH group
The water oxygen originates exclusively from the alcohol
The carbonyl oxygen is expelled as water
The reaction is an electrophilic aromatic substitution
mdcat-b10-chem-65.explainHtml: Fischer esterification proceeds via nucleophilic acyl substitution on the protonated carboxylic acid. When methanol containing ¹⁸O (CH3-¹⁸OH) is used, the ¹⁸O label appears in the ester product (R-CO-¹⁸OCH3), proving that the C-O bond of the carboxylic acid is cleaved and the alcohol oxygen is retained in the ester.

mdcat-b10-chem-66.qHtml: Which of the following substituted acetic acids is the strongest acid due to the electron-withdrawing inductive effect (-I)?
mdcat-b10-chem-66.explainHtml: Electronegative chlorine atoms exert a strong electron-withdrawing inductive effect (-I), dispersing the negative charge on the carboxylate conjugate base (R-COO⁻) and stabilizing it. With three chlorines, CCl3COOH (pKa ≈ 0.65) is by far the strongest acid among the options.

mdcat-b10-chem-67.qHtml: Decarboxylation of the sodium salt of a monocarboxylic acid by heating with soda lime (a mixture of NaOH and CaO) produces:
optionsHtml: An alkane containing one fewer carbon atom than the parent carboxylic acid, and sodium carbonate (Na2CO3)
An alkene of identical carbon chain length
A symmetrical ketone and hydrogen gas
mdcat-b10-chem-67.explainHtml: Heating a sodium carboxylate with soda lime (NaOH + CaO) removes the carboxyl group as sodium carbonate: R-COONa + NaOH -(CaO, heat)→ R-H + Na2CO3. The resulting alkane contains one less carbon atom than the starting carboxylic acid salt.

mdcat-b10-chem-68.qHtml: At its characteristic isoelectric point (pI), an amino acid in aqueous solution exists predominantly in which ionic form?
optionsHtml: A dipolar zwitterion (+H3N-CH(R)-COO⁻) with a net electrical charge of zero
A fully protonated cation (+H3N-CH(R)-COOH) carrying a net +1 charge
A fully deprotonated anion (H2N-CH(R)-COO⁻) carrying a net -1 charge
An uncharged non-polar neutral covalent molecule (H2N-CH(R)-COOH)
mdcat-b10-chem-68.explainHtml: At physiological pH and at the isoelectric point (pI), the amino group is protonated (-NH3⁺) and the carboxylic acid group is dissociated (-COO⁻). This dipolar dipolar ion is called a zwitterion. Because positive and negative charges balance, the net charge is zero and it does not migrate in an electric field.

mdcat-b10-chem-69.qHtml: Which of the standard 20 amino acids is optically inactive (achiral) because its α-carbon is bonded to two identical hydrogen atoms?
mdcat-b10-chem-69.explainHtml: Glycine is the simplest amino acid, with -H as its side chain (R = H). Its α-carbon is bonded to two hydrogen atoms (NH2, COOH, H, H), meaning it lacks four distinct substituents. Consequently, glycine is symmetric, achiral, and optically inactive.

mdcat-b10-chem-70.qHtml: In the Biuret test for proteins, an alkaline solution containing dilute copper(II) sulfate (CuSO4) produces a characteristic violet-purple coordination complex in the presence of:
optionsHtml: Molecules containing two or more peptide linkages (-CO-NH-)
Isolated free amino acids lacking peptide bonds
mdcat-b10-chem-70.explainHtml: The Biuret test detects peptide bonds. In alkaline solution, Cu2⁺ ions coordinate with four nitrogen atoms from adjacent peptide linkages (-CONH-) across peptide backbones, forming a characteristic violet-purple chelate complex. Free amino acids (except histidine) give a negative Biuret test.

mdcat-b10-chem-71.qHtml: The α-helix and β-pleated sheet secondary structures of proteins are stabilized predominantly by:
optionsHtml: Hydrogen bonds between peptide backbone amide N-H groups and carbonyl C=O oxygen atoms
Covalent disulfide linkages between cysteine residues
Ionic salt bridges between Lys and Asp side chains
Hydrophobic interactions between non-polar side chains
mdcat-b10-chem-71.explainHtml: Secondary protein structures (Linus Pauling's α-helix and β-pleated sheet) are maintained by regular, repetitive hydrogen bonding between backbone C=O (acceptor) and N-H (donor) groups. In an α-helix, the hydrogen bond forms between the C=O of residue n and the N-H of residue n+4.

mdcat-b10-chem-72.qHtml: Nylon-6,6 is a commercially vital synthetic polyamide prepared by step-growth condensation polymerization between which two monomeric compounds?
mdcat-b10-chem-72.explainHtml: Nylon-6,6 is synthesized by condensing hexamethylenediamine, H2N-(CH2)6-NH2 (6 carbons), with adipic acid, HOOC-(CH2)4-COOH (6 carbons). Elimination of water molecules forms repeating amide linkages [-NH-(CH2)6-NH-CO-(CH2)4-CO-]n.

mdcat-b10-chem-73.qHtml: In the stratosphere, chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) deplete the protective ozone layer through a catalytic free-radical cycle initiated by ultraviolet photodissociation releasing:
mdcat-b10-chem-73.explainHtml: UV radiation (λ < 220 nm) cleaves C-Cl bonds in CFCs: CF2Cl2 + hν → •CF2Cl + Cl•. The chlorine radical catalytically destroys ozone in a self-sustaining cycle: Cl• + O3 → ClO• + O2, followed by ClO• + O• → Cl• + O2. A single chlorine radical can destroy over 100,000 ozone molecules.

mdcat-b10-chem-74.qHtml: Photochemical smog, typical of sunny urban basins with heavy vehicular emissions, is characterized by a brownish haze caused primarily by which atmospheric pollutant?
optionsHtml: Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and secondary photochemical oxidants such as tropospheric ozone and peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN)
Sulfur dioxide (SO2) from coal combustion in damp winter fog
Carbon monoxide (CO) reacting with nitrogen gas
mdcat-b10-chem-74.explainHtml: Photochemical (oxidizing / Los Angeles) smog forms when sunl acts on vehicular NOx and unburned volatile hydrocarbons. NO is oxidized to brown NO2 gas, which photolyzes to yield ozone (O3), aldehydes, and eye-irritating peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN). Classical smog is reducing (SO2 + soot).

mdcat-b10-chem-75.qHtml: What is the primary chemical mechanism by which acid rain (pH < 5.6, resulting from atmospheric SO2 and NOx emissions) leaches toxic heavy metals from soil and causes ecological damage in freshwater aquatic ecosystems?
optionsHtml: Protons (H⁺) displace bound toxic metal cations (such as Al3⁺ and Cd2⁺) from soil clay minerals into runoff water, where aluminum ions damage fish gills
Acid rain neutralizes all dissolved oxygen in water bodies
Sulfuric acid acts as a biological reducing agent that coagulates algae
Acid rain precipitates calcium carbonate onto lake beds
mdcat-b10-chem-75.explainHtml: Acid rain (containing H2SO4 and HNO3) introduces high concentrations of H⁺ ions into soil. Protons displace essential cations (Ca2⁺, Mg2⁺) causing nutrient depletion, and exchange with insoluble aluminum silicates to mobilize soluble, highly toxic Al3⁺ ions into streams and lakes, causing mucus accumulation and asphyxiation in fish gills.

mdcat-new-phy-1.qHtml: Which of the following is an SI supplementary unit?
mdcat-new-phy-1.explainHtml: Radian (plane angle) and Steradian (solid angle) are classified as supplementary SI units in the International System of Units. Candela is a base unit, while Coulomb and Weber are derived units.

mdcat-new-phy-2.qHtml: A student measures a length with a meter rod of least count 0.1 cm and records it as 20.0 cm. What is the percentage uncertainty in this measurement?
mdcat-new-phy-2.explainHtml: Percentage uncertainty = (Least Count / Measured Value) * 100% = (0.1 cm / 20.0 cm) * 100% = 0.5%.

mdcat-new-phy-3.qHtml: Which physical quantity has the dimensional formula [M L2 T⁻²]?
mdcat-new-phy-3.explainHtml: Torque τ = r * F has dimensions [L] * [M L T⁻²] = [M L2 T⁻²], identical to work and energy. Power is [M L2 T⁻³], Momentum is [M L T^{-1}], and Force is [M L T⁻²].

mdcat-new-phy-4.qHtml: The radius of a solid sphere is measured to be (2.0 ± 0.1) cm. What is the fractional uncertainty in its calculated volume?
mdcat-new-phy-4.explainHtml: Volume V = (4/3)π r3. Fractional uncertainty in V = 3 * (Δr / r) = 3 * (0.1 / 2.0) = 3 * 0.05 = 0.15 (or 15%).

mdcat-new-phy-5.qHtml: Which of the following physical quantities is a true scalar quantity?
mdcat-new-phy-5.explainHtml: Electric potential is the work done per unit charge and is a scalar quantity with only magnitude and sign, lacking spatial direction.

mdcat-new-phy-6.qHtml: If the scalar product and vector product of two vectors have equal magnitudes (|A · B| = |A × B|), what is the angle between them?
mdcat-new-phy-6.explainHtml: |A · B| = AB cos θ, and |A × B| = AB sin θ. Equating the two gives AB cos θ = AB sin θ => tan θ = 1 => θ = 45∘. (or 225∘).

mdcat-new-phy-7.qHtml: Two forces of 6 N and 8 N act on a body simultaneously at a r angle (90∘). What is the magnitude of the resultant force?
mdcat-new-phy-7.explainHtml: R = {F₁² + F₂² + 2F₁F₂ cos 90∘} = {62+82 + 0} = {36 + 64} = {100} = 10 N.

mdcat-new-phy-8.qHtml: For what value of parameter "k" are the two vectors A = 2î + 3ĵ - 4k̂ and B = 4î - 2ĵ + k k̂ mutually orthogonal?
mdcat-new-phy-8.explainHtml: Two vectors are orthogonal if their dot product A · B = 0. (2)(4) + (3)(-2) + (-4)(k) = 0 \implies 8 - 6 - 4k = 0 \implies 2 = 4k \implies k = 0.5.

mdcat-new-phy-9.qHtml: A body is dropped from rest from a he of 80 m above the ground. Taking g = 10 m/s2, how long does it take to reach the ground?
mdcat-new-phy-9.explainHtml: Using h = vi*t + (1/2)gt2 with vi = 0: 80 = (1/2)(10)t2 \implies 80 = 5t2⟹t2 = 16 \implies t = 4 s.

mdcat-new-phy-10.qHtml: The area under a velocity-time graph represents which physical quantity?
mdcat-new-phy-10.explainHtml: The integral of velocity with respect to time (area under the v-t graph) represents total displacement: s = ∫ v dt.

mdcat-new-phy-11.qHtml: At what launch angle θ is the maximum he attained by a projectile equal to one-fourth of its horizontal range (H = R/4)?
mdcat-new-phy-11.explainHtml: The general relation is R = 4H cot θ => H/R = (tan θ) / 4. Given H = R/4, we get 1/4 = (tan θ)/4 \implies tan θ = 1 => θ = 45∘.

mdcat-new-phy-12.qHtml: A ball of mass 0.2 kg moving horizontally at 20 m/s strikes a rigid vertical wall and rebounds elastically in the opposite direction with the same speed. If the contact duration is 0.02 seconds, the average force exerted on the wall is:
mdcat-new-phy-12.explainHtml: Change in momentum Δp = m(vf - vi) = 0.2 * (-20 - 20) = -8 kg·m/s. Magnitude of average force F = |Δp| / Δt = 8 / 0.02 = 400 N.

mdcat-new-phy-13.qHtml: How much work is done by the centripetal force on an object moving with constant speed in a circular path?
mdcat-new-phy-13.explainHtml: Centripetal force is always directed radially inwards toward the center, perpendicular to the instantaneous tangential displacement (θ = 90∘). Since W = F d cos 90∘ = 0, no work is done.

mdcat-new-phy-14.qHtml: If the linear momentum of a moving body is increased by 50%, by what percentage does its kinetic energy increase?
mdcat-new-phy-14.explainHtml: KE = p2 / (2m). If p becomes 1.5p, then KE_new = (1.5p)^{2} / (2m) = 2.25 * KE_initial. Fractional increase = (2.25 - 1) = 1.25 = 125%.

mdcat-new-phy-15.qHtml: An electric pump lifts 600 kg of water to a he of 20 meters in 1 minute. Assuming g = 10 m/s2, what is the output power of the pump?
mdcat-new-phy-15.explainHtml: Work = mgh = 600 kg * 10 m/s2 * 20 m = 120,000 J. Power = Work / time = 120,000 J / 60 s = 2,000 W (2 kW).

mdcat-new-phy-16.qHtml: A variable force F = (3x2 + 2x) N acts on a particle, displacing it from x = 0 to x = 2 meters. What is the total work done on the particle?
mdcat-new-phy-16.explainHtml: W = ∫₀² (3x2 + 2x) dx = [x3+x2]₀² = (23+22) - 0 = (8 + 4) = 12 J.

mdcat-new-phy-17.qHtml: What is the angular speed (ω) of the hour hand of a standard analog clock in rad/s?
mdcat-new-phy-17.explainHtml: The hour hand completes one full revolution (2π radians) in 12 hours. Time T = 12 * 3600 s = 43,200 s. ω = 2π / 43,200 = π / 21,600 rad/s.

mdcat-new-phy-18.qHtml: A vehicle of mass 1000 kg rounds a flat horizontal circular curve of radius 50 m. If the coefficient of static friction between tires and road is 0.5, what is the maximum safe speed without skidding? (Take g = 10 m/s2)
mdcat-new-phy-18.explainHtml: Maximum safe speed v_max = {μ s * g * r} = {0.5 * 10 * 50} = {250} ≈ 15.8 m/s.

mdcat-new-phy-19.qHtml: A stone of mass "m" tied to a string of length "r" is whirled in a vertical circle. What is the minimum tension in the string at the lowest point of the circle so that it safely completes the vertical loop without slacking?
mdcat-new-phy-19.explainHtml: At critical looping, speed at the bottom is v = {5gr}. The tension at the bottom is T = mg + mv2/r = mg + m(5gr)/r = mg + 5mg = 6mg.

mdcat-new-phy-20.qHtml: A solid cylinder (I = 1/2 MR2) and a thin hollow hoop (I = MR2) of equal mass and radius roll down an inclined plane from rest without slipping. The ratio of their linear accelerations (a_cylinder / a_hoop) is:
mdcat-new-phy-20.explainHtml: Acceleration for rolling without slipping is a = g sin θ / (1 + I / MR2). For solid cylinder: a_cyl = g sin θ / (1 + 0.5) = (2/3) g sin θ. For hoop: a_hoop = g sin θ / (1 + 1) = (1/2) g sin θ. Ratio = (2/3) / (1/2) = 4/3.

mdcat-new-phy-21.qHtml: According to the equation of continuity for an incompressible fluid in steady flow, which quantity remains constant throughout the streamline flow?
mdcat-new-phy-21.explainHtml: The equation of continuity states that A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ = constant, meaning the volumetric flow rate (m3/s) remains constant along the pipe.

mdcat-new-phy-22.qHtml: Bernoulli's theorem in fluid dynamics is a direct consequence of the law of conservation of:
mdcat-new-phy-22.explainHtml: Bernoulli's equation (P + 1/2 ρv2 + ρgh = constant) is derived directly from the principle of conservation of energy for ideal, non-viscous fluid flow.

mdcat-new-phy-23.qHtml: Water flows through a horizontal pipe. At a constriction where the pipe diameter is halved, the speed of the water:
mdcat-new-phy-23.explainHtml: Area A is proportional to diameter squared (A ∝ d2). Halving the diameter reduces cross-sectional area to (1/2)^{2} = 1/4. From A₁v₁ = A₂v₂, speed must increase by a factor of 4.

mdcat-new-phy-24.qHtml: A spherical raindrop of radius r reaches a terminal falling velocity vt in air. According to Stokes' law, how does terminal velocity scale with the droplet radius r?
mdcat-new-phy-24.explainHtml: Equating we mg = (4/3)πr3ρg to Stokes drag Fd = 6πηr vt gives vt = (2/9) r2 g (ρ - σ) / η. Thus, terminal velocity is directly proportional to r2.

mdcat-new-phy-25.qHtml: In simple harmonic motion (SHM), the restoring acceleration is always directly proportional to:
optionsHtml: Displacement from the mean position and directed towards it
mdcat-new-phy-25.explainHtml: The defining equation of SHM is a = -ω²x, stating that acceleration is directly proportional to displacement x and always directed towards the equilibrium position.

mdcat-new-phy-26.qHtml: A simple pendulum has a time period T on Earth. If its length is increased by a factor of 4, what is its new time period?
mdcat-new-phy-26.explainHtml: T = 2π {l/g}. If length becomes 4l, T_new = 2π {4l/g} = 2 * (2π {l/g}) = 2T.

mdcat-new-phy-27.qHtml: At what displacement from the mean position is the kinetic energy of an oscillator executing SHM equal to its potential energy (KE = PE)?
optionsHtml: x = x₀ / {2}
x = x₀ / {3}
mdcat-new-phy-27.explainHtml: Total energy E = 1/2 k x₀². When KE = PE, each equals E/2. So PE = 1/2 k x2 = 1/2 (1/2 k x₀²) \implies x2 = x₀²/2 \implies x = x₀ / {2}.

mdcat-new-phy-28.qHtml: A mass-spring system executes SHM with amplitude x₀. If the mass is doubled while the spring constant is halved, what happens to the natural frequency of oscillation?
mdcat-new-phy-28.explainHtml: Frequency f = (1 / 2π) {k / m}. If k becomes k/2 and m becomes 2m, then the term inside the square root becomes (k/2)/(2m) = k/(4m). Taking the square root gives 1/2, so f_new = f / 2.

mdcat-new-phy-29.qHtml: What is the fundamental difference between transverse waves and longitudinal waves?
optionsHtml: In transverse waves, particle oscillations are perpendicular to wave propagation, whereas in longitudinal waves they are parallel.
Transverse waves require a material medium while longitudinal waves do not.
Longitudinal waves cannot undergo reflection or refraction.
Transverse waves travel faster than longitudinal waves in all media.
mdcat-new-phy-29.explainHtml: In transverse waves (e.g. l, ripples), particles oscillate perpendicular to wave direction. In longitudinal waves (e.g. sound), oscillations occur parallel to wave direction.

mdcat-new-phy-30.qHtml: A sound source emits a wave of frequency 500 Hz that travels in air at 340 m/s. What is the wavelength of this sound wave?
mdcat-new-phy-30.explainHtml: Using the fundamental wave relation v = f λ => λ = v / f = 340 m/s / 500 Hz = 0.68 m.

mdcat-new-phy-31.qHtml: A pipe of length L is open at one end and closed at the other. What is the wavelength of its fundamental harmonic resonance?
mdcat-new-phy-31.explainHtml: In a closed organ pipe, a node forms at the closed end and an antinode at the open end. The fundamental mode spans a quarter of a wavelength: L = λ/4 => λ = 4L.

mdcat-new-phy-32.qHtml: A stationary observer hears a frequency of 1100 Hz from an approaching ambulance moving at 30 m/s. If the speed of sound is 330 m/s, what is the actual emitted frequency of the siren?
mdcat-new-phy-32.explainHtml: For a source moving toward a stationary observer: f' = f * [v / (v - vs)]. Rearranging: f = f' * [(v - vs) / v] = 1100 * [(330 - 30) / 330] = 1100 * (300 / 330) = 1100 * (10 / 11) = 1000 Hz.

mdcat-new-phy-33.qHtml: In an isothermal process involving an ideal gas, which of the following thermodynamic variables remains constant?
optionsHtml: Internal energy changes while temperature fluctuates
mdcat-new-phy-33.explainHtml: An isothermal process occurs at constant temperature (ΔT = 0). For an ideal gas whose internal energy depends solely on temperature, ΔU = 0 as well.

mdcat-new-phy-34.qHtml: The first law of thermodynamics (Q = ΔU + W) is a statement of the conservation of:
mdcat-new-phy-34.explainHtml: The first law of thermodynamics states that the total heat energy supplied to a system equals the increase in internal energy plus the work done by the system, exemplifying conservation of energy.

mdcat-new-phy-35.qHtml: During an adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas, work is done by the gas on the surroundings. What happens to the internal energy and temperature of the gas?
optionsHtml: Internal energy decreases and temperature falls
Internal energy increases and temperature rises
Internal energy and temperature remain constant
Temperature falls while internal energy remains constant
mdcat-new-phy-35.explainHtml: In an adiabatic process, Q = 0. By the first law, 0 = ΔU + W \implies W = -ΔU. When the gas expands (W > 0), ΔU must be negative, so internal energy decreases and temperature drops.

mdcat-new-phy-36.qHtml: A Carnot engine operates between a hot reservoir at 500 K and a cold sink at 300 K. What is its maximum theoretical thermal efficiency?

mdcat-new-phy-37.qHtml: What is the electric field intensity inside a hollow, uniformly charged conducting sphere?
optionsHtml: Uniform and equal to the surface value
mdcat-new-phy-37.explainHtml: According to Gauss's Law, the net enclosed charge inside any Gaussian surface placed inside a hollow charged conductor is zero (q_enc = 0), so the electric field E = 0 everywhere inside.

mdcat-new-phy-38.qHtml: Two point charges separated by distance "r" experience an electrostatic force F. If the distance between them is doubled (2r), the new force becomes:
mdcat-new-phy-38.explainHtml: Coulomb's Law states F = k q₁q₂ / r2. Since F is inversely proportional to r2, doubling distance reduces the force to F / (2)^{2} = F / 4.

mdcat-new-phy-39.qHtml: A parallel plate capacitor has capacitance C in vacuum. If a dielectric slab with dielectric constant εr = 4 is inserted between the plates, the new capacitance is:
mdcat-new-phy-39.explainHtml: Capacitance with a dielectric is C_med = εr * C_vac. With εr = 4, the capacitance increases fourfold to 4C.

mdcat-new-phy-40.qHtml: A 10 μF capacitor is charged to a potential difference of 100 V. What is the total electrostatic energy stored in its electric field?
mdcat-new-phy-40.explainHtml: Energy U = 1/2 C V2 = 1/2 * (10 × 10⁻⁶ F) * (100 V)^{2} = 5 × 10⁻⁶ * 10,000 = 0.05 Joules.

mdcat-new-phy-41.qHtml: Three resistors of resistances 2 Ω, 3 Ω, and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?

mdcat-new-phy-42.qHtml: A copper wire of resistance R is stretched uniformly so that its length doubles while volume remains constant. What is its new electrical resistance?
mdcat-new-phy-42.explainHtml: When stretched uniformly to twice its length (L' = 2L), volume conservation (V = A*L) dictates that cross-sectional area halves (A' = A/2). Resistance R' = ρ L' / A' = ρ (2L) / (A/2) = 4 (ρ L / A) = 4R.

mdcat-new-phy-43.qHtml: A battery of emf 12 V and internal resistance 2 Ω is connected across an external load of 4 Ω. What is the terminal potential difference across the battery?
mdcat-new-phy-43.explainHtml: Circuit current I = E / (R + r) = 12 / (4 + 2) = 2 A. Terminal voltage Vt = E - I*r = 12 - (2 * 2) = 12 - 4 = 8 V (or Vt = I*R = 2 * 4 = 8 V).

mdcat-new-phy-44.qHtml: Kirchhoff's First Rule (Junction Rule: Σ I = 0) and Second Rule (Loop Rule: Σ V = 0) are based respectively on the conservation of:
mdcat-new-phy-44.explainHtml: Kirchhoff's Junction rule reflects conservation of electric charge (current in = current out). The Loop rule reflects conservation of energy (sum of potential gains and drops around a closed loop is zero).

mdcat-new-phy-45.qHtml: What is the magnetic force experienced by a stationary electric charge (v = 0) placed in a strong uniform magnetic field B?
mdcat-new-phy-45.explainHtml: Lorentz magnetic force is F = q (v × B) = q v B sin θ. If velocity v = 0, F = 0 regardless of the field strength.

mdcat-new-phy-46.qHtml: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field perpendicularly. What is the path traced by the particle?
mdcat-new-phy-46.explainHtml: When velocity is perpendicular to B (θ = 90∘), the magnetic force acts as a centripetal force constantly perpendicular to the velocity, bending the particle into a uniform circle.

mdcat-new-phy-47.qHtml: Two long parallel wires carry currents in the same direction. What is the nature of the magnetic interaction between them?
mdcat-new-phy-47.explainHtml: By applying the r-hand rule to find magnetic field directions and the resulting magnetic force F = I (L × B), parallel currents in the same direction attract each other.

mdcat-new-phy-48.qHtml: An electron of mass m and charge e accelerates from rest through a potential difference V and enters a transverse magnetic field B. What is the radius of its circular orbit?
optionsHtml: r = {2 m V / e} / B
r = B {2 m V / e}
r = e B / {2 m V}
mdcat-new-phy-48.explainHtml: Kinetic energy 1/2 m v2 = e V \implies v = {2 e V / m}. Radius in magnetic field is r = m v / (e B) = [m / (e B)] * {2 e V / m} = {2 m V / e} / B.

mdcat-new-phy-49.qHtml: Lenz's Law of electromagnetic induction is a direct manifestation of which fundamental conservation law?
mdcat-new-phy-49.explainHtml: Lenz's law states that induced current opposes the change that causes it. Mechanical work done against this opposing magnetic force is converted into electrical energy, satisfying conservation of energy.

mdcat-new-phy-50.qHtml: A magnetic flux through a coil of 50 turns changes uniformly from 0.8 Wb to 0.2 Wb in 0.1 seconds. What is the magnitude of the induced EMF in the coil?

mdcat-new-phy-51.qHtml: The primary coil of an ideal step-down transformer has 1000 turns and is supplied with 220 V AC. If the secondary coil has 50 turns, what is the output voltage?
mdcat-new-phy-51.explainHtml: Transformer equation: Vs / Vp = Ns / Np \implies Vs = Vp * (Ns / Np) = 220 V * (50 / 1000) = 220 * 0.05 = 11 V.

mdcat-new-phy-52.qHtml: A p-type semiconductor is obtained by doping pure intrinsic silicon with which type of impurity atom?
mdcat-new-phy-52.explainHtml: Doping silicon with trivalent impurities (Group III elements like Boron, Aluminum) creates holes as majority charge carriers, forming a p-type semiconductor.

mdcat-new-phy-53.qHtml: What happens to the width of the depletion region in a semiconductor p-n junction diode when it is reverse-biased?
mdcat-new-phy-53.explainHtml: Under reverse bias, external electric fields pull majority charge carriers away from the junction, leaving behind more immobilized uncompensated ions and widening the depletion barrier.

mdcat-new-phy-54.qHtml: In an operational amplifier (op-amp) connected in an inverting amplifier configuration with input resistor R₁ = 10 kΩ and feedback resistor Rf = 100 kΩ, what is the closed-loop voltage gain (Av)?
mdcat-new-phy-54.explainHtml: For an ideal inverting amplifier, closed-loop gain Av = - (Rf / R₁) = - (100 kΩ / 10 kΩ) = -10.

mdcat-new-phy-55.qHtml: According to Max Planck's quantum theory, the energy of a single photon is directly proportional to its:
mdcat-new-phy-55.explainHtml: Planck's equation E = h f states that photon energy is directly proportional to the radiation frequency f.

mdcat-new-phy-56.qHtml: In the photoelectric effect, if the intensity of the incident l of frequency above the threshold frequency is doubled, which of the following quantities doubles?
mdcat-new-phy-56.explainHtml: L intensity corresponds to the number of photons arriving per second. Doubling intensity doubles emitted photoelectrons per second (current), but does not alter individual photon energy or maximum KE.

mdcat-new-phy-57.qHtml: What is the de Broglie wavelength associated with an electron (mass m = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg) moving with a speed of 1.0 × 10⁶ m/s? (Take Planck's constant h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s)

mdcat-new-phy-58.qHtml: Which type of nuclear radiation has the highest ionization power?
mdcat-new-phy-58.explainHtml: Alpha particles (Helium-4 nuclei with charge +2e and large mass) exert strong electrostatic forces on orbital electrons, having the highest specific ionization power (about 100 times greater than beta).

mdcat-new-phy-59.qHtml: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 8 days. Starting with a 64-gram sample, how much of the original isotope remains undecayed after 32 days?
mdcat-new-phy-59.explainHtml: Number of half-lives elapsed n = 32 / 8 = 4 half-lives. Remaining mass = 64 / 24 = 64 / 16 = 4 grams.

mdcat-new-phy-60.qHtml: When a nucleus undergoes β-minus (β⁻) radioactive decay, what happens to its proton number (Z) and nucleon number (A)?
optionsHtml: Z increases by 1, A remains unchanged
Z decreases by 1, A remains unchanged
Z decreases by 2, A decreases by 4
Both Z and A remain unchanged
mdcat-new-phy-60.explainHtml: In β⁻ decay, a neutron converts into a proton, an electron (β⁻), and an electron antineutrino: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄. Thus, atomic number Z increases by 1, while total mass number A remains constant.

mdcat-b2-phys-1.qHtml: A body is dropped from rest from the top of a tower. Neglecting air resistance and taking g = 9.8 m/s2, what distance does it travel in the first 3 seconds of free fall?
mdcat-b2-phys-1.explainHtml: Using equation S = vit + (1/2)gt2 with vi = 0: S = 0.5 × 9.8 × (3)^{2} = 4.9 × 9 = 44.1 m.

mdcat-b2-phys-2.qHtml: A projectile is launched with an initial velocity v₀ at an angle of 30∘ above the horizontal. At what other launch angle will the horizontal range R be identical, assuming equal initial speed?
mdcat-b2-phys-2.explainHtml: Horizontal range R = (v₀² sin 2θ) / g. Range is equal for complementary launch angles θ and (90∘ - θ). Since sin(2 × 30∘) = sin(60∘) and sin(2 × 60∘) = sin(120∘) = sin(60∘), range at 60∘ equals range at 30∘.

mdcat-b2-phys-3.qHtml: In an elastic one-dimensional collision between two bodies of equal mass, where body 1 moves with velocity v and body 2 is initially at rest, what are their velocities after the collision?
optionsHtml: Body 1 comes to rest (v₁' = 0) and body 2 moves with velocity v₂' = v
Both move together with velocity v/2
Body 1 rebounds with -v and body 2 remains at rest
Both move with equal velocity v/{2} in opposite directions
mdcat-b2-phys-3.explainHtml: When two bodies of identical mass undergo a head-on elastic collision, they completely exchange their velocities: v₁' = 0 and v₂' = v.

mdcat-b2-phys-4.qHtml: A spherical raindrop of radius r falls through air with dynamic viscosity η. According to Stokes' Law (F = 6πηrv), what is the terminal velocity vt directly proportional to?
optionsHtml: Square of the radius (vt ∝ r2)
Cube of the radius (vt ∝ r3)
mdcat-b2-phys-4.explainHtml: At terminal velocity, drag force balances submerged we: 6πηrvt = (4/3)πr3(ρ - σ)g. Solving for vt yields vt = [2r2g(ρ - σ)] / (9η), so vt ∝ r2.

mdcat-b2-phys-5.qHtml: How much work is done by the gravitational force on an artificial satellite of mass m orbiting Earth in a stable circular orbit of radius r for one complete revolution?
mdcat-b2-phys-5.explainHtml: Gravitational centripetal force is directed radially inward toward Earth's center, strictly perpendicular to the satellite's displacement vector at all points (θ = 90∘). Work W = F·d·cos(90∘) = 0 J.

mdcat-b2-phys-6.qHtml: One kilowatt-hour (1 kWh) of commercial electrical energy is equivalent to how many Joules?
optionsHtml: 3.6 × 103 J

mdcat-b2-phys-7.qHtml: If the linear momentum p of an object is doubled, by what factor does its kinetic energy (K = p2 / 2m) increase?
mdcat-b2-phys-7.explainHtml: Kinetic energy is given by K = p2 / (2m). If momentum is doubled (p' = 2p), then K' = (2p)^{2} / (2m) = 4 [p2 / (2m)] = 4K.

mdcat-b2-phys-8.qHtml: An electric water pump with an efficiency of 80% lifts 300 kg of water to a vertical he of 20 meters in 10 seconds (take g = 9.8 m/s2). What input electrical power is consumed by the pump motor?
mdcat-b2-phys-8.explainHtml: Output work = mgh = 300 × 9.8 × 20 = 58,800 J. Useful output power = 58,800 J / 10 s = 5,880 W. Input power = Output power / efficiency = 5,880 W / 0.80 = 7,350 W.

mdcat-b2-phys-9.qHtml: A spring with spring constant k is compressed by an initial distance x. What additional work must be performed to compress the spring further from x to 2x?
mdcat-b2-phys-9.explainHtml: Initial potential energy U₁ = (1/2)kx2. Final potential energy at 2x is U₂ = (1/2)k(2x)^{2} = (4/2)kx2=2kx2. Work required ΔU = U₂ - U₁ = 2kx2 - 0.5kx2 = 1.5kx2 = (3/2)kx2.

mdcat-b2-phys-10.qHtml: A particle moves in a circle of radius r with constant speed v. The direction of its centripetal acceleration is always:
optionsHtml: Directed radially inward toward the center of the circular path
Directed tangential to the path in the direction of motion
Directed radially outward away from the center
Perpendicular to the plane of rotation
mdcat-b2-phys-10.explainHtml: Centripetal acceleration arises from continuous change in the direction of linear velocity and points radially inward toward the instantaneous center of curvature.

mdcat-b2-phys-11.qHtml: What is the rotational kinetic energy of a solid cylinder of mass M and radius R (moment of inertia I = (1/2)MR2) rotating about its longitudinal axis with angular velocity ω?
optionsHtml: (1/4) M R2 ω²
(1/2) M R2 ω²
M R2 ω²
mdcat-b2-phys-11.explainHtml: Rotational kinetic energy K_rot = (1/2)Iω². Substituting I = (1/2)MR2 gives K_rot = (1/2)[(1/2)MR2]ω² = (1/4)MR2ω².

mdcat-b2-phys-12.qHtml: According to the Law of Conservation of Angular Momentum (L = Iω = constant), when a spinning figure skater pulls her outstretched arms inward, her:
optionsHtml: Moment of inertia decreases and angular velocity increases
Moment of inertia increases and angular velocity decreases
Both moment of inertia and angular velocity increase
mdcat-b2-phys-12.explainHtml: Bringing mass closer to the rotational axis reduces moment of inertia I = Σmr2. In the absence of external torque, L = Iω is conserved, so angular velocity ω must increase.

mdcat-b2-phys-13.qHtml: What is the orbital speed v of a geostationary satellite orbiting Earth at a distance r from the center of Earth of mass M (G = gravitational constant)?
optionsHtml: v = {GM / r}
v = {2GM / r}
v = {GM r}
mdcat-b2-phys-13.explainHtml: Centripetal force is provided by gravity: mv2/r = GMm/r2. Solving for v yields orbital velocity v = {GM / r}.

mdcat-b2-phys-14.qHtml: The time period T of a simple pendulum executing simple harmonic motion (SHM) of length L in a gravitational field g is given by:
optionsHtml: T = 2π {L / g}
T = 2π {g / L}
T = (1/2π) {L / g}
T = 2π {m / k}
mdcat-b2-phys-14.explainHtml: For small angular amplitudes, the restoring torque gives angular frequency ω = {g / L}. Hence the time period T = 2π / ω = 2π {L / g}, independent of bob mass.

mdcat-b2-phys-15.qHtml: In simple harmonic motion of a mass-spring system, at the mean (equilibrium) position:
optionsHtml: Velocity is maximum, acceleration is zero, and kinetic energy is maximum
Velocity is zero, acceleration is maximum, and potential energy is maximum
Both kinetic energy and potential energy are zero
Acceleration is maximum and velocity is maximum
mdcat-b2-phys-15.explainHtml: At x = 0 (mean position), displacement is zero so restoring force and acceleration a = -ω²x are zero. All energy is kinetic, and velocity v = ω{A2−x2} = ωA is maximum.

mdcat-b2-phys-16.qHtml: What is the total mechanical energy E of a simple harmonic oscillator of mass m, angular frequency ω, and amplitude A?
mdcat-b2-phys-16.explainHtml: Total energy is constant throughout SHM and equals maximum kinetic energy: E = (1/2)m v_max2 = (1/2)m(ωA)^{2} = (1/2)mω²A2.

mdcat-b2-phys-17.qHtml: Which wave property remains strictly unchanged when a monochromatic l wave passes from air into a denser medium like water or glass?
mdcat-b2-phys-17.explainHtml: Frequency is determined solely by the wave source (rate of oscillation). When entering a denser optical medium, speed v and wavelength λ decrease proportionally (v = fλ), leaving f constant.

mdcat-b2-phys-18.qHtml: Two sound waves with slightly different frequencies of 256 Hz and 260 Hz interfere. How many beats per second will be heard by an observer?
mdcat-b2-phys-18.explainHtml: The beat frequency f_beat equals the absolute difference between the frequencies of the two interfering waves: f_beat = |f₁ - f₂| = ∣260−256∣ = 4 Hz (4 beats/s).

mdcat-b2-phys-19.qHtml: In a stationary (standing) wave formed on a stretched string fixed at both ends, the distance between two consecutive nodes is equal to:
mdcat-b2-phys-19.explainHtml: In standing waves, adjacent nodes are separated by λ/2, and adjacent antinodes are also separated by λ/2. The distance between a node and an adjacent antinode is λ/4.

mdcat-b2-phys-20.qHtml: According to the Doppler effect, what happens to the apparent pitch (frequency) heard by a stationary observer when an ambulance sounding its siren approaches the observer at high speed?
optionsHtml: Apparent frequency increases because sound waves are compressed in front of the source
Apparent frequency decreases because wave speed increases
Pitch remains unchanged but loudness increases
Apparent frequency drops to zero as the ambulance passes
mdcat-b2-phys-20.explainHtml: As the sound source moves toward the observer, wave crests are emitted closer together in space, shortening the observed wavelength (λ' = λ - vs/f) and increasing apparent frequency f' = f [v / (v - vs)].

mdcat-b2-phys-21.qHtml: In an organ pipe of length L closed at one end, the fundamental resonant frequency (first harmonic) is f₁ = v / (4L). What is the frequency of the second resonant overtone (third harmonic) permitted in this closed pipe?
mdcat-b2-phys-21.explainHtml: An organ pipe closed at one end supports only odd harmonics (n = 1, 3, 5, ...). The first overtone corresponds to the third harmonic: f₃ = 3 f₁ = 3v / (4L).

mdcat-b2-phys-22.qHtml: In a thermodynamic adiabatic process, what quantity remains strictly zero throughout the expansion or compression?
optionsHtml: Heat transfer into or out of the system (Q = 0)
mdcat-b2-phys-22.explainHtml: An adiabatic process is thermally insulated from the surroundings so that no heat enters or leaves the system (Q = 0). By the First Law, ΔU = -W.

mdcat-b2-phys-23.qHtml: What is the maximum theoretical efficiency (Carnot efficiency) of a heat engine operating between a hot reservoir at 600 K and a cold sink at 300 K?
mdcat-b2-phys-23.explainHtml: Carnot efficiency η = 1 - (Tc / Th) = 1 - (300 K / 600 K) = 1 - 0.50 = 0.50 or 50%.

mdcat-b2-phys-24.qHtml: For an ideal gas, the molar heat capacity at constant pressure (Cp) and at constant volume (Cv) are related by Mayer's relation as:
mdcat-b2-phys-24.explainHtml: Mayer's relation states that Cp - Cv = R, reflecting the additional work PΔV = RΔT done by an expanding gas when heated at constant pressure compared to constant volume.

mdcat-b2-phys-25.qHtml: According to the Second Law of Thermodynamics (Clausius statement), natural spontaneous heat flow can never occur without external work from:
optionsHtml: A body at lower temperature to a body at higher temperature
A body at higher temperature to a body at lower temperature
An isolated system to an open system
A compressed gas to a vacuum
mdcat-b2-phys-25.explainHtml: Clausius formulation of the second law states that it is impossible to construct a cyclic machine whose sole result is the transfer of heat from a cooler body to a hotter body without external work input.

mdcat-b2-phys-26.qHtml: According to Coulomb's Law, if the distance between two point charges is tripled while their charges remain unchanged, the electrostatic force between them becomes:
mdcat-b2-phys-26.explainHtml: Coulomb's Law states F ∝ 1/r2. If distance r is tripled (r' = 3r), force F' = F / (3)^{2} = F / 9.

mdcat-b2-phys-27.qHtml: What is the electric field intensity E inside the hollow cavity of an isolated charged spherical conducting shell of radius R?
optionsHtml: q / (4πε₀R2)
mdcat-b2-phys-27.explainHtml: By Gauss's Law, a Gaussian surface drawn inside the cavity encloses zero net charge (q_enc = 0). Therefore, the electric field is strictly zero everywhere inside the conductor.

mdcat-b2-phys-28.qHtml: When a dielectric slab of dielectric constant εr is inserted between the plates of an isolated charged parallel-plate capacitor, how are its capacitance C and electric field E affected?
optionsHtml: Capacitance increases by factor εr and electric field decreases by factor εr
Capacitance decreases and electric field increases
Both capacitance and electric field remain unchanged
Capacitance increases and potential difference increases
mdcat-b2-phys-28.explainHtml: Bound surface polarization charges in the dielectric create an opposing internal electric field, reducing E = E₀/εr and potential difference V = V₀/εr. Since Q is constant, C = Q/V = εr·C₀ increases.

mdcat-b2-phys-29.qHtml: What is the electric potential V at a distance r from an isolated point charge q in a vacuum?
optionsHtml: V = q / (4πε₀r2)
V = q2 / (4πε₀r)
mdcat-b2-phys-29.explainHtml: Electric potential is the work done per unit positive charge bringing it from infinity to r: V = ∫ -E·dr = q / (4πε₀r).

mdcat-b2-phys-30.qHtml: How much electrostatic energy is stored in a 10 μF capacitor charged to a potential difference of 200 V?
mdcat-b2-phys-30.explainHtml: Stored electrostatic energy U = (1/2)CV2 = 0.5 × (10 × 10⁻⁶ F) × (200 V)^{2} = 5 × 10⁻⁶ × 40,000 = 0.20 J.

mdcat-b2-phys-31.qHtml: According to Ohm's Law, for an ohmic metallic conductor at constant temperature, the current I flowing through the conductor is:
optionsHtml: Directly proportional to the potential difference V across its ends
Inversely proportional to the potential difference V
Directly proportional to the square of the potential difference
mdcat-b2-phys-31.explainHtml: Ohm's Law states that current is directly proportional to voltage (V = IR) as long as physical conditions such as temperature remain unchanged.

mdcat-b2-phys-32.qHtml: Kirchhoff's First Rule (Current/Junction Rule, ΣI = 0) is a direct consequence of the conservation of:
mdcat-b2-phys-32.explainHtml: At any electrical circuit junction, charge cannot accumulate or disappear; the sum of currents entering must equal the sum of currents leaving (conservation of charge).

mdcat-b2-phys-33.qHtml: A uniform copper wire of resistance R is uniformly stretched so that its length doubles (L' = 2L) while keeping its total volume constant. What is the new electrical resistance R' of the stretched wire?
mdcat-b2-phys-33.explainHtml: Volume V = A·L is constant. When length doubles (L' = 2L), cross-sectional area halves (A' = A/2). Since R = ρL/A, new resistance R' = ρ(2L)/(A/2) = 4(ρL/A) = 4R.

mdcat-b2-phys-34.qHtml: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge consisting of four resistors P, Q, R, and S, what condition holds true when no current flows through the central galvanometer?
mdcat-b2-phys-34.explainHtml: When potentials at the bridge nodes are equal (null deflection in galvanometer), ratio of resistance branches satisfies P/Q = R/S.

mdcat-b2-phys-35.qHtml: A cell of electromotive force E = 12 V and internal resistance r = 1.0 Ω is connected across an external load resistor R. For maximum power transfer from the cell to the load, what must be the value of R, and what is the maximum power delivered?
mdcat-b2-phys-35.explainHtml: By the Maximum Power Transfer Theorem, load resistance must match internal resistance: R = r = 1.0 Ω. P_max = E2 / (4r) = 122 / (4 × 1) = 144 / 4 = 36 W.

mdcat-b2-phys-36.qHtml: What is the magnetic force F experienced by a charged particle q moving with velocity v parallel to a uniform magnetic field B (angle θ = 0∘)?
mdcat-b2-phys-36.explainHtml: Lorentz magnetic force is F = q(v × B) = q v B sin(θ). For motion parallel to magnetic field lines, θ = 0∘ and sin(0∘) = 0, so no magnetic deflection force acts on the charge.

mdcat-b2-phys-37.qHtml: According to Ampere's Circuital Law, the magnetic field B inside a tightly wound long solenoid of n turns per unit length carrying current I is given by:
mdcat-b2-phys-37.explainHtml: Evaluating line integral ∮ B·dl around an Amperian loop inside an ideal long solenoid yields uniform axial magnetic field B = μ₀ n I.
