mdcat-b10-lr-10.qHtml: In a medical research cohort, Dr. Farooq is older than Dr. Gohar, but younger than Dr. Haroon. Dr. Ilyas is younger than Dr. Gohar. Who is the youngest member of the research cohort?
mdcat-b10-lr-10.explainHtml: Ranking by age from oldest to youngest: Dr. Haroon > Dr. Farooq > Dr. Gohar. Since Dr. Ilyas is younger than Dr. Gohar, the complete descending order is: Dr. Haroon > Dr. Farooq > Dr. Gohar > Dr. Ilyas. Thus, Dr. Ilyas is the youngest.

mdcat-b10-lr-11.qHtml: Problem Statement: "A tertiary care hospital experiences recurrent nocturnal electrical grid failures, during which backup diesel generators take up to 90 seconds to deliver full load, endangering mechanical ventilators in the ICU." Proposed Courses of Action: I. Install dedicated uninterruptible power supply (UPS) battery backup units on critical life-support devices to bridge the 90-second transition window. II. Cease admitting critically ill patients to the ICU during n shifts. Which course(s) of action should be approved?
optionsHtml: Only Course of Action I should be approved
Only Course of Action II should be approved
Both Course I and Course II should be approved
Neither Course I nor Course II should be approved
mdcat-b10-lr-11.explainHtml: Course I is practical, feasible, and directly resolves the danger of power interruption during generator spin-up without degrading clinical care. Course II is extreme, unethical, and violates the fundamental duty of a tertiary care ICU.

mdcat-b10-lr-12.qHtml: Problem Statement: "A sudden seasonal outbreak of dengue hemorrhagic fever has severely overwhelmed the bed capacity of a municipal public hospital." Proposed Courses of Action: I. Establish temporary triage and hydration wards in adjacent civic centers staffed by redeployed clinical teams. II. Deploy municipal public health squads to conduct targeted indoor residual spraying and eliminate stagnant water breeding sites. Which course(s) of action is/are appropriate?
optionsHtml: Both Course I and Course II are appropriate
Neither Course I nor Course II is appropriate
mdcat-b10-lr-12.explainHtml: Course I immediately relieves hospital bed strain by expanding clinical capacity for supportive rehydration. Course II attacks the vector at the community level to interrupt transmission. Both actions are synergistic and appropriate.

mdcat-b10-lr-13.qHtml: Problem Statement: "Routine quality assurance testing detected that 15% of sterile surgical glove batches delivered to a teaching hospital had microscopic perforations." Proposed Courses of Action: I. Immediately quarantine the entire shipment and issue a hospital-wide recall of the affected batch numbers. II. Discard all stored surgical instruments in the operating suites. Which course(s) of action should be taken?
optionsHtml: Only Course of Action I should be taken
Only Course of Action II should be taken
Both Course I and Course II should be taken
Neither Course I nor Course II should be taken
mdcat-b10-lr-13.explainHtml: Course I directly and proportionally targets the defective batches of gloves to safeguard patient safety. Course II is an unnecessary, wasteful overreaction because instruments stored in sterile packaging are uncontaminated and can be autoclaved as standard protocol.

mdcat-b10-lr-14.qHtml: Events: Statement (A): Municipal authorities repaired leaking subterranean sewer lines and heavily chlorinated municipal water supply mains across the southern district. Statement (B): The incidence of waterborne cholera and acute bacterial dysentery dropped by 85% in the southern district over the subsequent two months. What is the logical relationship between (A) and (B)?
optionsHtml: Statement (A) is the cause and Statement (B) is its effect
Statement (B) is the cause and Statement (A) is its effect
Both statements are effects of an unrelated common cause
mdcat-b10-lr-14.explainHtml: Repairing sewage leaks and chlorinating water (A) eradicates enteric bacterial contamination from drinking water, which directly produces the dramatic decline in waterborne diseases (B). Thus, (A) is the cause and (B) is the effect.

mdcat-b10-lr-15.qHtml: Events: Statement (A): The provincial transport authority made motorcycle helmet usage strictly mandatory under heavy legal penalties. Statement (B): The metropolitan trauma center documented a 45% decline in fatal traumatic brain injuries among motorcyclists. What is the logical relationship between (A) and (B)?
optionsHtml: Statement (A) is the cause and Statement (B) is its effect
Statement (B) is the cause and Statement (A) is its effect
Statement (A) is an effect of Statement (B)
mdcat-b10-lr-15.explainHtml: Mandatory helmet enforcement (A) increases rider compliance and head protection, directly leading to the reduction in severe skull fractures and fatal traumatic brain injuries (B).

tcat-math-ns-1.qHtml: What is the multiplicative identity in the set of complex numbers C?
tcat-math-ns-1.explainHtml: The multiplicative identity in complex numbers is (1, 0) because for any z = (x, y), (x, y) × (1, 0) = (x·1 - y·0, x·0 + y·1) = (x, y).

tcat-math-ns-2.qHtml: Which set is NOT closed under addition?
tcat-math-ns-2.explainHtml: The sum of two odd integers is always an even integer (e.g., 3 + 5 = 8). Since 8 is not an odd integer, the set of odd integers is not closed under addition.

tcat-math-ns-3.qHtml: What is the modulus of the complex number z = (3 - 4i) / (1 + i)?
tcat-math-ns-3.explainHtml: ∣z∣=∣3−4i∣ / ∣1+i∣. |3 - 4i| ={32+(−4)2} = {25} = 5. |1 + i| ={12+12} = {2}. Therefore, ∣z∣ = 5 / {2}.

tcat-math-ns-4.qHtml: Evaluate i107 where i = {-1}.
tcat-math-ns-4.explainHtml: Since i4 = 1, we divide the exponent 107 by 4: 107 = 4(26) + 3. Thus i107 = (i4)^{26} · i3 = 1 · (-i) = -i.

tcat-math-ns-5.qHtml: What is the polar form of the complex number z = -1 - i{3}?
optionsHtml: 2(cos(4\pi/3) + isin(4\pi/3))
2(cos(2\pi/3) + isin(2\pi/3))
2(cos(5\pi/3) + isin(5\pi/3))
4(cos(4\pi/3) + isin(4\pi/3))
tcat-math-ns-5.explainHtml: Modulus r = {(−1)2 + (-{3})^2} = {1 + 3} = 2. Since both real and imaginary parts are negative, z lies in the third quadrant. Reference angle α = \arctan({3}/1) = π/3, so argument θ = π + π/3 = 4\pi/3. Thus z = 2(cos(4\pi/3) + isin(4\pi/3)).

tcat-math-sfg-1.qHtml: If a set S has 4 elements, how many non-empty proper subsets does S have?
tcat-math-sfg-1.explainHtml: Total subsets = 2n=24 = 16. Proper subsets exclude S itself (16 - 1 = 15). Non-empty proper subsets also exclude the empty set (15 - 1 = 14).

tcat-math-sfg-2.qHtml: A function f: A → B is said to be bijective if it is:
tcat-math-sfg-2.explainHtml: By definition, a bijective function (one-to-one correspondence) must satisfy both injectivity (every element in B has at most one pre-image) and surjectivity (every element in B has at least one pre-image).

tcat-math-sfg-3.qHtml: What is the identity element of the group (Q^+, *) under the binary operation a * b = (ab) / 3?
tcat-math-sfg-3.explainHtml: Let e be the identity element. Then a * e = a \implies (a · e) / 3 = a. Multiplying both sides by 3 and dividing by a (since a \ne 0) gives e = 3.

tcat-math-sfg-4.qHtml: What is the natural domain of the real-valued function f(x) = {9 - x2}?
tcat-math-sfg-4.explainHtml: For f(x) to be real, the radicand must be non-negative: 9 - x2 \ge 0 \implies x2 \le 9 => -3 \le x \le 3. Hence domain is [-3, 3].

tcat-math-sfg-5.qHtml: What is the inverse of the element 5 in the group (Q^+, *) where a * b = (a · b) / 2?
tcat-math-sfg-5.explainHtml: First find identity e: a * e = a \implies (a · e) / 2 = a \implies e = 2. Now let b be the inverse of 5: 5 * b = e \implies (5 · b) / 2 = 2 \implies 5b = 4 \implies b = 4/5.

tcat-math-mat-1.qHtml: A square matrix A is called skew-symmetric if:
optionsHtml: AT = -A
AT = A
A · AT = I
∣A∣ = 0
tcat-math-mat-1.explainHtml: A matrix A is symmetric if AT = A, and skew-symmetric if AT = -A. For skew-symmetric matrices, all diagonal entries must be zero.

tcat-math-mat-2.qHtml: If A is a matrix of order 3x2 and B is of order 2x4, what is the order of matrix AB?
tcat-math-mat-2.explainHtml: Matrix multiplication of (m x k) and (k x n) yields an (m x n) matrix. Here, (3x2) × (2x4) yields a 3x4 matrix.

tcat-math-mat-3.qHtml: If A is an invertible matrix of order 3 with ∣A∣ = 4, what is |2A|?
tcat-math-mat-3.explainHtml: For an n x n square matrix A and scalar k, |kA| = kn∣A∣. Here n = 3, so |2A| = 23 · ∣A∣ = 8 · 4 = 32.

tcat-math-mat-4.qHtml: For an n x n matrix A, what is the value of A · adj(A)?
optionsHtml: ∣A∣ · I_n
tcat-math-mat-4.explainHtml: By the fundamental theorem of adjugate matrices, A · adj(A) = adj(A) · A = ∣A∣ · I_n, where I_n is the identity matrix.

tcat-math-mat-5.qHtml: If A is a 3x3 matrix with ∣A∣ = 5, what is the value of |adj(adj(A))|?
tcat-math-mat-5.explainHtml: For an n x n matrix, |adj(adj(A))| = |A|^{(n−1)2}. For n = 3, (n−1)2=(2)2 = 4. Thus |adj(adj(A))| = 54 = 625.

tcat-math-mat-6.qHtml: For what value of k does the system of homogeneous equations x + ky + z = 0, 2x - y + 3z = 0, 3x + y + 4z = 0 have a non-trivial solution?
tcat-math-mat-6.explainHtml: A homogeneous linear system has non-trivial solutions if and only if its coefficient determinant is 0: |[1, k, 1], [2, -1, 3], [3, 1, 4]| = 1(-4 - 3) - k(8 - 9) + 1(2 - (-3)) = -7 + k + 5 = k - 2 = 0 \implies k = 2.

tcat-math-quad-1.qHtml: If ω is a complex cube root of unity, what is the value of 1 + ω+ω^2?
tcat-math-quad-1.explainHtml: The sum of all three cube roots of unity (1, ω, ω^2) is identically equal to zero (1 + ω+ω^2 = 0).

tcat-math-quad-2.qHtml: If the roots of ax2 + bx + c = 0 are real and equal, the discriminant b2 - 4ac must be:
tcat-math-quad-2.explainHtml: When discriminant b2 - 4ac = 0, the quadratic formula yields x = -b / (2a), giving two real and coincident (equal) roots.

tcat-math-quad-3.qHtml: If α and β are the roots of 2x2 - 4x + 1 = 0, what is the value of α^2 + β^2?
tcat-math-quad-3.explainHtml: Sum of roots α+β = -(-4)/2 = 2, and product αβ = 1/2. Therefore, α^2 + β^2 = (α+β)^2 - 2αβ=22 - 2(1/2) = 4 - 1 = 3.

tcat-math-quad-4.qHtml: What is the value of (1 - ω−ω^2)^5, where ω is a complex cube root of unity?
tcat-math-quad-4.explainHtml: Since 1 + ω+ω^2 = 0, -ω−ω^2 = 1. Thus 1 - ω−ω^2 = 1 + 1 = 2. Therefore, 25 = 32.

tcat-math-quad-5.qHtml: If the roots of the equation x2 - px + q = 0 differ by unity, which relationship is true?
optionsHtml: p2 = 4q + 1
p2 = 4q - 1
q2 = 4p + 1
p2 = 2q + 1
tcat-math-quad-5.explainHtml: Let roots be α and β. α+β = p, αβ = q, and |α−β| = 1. (α−β)^2 = (α+β)^2 - 4αβ⟹12=p2 - 4q \implies p2 = 4q + 1.

tcat-math-quad-6.qHtml: What is the sum of all fourth roots of 16?
tcat-math-quad-6.explainHtml: The equation x4 - 16 = 0 has four roots: 2, -2, 2i, -2i. Sum of roots = 2 + (-2) + 2i + (-2i) = 0 (or by Vieta formula, the coefficient of x3 is 0).

tcat-math-pf-1.qHtml: A rational fraction P(x)/Q(x) where degree of P(x) is strictly less than degree of Q(x) is called:
tcat-math-pf-1.explainHtml: By definition, if deg(P) < deg(Q), it is proper. If deg(P) \ge deg(Q), it is improper and must first be divided using polynomial long division.

tcat-math-pf-2.qHtml: What is the form of partial fractions for 1 / [(x - 1)(x + 2)]?
optionsHtml: A / (x−1)2 + B / (x + 2)
tcat-math-pf-2.explainHtml: For distinct non-repeated linear factors (x - a) and (x - b), the standard partial fraction decomposition is A/(x - a) + B/(x - b).

tcat-math-pf-3.qHtml: Find the value of A in the partial fraction resolution: 1 / [(x - 1)(x + 2)] = A / (x - 1) + B / (x + 2).
tcat-math-pf-3.explainHtml: Multiplying by (x - 1)(x + 2): 1 = A(x + 2) + B(x - 1). Setting x = 1 gives 1 = A(3) + 0 \implies A = 1/3.

tcat-math-pf-4.qHtml: What is the correct form of partial fraction decomposition for (x + 1) / [x2(x - 2)]?
optionsHtml: A / x + B / x2 + C / (x - 2)
A / x2 + B / (x - 2)
(Ax + B) / x2 + C / (x - 2)
tcat-math-pf-4.explainHtml: For a repeated linear factor (x)2, we must include terms for each ascending power: A/x + B/x2, along with C/(x - 2) for the distinct linear factor.

tcat-math-pf-5.qHtml: Resolve into partial fractions: (2x + 3) / [(x - 1)(x2 + 1)]. What is the coefficient of x in the numerator of the quadratic term (Bx + C)/(x2 + 1)?
tcat-math-pf-5.explainHtml: 2x + 3 = A(x2 + 1) + (Bx + C)(x - 1). Put x = 1: 5 = 2A \implies A = 5/2. Equating coefficients of x2: 0 = A + B \implies B = -A = -5/2.

tcat-math-seq-1.qHtml: What is the 10th term of the arithmetic progression 2, 7, 12, 17, ...?

tcat-math-seq-2.qHtml: What is the sum of the infinite geometric series 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ...?

tcat-math-seq-3.qHtml: If the arithmetic mean between two positive numbers a and b is 5 and their geometric mean is 4, what is their harmonic mean?
tcat-math-seq-3.explainHtml: By the fundamental relation between AM, GM, and HM: GM2 = AM · HM. Therefore, 42 = 5 · HM \implies 16 = 5 · HM \implies HM = 16/5 = 3.2.

tcat-math-seq-4.qHtml: What is the sum of the first n natural numbers 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + n?
tcat-math-seq-4.explainHtml: _(k=1)^n k = n(n + 1)/2. (While k^(2) = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 and k^(3) = [n(n+1)/2]²).

tcat-math-seq-5.qHtml: If the p-th term of an HP is q and the q-th term is p, what is the (pq)-th term?
tcat-math-seq-5.explainHtml: In the corresponding AP, the p-th term is 1/q and the q-th term is 1/p. Common difference d = (1/p - 1/q)/(q - p) = 1/(pq). First term a = 1/(pq). Thus the (pq)-th term of AP is a + (pq - 1)d = 1/(pq) + (pq - 1)/(pq) = pq/(pq) = 1. Hence in HP it is 1/1 = 1.

tcat-math-pcp-1.qHtml: What is the numerical value of 7P3?

tcat-math-pcp-2.qHtml: In how many different ways can 5 people be seated in a circular ring?
tcat-math-pcp-2.explainHtml: The number of circular permutations of n distinct objects is (n - 1)!. For 5 people: (5 - 1)! = 4! = 24.

tcat-math-pcp-3.qHtml: If (8n​)=(12n​), what is the value of n?
tcat-math-pcp-3.explainHtml: If nCx = nCy and x \ne y, then x + y = n. Here, 8 + 12 = n \implies n = 20.

tcat-math-pcp-4.qHtml: Two unbiased dice are rolled simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is 7?
tcat-math-pcp-4.explainHtml: Total outcomes = 36. Favorable outcomes giving sum 7 are: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) = 6 pairs. P = 6/36 = 1/6.

tcat-math-pcp-5.qHtml: A committee of 4 is to be chosen from 6 men and 4 women. What is the probability that the committee contains at least one woman?
tcat-math-pcp-5.explainHtml: Total ways to choose 4 from 10 = (410​) = 210. Ways with NO women (all 4 men) = (46​) = 15. Probability of no women = 15/210 = 1/14. Probability of at least one woman = 1 - 1/14 = 13/14.

tcat-math-mib-1.qHtml: What is the total number of terms in the binomial expansion of (a+b)n for positive integer n?
tcat-math-mib-1.explainHtml: The binomial expansion of (a+b)n contains (n + 1) terms, starting from r = 0 up to r = n.

tcat-math-mib-2.qHtml: What is the sum of all binomial coefficients C0 + C1 + C2 + ... + Cn in the expansion of (1+x)n?
tcat-math-mib-2.explainHtml: Setting x = 1 in (1+x)n = C0 + C1·x + C2·x2 + ... + Cn·xn gives (1+1)n=2n.

tcat-math-mib-3.qHtml: What is the term independent of x in the expansion of (x+1/x)6?
tcat-math-mib-3.explainHtml: General term Tr+1​=(r6​) · x6−r · (x−1)^r = (r6​) · x6−2r. For term independent of x, set 6 - 2r = 0 \implies r = 3. T4​=(36​) = 20.

tcat-math-mib-4.qHtml: What is the middle term in the expansion of (x−2y)8?
tcat-math-mib-4.explainHtml: When n is even (n = 8), there is a single middle term at position (n/2 + 1) = 8/2 + 1 = 5th term (T5).

tcat-math-mib-5.qHtml: For what range of x is the infinite binomial series (1 - 2x)^{-1/2} valid and convergent?
optionsHtml: ∣x∣ < 1/2
∣x∣ < 1
∣x∣ < 2
∣x∣ \le 1/2
tcat-math-mib-5.explainHtml: The binomial series (1+y)n for rational non-integer n converges if and only if ∣y∣ < 1. Here y = -2x, so |-2x| < 1 \implies 2|x| < 1 \implies ∣x∣ < 1/2.

tcat-math-fot-1.qHtml: How many radians are in an angle of 135 degrees?
tcat-math-fot-1.explainHtml: θ (rad) = 135∘ × (π / 180∘) = (135/180)π = 3\pi/4 radians.

tcat-math-fot-2.qHtml: What is the area of a circular sector with radius r and central angle θ radians?
optionsHtml: (1/2) r2\theta
r2\theta
π r2\theta
tcat-math-fot-2.explainHtml: The formula for the area of a sector is A = (1/2)r2θ, where θ is measured in radians.

tcat-math-fot-3.qHtml: If sin(θ) = -3/5 and θ is in the third quadrant, what is the value of tan(θ)?
tcat-math-fot-3.explainHtml: In the third quadrant, tangent is positive. Since sin(θ) = -3/5, cos(θ) = -{1 - (−3/5)2} = -4/5. Thus tan(θ) = sin/cos = (-3/5)/(-4/5) = 3/4.

tcat-math-fot-4.qHtml: An arc of length 15 cm subtends a central angle of 1.5 radians in a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
tcat-math-fot-4.explainHtml: Using the arc length formula l = rθ: 15 = r(1.5) \implies r = 15 / 1.5 = 10 cm.

tcat-math-fot-5.qHtml: If \sec(θ) + tan(θ) = 3, what is the value of \sec(θ) - tan(θ)?
tcat-math-fot-5.explainHtml: Since \sec2(θ) - tan^2(θ) = 1, (\sec(θ) + tan(θ))(\sec(θ) - tan(θ)) = 1. Given \sec(θ) + tan(θ) = 3, it follows that \sec(θ) - tan($\theta) = 1/3.

tcat-math-ti-1.qHtml: What is the simplified form of sin(2α)?
optionsHtml: 2sin(α)cos(α)
cos^2(α) - sin^2(α)
2sin(α)
sin^2(α)
tcat-math-ti-1.explainHtml: By the double-angle identity: sin(2α) = 2sin(α)cos(α).

tcat-math-ti-2.qHtml: What is the value of cos(90∘+θ)?
optionsHtml: -sin(θ)
sin(θ)
cos(θ)
-cos(θ)
tcat-math-ti-2.explainHtml: cos(90∘+θ) = cos(90∘)cos(θ) - sin(90∘)sin(θ) = 0 - 1·sin(θ) = -sin(θ).

tcat-math-ti-3.qHtml: What is the exact value of cos(15∘)?
optionsHtml: ({6} + {2}) / 4
({6} - {2}) / 4
tcat-math-ti-3.explainHtml: cos(15∘) = cos(45∘−30∘) = cos(45∘)cos(30∘) + sin(45∘)sin(30∘) = (1/{2})({3}/2) + (1/{2})(1/2) = ({3} + 1)/(2{2}) = ({6} + {2})/4.

tcat-math-ti-4.qHtml: Express 2sin(5θ)cos(3θ) as a sum or difference of trigonometric functions.
optionsHtml: sin(8θ) + sin(2θ)
cos(8θ) + cos(2θ)
sin(8θ) - sin(2θ)
cos(8θ) - cos(2θ)
tcat-math-ti-4.explainHtml: Using product-to-sum formula: 2sin(A)cos(B) = sin(A + B) + sin(A - B). Here A = 5θ, B = 3θ⟹sin(8θ) + sin(2θ).

tcat-math-ti-5.qHtml: If tan(α) = 1/2 and tan(β) = 1/3, what is the value of α+β?
optionsHtml: π / 4 (45∘)
π / 6 (30∘)
π / 3 (60∘)
π / 2 (90∘)
tcat-math-ti-5.explainHtml: tan(α+β) = (tanα+tanβ) / (1 - tanαtanβ) = (1/2 + 1/3) / (1 - (1/2)(1/3)) = (5/6) / (5/6) = 1. Since α, β are acute, α+β = \arctan(1) = π/4.

tcat-math-tfg-1.qHtml: What is the period of the tangent function y = tan(x)?
optionsHtml: π
π / 2
tcat-math-tfg-1.explainHtml: The fundamental period of tan(x) and \cot(x) is π, while the period of sin(x), cos(x), \sec(x), and \csc(x) is 2\pi.

tcat-math-tfg-2.qHtml: What is the range of the function f(x) = cos(x)?
tcat-math-tfg-2.explainHtml: For all real values of x, -1 \le cos(x) \le 1, so the range is the closed interval [-1, 1].

tcat-math-tfg-3.qHtml: What is the period of the function f(x) = 3sin(4x)?
optionsHtml: π / 2
π
π / 4
tcat-math-tfg-3.explainHtml: The period of sin(kx) is 2\pi / ∣k∣. Here k = 4, so period = 2\pi / 4 = π / 2.

tcat-math-tfg-4.qHtml: What is the maximum value attained by the function f(x) = 3sin(x) + 4cos(x)?
tcat-math-tfg-4.explainHtml: The maximum value of asin(x) + bcos(x) is {a2+b2}. Here {32+42} = {9 + 16} = {25} = 5.

tcat-math-tfg-5.qHtml: At which points does the function f(x) = tan(x) have vertical asymptotes?
optionsHtml: x = (2k + 1)π/2, k \in Z
tcat-math-tfg-5.explainHtml: tan(x) = sin(x)/cos(x) is undefined wherever cos(x) = 0. The zeros of cosine occur at odd multiples of π/2, i.e., x = (2k + 1)π/2 for all integers k.

tcat-math-aot-1.qHtml: According to the Law of Cosines for a triangle ABC, c2 is equal to:
optionsHtml: a2+b2 - 2abcos(C)
a2+b2 + 2abcos(C)
a2−b2 - 2abcos(C)
(a+b)2−cos(C)
tcat-math-aot-1.explainHtml: The Law of Cosines states c2=a2 + b2 - 2abcos(C).

tcat-math-aot-2.qHtml: In a triangle ABC, the circumradius R is given by:
optionsHtml: a / (2sin A)
a / sin A
2a / sin A
tcat-math-aot-2.explainHtml: By the extended Law of Sines: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R \implies R = a / (2sin A) = abc / (4\Delta).

tcat-math-aot-3.qHtml: What is the inradius r of a triangle with area \δ = 24 $cm^{2} and semi-perimeter s = 8 cm?
tcat-math-aot-3.explainHtml: The inradius formula is r = \$\delta / s. Here r = 24 / 8 = 3 cm.

tcat-math-aot-4.qHtml: In a triangle ABC, if a = 5, b = 6, and c = 7, what is the value of cos(A)?
tcat-math-aot-4.explainHtml: cos(A) = (b2+c2 - a2) / (2bc) = (36 + 49 - 25) / (2 · 6 · 7) = 60 / 84 = 5/7.

tcat-math-aot-5.qHtml: For an equilateral triangle of side a, what is the ratio of inradius r to circumradius R (r : R)?
tcat-math-aot-5.explainHtml: For an equilateral triangle, r = a / (2{3}) and R = a / {3}. Thus r / R = [a/(2{3})] / [a/{3}] = 1/2, so the ratio is 1 : 2.

tcat-math-fl-1.explainHtml: Using \lim_{θ \to 0} sin(θ)/θ = 1, \\limx→0​ 7 · [$\sin(7x)/(7x)] = 7(1) = 7.

tcat-math-fl-2.qHtml: A function f(x) is said to be even if:
tcat-math-fl-2.explainHtml: A function is even if f(-x) = f(x) for all x in its domain (symmetric about the y-axis), and odd if f(-x) = -f(x).

tcat-math-fl-3.qHtml: Evaluate the limit limn→∞​(1+1/n)3n.
tcat-math-fl-3.explainHtml: By definition of Euler number, limn→∞​(1+1/n)n = e. Thus [(1+1/n)n]^3 = e3.

tcat-math-fl-4.explainHtml: Factor numerator: x3 - 8 = (x - 2)(x2 + 2x + 4). Cancel (x - 2): \\limx→2​ ($x^{2} + 2x + 4) = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

tcat-math-fl-5.qHtml: Evaluate \\_(x → 0){1 - cos(x)}{$x^{2}}.
tcat-math-fl-5.explainHtml: 1 - cos(x) = 2sin^2(x/2). So [2sin^2(x/2)] / x2 = (1/2) · [sin(x/2) / (x/2)]^2 → (1/2)(1)2 = 1/2.

tcat-math-fl-6.qHtml: For what value of k is the function f(x) = { (x2 - 9)/(x - 3) for x \ne 3, k for x = 3 } continuous at x = 3?
tcat-math-fl-6.explainHtml: For continuity, \\limx→3​ f(x) = f(3). \\limx→3​ (x2 - 9)/(x - 3) = \\$\lim_{x \to 3} (x + 3) = 6. Thus k = 6.

tcat-math-diff-1.qHtml: What is the derivative of f(x) = ln(x) with respect to x for x > 0?
tcat-math-diff-1.explainHtml: The standard derivative of the natural logarithm ln(x) is d/dx [ln(x)] = 1/x.

tcat-math-diff-2.qHtml: What is the derivative of tan(x) with respect to x?
optionsHtml: tan^2(x)
tcat-math-diff-2.explainHtml: By trigonometric differentiation: d/dx [tan(x)] = \$sec^{2}(x).

tcat-math-diff-3.qHtml: If y = e3xsin(2x), find dy/dx at x = 0.
tcat-math-diff-3.explainHtml: dy/dx = 3e3xsin(2x) + 2e3xcos(2x). At x = 0: dy/dx = 3(1)(0) + 2(1)(1) = 2.

tcat-math-diff-4.qHtml: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve y = x3 - 3x + 2 at x = 2.
tcat-math-diff-4.explainHtml: dy/dx = 3x2 - 3. At x = 2, slope m = 3(2)2 - 3 = 12 - 3 = 9.

tcat-math-diff-5.qHtml: If x = acos^3(θ) and y = asin^3(θ), what is dy/dx at θ = π/4?
tcat-math-diff-5.explainHtml: dx/dθ = -3acos^2(θ)sin(θ), dy/dθ = 3asin^2(θ)cos(θ). dy/dx = (dy/dθ)/(dx/dθ) = -tan(θ). At θ = π/4, dy/dx = -tan(π/4) = -1.

tcat-math-diff-6.qHtml: What is the maximum value of the function f(x) = x(10 - x) on the interval [0, 10]?
tcat-math-diff-6.explainHtml: f(x) = 10x - x2. f'(x) = 10 - 2x = 0 \implies x = 5. f''(x) = -2 < 0 (maximum). Maximum value f(5) = 5(10 - 5) = 25.

optionsHtml: tan(x) + c
-tan(x) + c
\sec(x)tan(x) + c
tcat-math-int-1.explainHtml: Since d/dx [tan(x)] = \sec2(x), \int \sec2(x) dx = tan(x) + c.

tcat-math-int-2.qHtml: Evaluate the definite integral \int_0^1 (3x2 + 2x) dx.
tcat-math-int-2.explainHtml: (3x^(2) + 2x) dx = [x^(3) + x^(2)]_0¹ = (1 + 1) - (0) = 2.

tcat-math-int-3.qHtml: Evaluate \int {2x}{x2 + 1} dx.
optionsHtml: ln(x2 + 1) + c
1/(x2 + 1) + c
2ln(x) + c
tcat-math-int-3.explainHtml: The numerator is the exact derivative of the denominator: \int [f'(x)/f(x)] dx = ln|f(x)| + c. Thus ln(x2 + 1) + c.

tcat-math-int-4.qHtml: Evaluate by parts: \int x ex dx.
optionsHtml: ex (x - 1) + c
ex (x + 1) + c
x ex−e−x + c
ex + c
tcat-math-int-4.explainHtml: Let u = x, dv = ex dx \implies du = dx, v = ex. \int x ex dx = x ex - \int ex dx = x ex−ex + c = ex(x - 1) + c.

tcat-math-int-5.qHtml: What is the area enclosed between the parabola y = x2 and the line y = 4?
tcat-math-int-5.explainHtml: Intersections occur at x2 = 4 \implies x = -2 to 2. Area = \int_{-2}^2 (4 - x2) dx = 2 \int_0^2 (4 - x2) dx = 2 [4x - x3/3]_0^2 = 2 [8 - 8/3] = 2(16/3) = 32/3.

tcat-math-int-6.qHtml: Evaluate \int_0^{π/2} {sin(x)}{sin(x) + cos(x)} dx.
optionsHtml: π / 4
π / 2
π
tcat-math-int-6.explainHtml: Let I = \int_0^{π/2} {sin x}{sin x + cos x} dx. Using \int_0^a f(x)dx = \int_0^a f(a - x)dx, I = \int_0^{π/2} {cos x}{cos x + sin x} dx. Adding both: 2I = \int_0^{π/2} 1 dx = π/2 \implies I = π/4.

tcat-math-ag-1.qHtml: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to 2x - 3y + 6 = 0?
tcat-math-ag-1.explainHtml: Slope of given line is m1 = -A/B = -2/(-3) = 2/3. For perpendicular lines, m1 · m2 = -1 \implies m2 = -1 / (2/3) = -3/2.

tcat-math-ag-2.qHtml: What is the perpendicular distance from the origin (0, 0) to the line 3x + 4y - 10 = 0?
tcat-math-ag-2.explainHtml: Distance d = |ax1 + by1 + c| / {a2+b2} = |3(0) + 4(0) - 10| / {32+42} = 10 / 5 = 2.

tcat-math-ag-3.qHtml: What is the point dividing the segment joining A(1, 2) and B(4, 8) internally in the ratio 1 : 2?

tcat-math-ag-4.qHtml: What is the equation of the line passing through (2, 3) with an inclination of 45∘?
tcat-math-ag-4.explainHtml: m = tan(45∘) = 1. Equation is y - y1 = m(x - x1) \implies y - 3 = 1(x - 2) \implies y - 3 = x - 2 \implies x - y + 1 = 0.

tcat-math-ag-5.qHtml: Find the distance between the two parallel lines 3x - 4y + 5 = 0 and 3x - 4y - 15 = 0.
tcat-math-ag-5.explainHtml: Distance between parallel lines ax + by + c1 = 0 and ax + by + c2 = 0 is d = |c1 - c2| / {a2+b2} = |5 - (-15)| / {9 + 16} = 20 / 5 = 4.

tcat-math-lp-1.qHtml: Which point satisfies the linear inequality 2x + 3y \le 6?

tcat-math-lp-2.qHtml: In linear programming, the non-negative constraints x \ge 0, y \ge 0 restrict the feasible region to which quadrant?
tcat-math-lp-2.explainHtml: x \ge 0 and y \ge 0 restricts all valid points to the upper-r quadrant (first quadrant).

tcat-math-lp-3.qHtml: A point where two boundary lines of a feasible region intersect is called a:
tcat-math-lp-3.explainHtml: By definition, the vertices of the polygonal feasible region where bounding constraints intersect are called corner points (or vertices/extreme points).

tcat-math-lp-4.qHtml: Maximize the objective function Z = 3x + 5y given corner points (0, 0), (4, 0), (2, 3), and (0, 4).

tcat-math-lp-5.qHtml: If a feasible region in a linear programming problem is unbounded, then the objective function:
optionsHtml: May not have a maximum value
Must have both maximum and minimum values
Always has infinitely many optimal solutions
tcat-math-lp-5.explainHtml: For an unbounded feasible region, the objective function may increase indefinitely, meaning a finite maximum may not exist.

tcat-math-cs-1.qHtml: What is the eccentricity e of a parabola?
tcat-math-cs-1.explainHtml: For a circle e = 0, for an ellipse e < 1, for a parabola e = 1, and for a hyperbola e > 1.

tcat-math-cs-2.qHtml: What is the radius of the circle given by x2+y2 - 4x + 6y - 12 = 0?
tcat-math-cs-2.explainHtml: 2g = -4 \implies g = -2; 2f = 6 \implies f = 3; c = -12. Radius r = {g2+f2 - c} = {(−2)2+32 - (-12)} = {4 + 9 + 12} = {25} = 5.

tcat-math-cs-3.qHtml: What is the focus of the parabola y2 = -16x?
tcat-math-cs-3.explainHtml: Comparing with y2 = -4ax: 4a = 16 \implies a = 4. The parabola opens leftward, so focus is at (-a, 0) = (-4, 0).

tcat-math-cs-4.qHtml: What is the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse x2/25 + y2/9 = 1?
tcat-math-cs-4.explainHtml: Here a2 = 25 (a = 5) and b2 = 9. Length of latus rectum = 2b2 / a = 2(9) / 5 = 18/5.

tcat-math-cs-5.qHtml: What is the eccentricity of the hyperbola x2/16 - y2/9 = 1?
tcat-math-cs-5.explainHtml: c2=a2 + b2 = 16 + 9 = 25 \implies c = 5. Eccentricity e = c / a = 5 / 4.

tcat-math-vec-1.qHtml: What is the magnitude of the vector u = 2i - 3j + 6k?
tcat-math-vec-1.explainHtml: |u| ={22+(−3)2 + 62} = {4 + 9 + 36} = {49} = 7.

tcat-math-vec-2.qHtml: Two non-zero vectors u and v are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if:
tcat-math-vec-2.explainHtml: u · v = |u||v|cos(θ). Since cos(90∘) = 0, orthogonal vectors have dot product equal to 0.

tcat-math-vec-3.qHtml: Find the projection of vector a = i + 2j + 2k onto vector b = 2i + j - 2k.
tcat-math-vec-3.explainHtml: Projection = (a · b) / ∣b∣. a · b = 1(2) + 2(1) + 2(-2) = 2 + 2 - 4 = 0. Thus the projection is 0 (the vectors are perpendicular).

tcat-math-vec-4.qHtml: What is the area of a parallelogram whose adjacent sides are given by vectors a = i + j and b = j + k?
tcat-math-vec-4.explainHtml: Area = |a × b|. a = (1, 1, 0), b = (0, 1, 1). a × b = (1 - 0)i - (1 - 0)j + (1 - 0)k = i - j + k. Magnitude = {12+(−1)2 + 12} = {3}.

tcat-math-vec-5.qHtml: What is the volume of a parallelepiped determined by vectors u = (1, 0, 0), v = (0, 2, 0), and w = (1, 1, 3)?

tcat-math-ns-6.qHtml: Every non-terminating and non-periodic decimal fraction represents which type of number?
tcat-math-ns-6.explainHtml: Non-terminating and non-repeating (non-periodic) decimals cannot be expressed as p/q where p, q are integers and q \ne 0, so they represent irrational numbers.

tcat-math-ns-7.qHtml: What is the additive inverse of the complex number z = -4 + 7i?
tcat-math-ns-7.explainHtml: The additive inverse of a complex number z = a + bi is -z = -a - bi. For z = -4 + 7i, -z = 4 - 7i.

tcat-math-ns-8.qHtml: Find the multiplicative inverse of the complex number z = (1, 2) in ordered pair notation.
tcat-math-ns-8.explainHtml: For z = (a, b), the multiplicative inverse is (a / (a2+b2), -b / (a2+b2)). Here a = 1, b = 2, so a2+b2 = 5, yielding (1/5, -2/5).

tcat-math-ns-9.qHtml: Simplify the algebraic expression: (1+i)4.
tcat-math-ns-9.explainHtml: (1+i)2 = 1 + 2i + i2 = 2i. Therefore, (1+i)4=(2i)2=4i2 = -4.

tcat-math-ns-10.qHtml: According to De Moivre's theorem, what is the value of (cos(theta) + i*sin(theta))^n when n is a negative integer -m (where m is positive)?
tcat-math-ns-10.explainHtml: (cos(theta) + i*sin(theta))^(-m) = cos(-m*theta) + i*sin(-m*theta) = cos(m*theta) - i*sin(m*theta) because cosine is an even function and sine is odd.

tcat-math-ns-11.qHtml: What is the principal argument Arg(z) of the complex number z = -3​ + i?
tcat-math-ns-11.explainHtml: The point (-3​, 1) lies in the second quadrant. The reference angle is α = arctan(|1 / -3​|) = pi/6. Thus, Arg(z) = pi - pi/6 = 5*pi/6.

tcat-math-sfg-6.qHtml: If a finite set A contains 5 distinct elements, how many proper subsets does A possess?
tcat-math-sfg-6.explainHtml: The total number of subsets for a set with n elements is 2n=25 = 32. The number of proper subsets excludes the set itself: 2n - 1 = 31.

tcat-math-sfg-7.qHtml: Let f: R → R be defined by f(x) = 3x - 5. What is the inverse function f^{-1}(x)?
tcat-math-sfg-7.explainHtml: Let y = 3x - 5. Solving for x in terms of y yields 3x = y + 5 \implies x = (y + 5)/3. Therefore, f^{-1}(x) = (x + 5)/3.

tcat-math-sfg-8.qHtml: Which axiom is NOT required for an algebraic structure (S, *) to qualify as a semi-group?
tcat-math-sfg-8.explainHtml: A semi-group requires only closure and associativity. An identity element is required for a monoid, not a general semi-group.

tcat-math-sfg-9.qHtml: In any group (G, *), what is the inverse of the compound element (a * b) for all a, b in G?
tcat-math-sfg-9.explainHtml: By the reversal law of inverses in abstract algebra, (a∗b)−1 = b^{-1} * a^{-1}.

tcat-math-sfg-10.qHtml: What is the order of the cyclic group formed by the fourth roots of unity {1, -1, i, -i} under complex multiplication?
tcat-math-sfg-10.explainHtml: The set {1, -1, i, -i} has 4 elements and is generated by i (i1=i, i2=-1, i3=-i, i4=1). Its group order is 4.

tcat-math-mat-7.qHtml: If A is a square matrix of order n such that At = -A, then matrix A is called a:
tcat-math-mat-7.explainHtml: A matrix A is skew-symmetric if its transpose equals its negative (At = -A), with all principal diagonal entries equal to zero.

tcat-math-mat-8.qHtml: If A is a 3x3 matrix with determinant ∣A∣ = 4, what is the determinant of the scalar multiple 2A?
tcat-math-mat-8.explainHtml: For an n x n matrix, |k*A| = kn∗∣A∣. Here n = 3 and k = 2, so |2A| = 23 * 4 = 8 * 4 = 32.

tcat-math-mat-9.qHtml: If A is a non-singular square matrix of order 3 with determinant ∣A∣ = 3, what is the determinant of adj(A)?
tcat-math-mat-9.explainHtml: For any n x n matrix A, |adj(A)| = |A|^(n - 1). For n = 3, |adj(A)| = |A|^2 = 32 = 9.

tcat-math-mat-10.qHtml: What is the rank of the matrix A = [[1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 6], [3, 6, 9]]?
tcat-math-mat-10.explainHtml: Rows 2 and 3 are exact scalar multiples of Row 1 (R2 = 2*R1, R3 = 3*R1). In row echelon form, two rows reduce to zeros, leaving exactly 1 non-zero row.

tcat-math-mat-11.qHtml: If A and B are symmetric matrices of the same order, under what condition is the product AB also symmetric?
tcat-math-mat-11.explainHtml: (AB)t=Bt * At = BA. For AB to be symmetric, (AB)t must equal AB, meaning BA = AB (the matrices must commute).

tcat-math-quad-7.qHtml: What is the nature of the roots of the quadratic equation 3x2 - 4x + 2 = 0?
tcat-math-quad-7.explainHtml: Discriminant δ=b2 - 4ac = (−4)2 - 4(3)(2) = 16 - 24 = -8. Since δ < 0, roots are complex conjugate and unequal.

tcat-math-quad-8.qHtml: If the sum of the roots of k*x2 - 6x + 2k = 0 is equal to their product, find the value of k (where k \ne 0).
tcat-math-quad-8.explainHtml: Sum of roots = -(-6)/k = 6/k. Product of roots = 2k/k = 2. Setting 6/k = 2 gives k = 3.

tcat-math-quad-9.qHtml: If alpha and beta are the roots of x2 - 5x + 6 = 0, what is the numerical value of alpha2+beta2?
tcat-math-quad-9.explainHtml: α+β = 5 and α∗β = 6. Then alpha2+beta2=(α+beta)2 - 2*α∗β = 25 - 2(6) = 13.

tcat-math-quad-10.qHtml: Find the quadratic equation whose roots are the reciprocals of the roots of ax2 + bx + c = 0 (where a, c \ne 0).
optionsHtml: cx2 + bx + a = 0
cx2 - bx + a = 0
ax2 - bx + c = 0
cx2 + ax + b = 0
tcat-math-quad-10.explainHtml: Substituting x by 1/x: a(1/x)2 + b(1/x) + c = 0. Multiplying through by x2 yields cx2 + bx + a = 0.

tcat-math-quad-11.qHtml: If omega is an imaginary cube root of unity, simplify the expression: (2 + 5*ω + 2*omega2)^6.
tcat-math-quad-11.explainHtml: Rewrite as 2(1 + omega2) + 5*omega. Since 1 + ω+omega2 = 0, 1 + omega2 = -omega. So 2(-omega) + 5*ω = 3*omega. Raising to power 6 gives (3∗omega)6=36 * omega6 = 729 * 1 = 729.

tcat-math-pf-6.qHtml: Which of the following rational expressions represents an improper fraction?
optionsHtml: (x3 + 1) / (x2 + 4)
(x + 1) / (x2 + 4)
(2x - 3) / (x3 - 1)
tcat-math-pf-6.explainHtml: A rational fraction is improper when the degree of the numerator polynomial is greater than or equal to the degree of the denominator polynomial. Degree 3 \ge 2.

tcat-math-pf-7.qHtml: How many partial fractions will the proper rational fraction 1 / [(x - 1)(x + 2)(x - 3)] decompose into?
tcat-math-pf-7.explainHtml: The denominator contains 3 distinct non-repeated linear factors, producing 3 terms: A/(x - 1) + B/(x + 2) + C/(x - 3).

tcat-math-pf-8.qHtml: Find the constant A in the partial fraction expansion: 1 / [(x - 2)(x + 3)] = A/(x - 2) + B/(x + 3).
tcat-math-pf-8.explainHtml: Using the cover-up rule for A: multiply by (x - 2) and evaluate at x = 2: A = 1 / (2 + 3) = 1/5.

tcat-math-pf-9.qHtml: What is the correct partial fraction decomposition form for (x2 + 1) / [(x−1)2 * (x2 + 3)]?
optionsHtml: A/(x - 1) + B/(x−1)2 + (Cx + D)/(x2 + 3)
A/(x - 1) + B/(x2 + 3)
A/(x−1)2 + (Bx + C)/(x2 + 3)
A/(x - 1) + B/(x−1)2 + C/(x2 + 3)
tcat-math-pf-9.explainHtml: Repeated linear factor (x−1)2 gives A/(x - 1) + B/(x−1)2, and irreducible quadratic factor (x2 + 3) requires (Cx + D)/(x2 + 3).

tcat-math-pf-10.qHtml: If (x3) / (x2 - 1) is converted to proper rational form by polynomial division, what is the quotient polynomial?
tcat-math-pf-10.explainHtml: Dividing x3 by (x2 - 1): x3 = x*(x2 - 1) + x. Thus (x3)/(x2 - 1) = x + x/(x2 - 1). The quotient polynomial is x.

tcat-math-seq-6.qHtml: What is the common ratio r of the geometric progression: 2, -6, 18, -54, ...?
tcat-math-seq-6.explainHtml: The common ratio is r = a2 / a1 = -6 / 2 = -3.

tcat-math-seq-7.qHtml: What is the Harmonic Mean (HM) between the two positive numbers 2 and 8?

tcat-math-seq-8.qHtml: For what range of x does the infinite geometric series 1 + x + x2 + ... converge?
optionsHtml: ∣x∣ < 1
∣x∣ \le 1
tcat-math-seq-8.explainHtml: An infinite geometric series converges if and only if the absolute value of the common ratio ∣r∣ < 1. Here r = x, so ∣x∣ < 1.

tcat-math-seq-9.qHtml: If the sum of n terms of an arithmetic progression is S_n = 2n2 + 3n, find the 5th term a5​.
tcat-math-seq-9.explainHtml: an​ = S_n - S_{n-1}. S_5 = 2(25) + 3(5) = 65. S_4 = 2(16) + 3(4) = 44. Thus a5​ = 65 - 44 = 21.

tcat-math-seq-10.qHtml: What is the closed-form sum of squares of the first n natural numbers 12+22 + 32 + ... + n2?
tcat-math-seq-10.explainHtml: The formula for the sum of the squares of the first n natural numbers is Sigma k2 = n(n + 1)(2n + 1) / 6.

tcat-math-seq-11.qHtml: If A, G, and H are the Arithmetic, Geometric, and Harmonic means between two distinct positive numbers, which relationship holds strictly true?
tcat-math-seq-11.explainHtml: For any two unequal positive real numbers, A > G > H, with G2 = A * H.

tcat-math-pcp-6.qHtml: What is the numerical value of 0! (zero factorial)?
tcat-math-pcp-6.explainHtml: By mathematical definition and convention in combinatorics, 0! = 1.

tcat-math-pcp-7.qHtml: How many different 4-letter words can be formed using the letters of the word "MATHS" without repetition?

tcat-math-pcp-8.qHtml: A single card is drawn from a standard deck of 52 playing cards. What is the probability of drawing either a King or a Heart?
tcat-math-pcp-8.explainHtml: There are 4 Kings and 13 Hearts, with 1 card being the King of Hearts. By addition rule: P = 4/52 + 13/52 - 1/52 = 16/52 = 4/13.

tcat-math-pcp-9.qHtml: In how many ways can 6 beads of different colors be arranged to form a circular necklace?
tcat-math-pcp-9.explainHtml: For a necklace that can be flipped over, clockwise and counterclockwise arrangements are indistinguishable: (n - 1)! / 2 = 5! / 2 = 60.

tcat-math-pcp-10.qHtml: What is the total number of distinct permutations that can be formed using all letters of the word "PAKISTAN"?
tcat-math-pcp-10.explainHtml: "PAKISTAN" contains 8 letters with 'A' repeating 2 times. Total permutations = 8! / 2! = 40320 / 2 = 20160.

tcat-math-pcp-11.qHtml: If events A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5, what is P(A union B)?
tcat-math-pcp-11.explainHtml: For independent events, P(A intersect B) = 0.4 * 0.5 = 0.2. Then P(A union B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A intersect B) = 0.4 + 0.5 - 0.2 = 0.7.

tcat-math-mib-6.qHtml: In the principle of mathematical induction, what is the initial verification step called?
tcat-math-mib-6.explainHtml: The step verifying the proposition for the initial value (usually n = 1) is called the basis step or base step.

tcat-math-mib-7.qHtml: What is the sum of the odd binomial coefficients C1 + C3 + C5 + ... in the expansion of (1+x)n?
tcat-math-mib-7.explainHtml: Sum of all coefficients is 2n. Sum of odd coefficients equals sum of even coefficients = 2n / 2 = 2^{n - 1}.

tcat-math-mib-8.qHtml: What is the coefficient of x3 in the expansion of (1−2x)5?
tcat-math-mib-8.explainHtml: General term is (r5​) * 1^{5-r} * (−2x)r. For x3, r = 3: (35​)∗(−2)3 = 10 * (-8) = -80.

tcat-math-mib-9.qHtml: If the expansion of (x+a)n contains exactly 11 terms, what is the value of n?
tcat-math-mib-9.explainHtml: The binomial expansion of (x+a)n with positive integer exponent n contains exactly n + 1 terms. Therefore n + 1 = 11 \implies n = 10.

tcat-math-mib-10.qHtml: For what condition on x is the infinite binomial series (1+x)−2 valid and convergent?
optionsHtml: ∣x∣ < 1
∣x∣ \le 1
tcat-math-mib-10.explainHtml: When the exponent n is a rational or negative number, the expansion of (1+x)n converges if and only if ∣x∣ < 1.

tcat-math-fot-6.qHtml: If an angle in standard position has its terminal side lying on the negative y-axis, what is its radian measure?
tcat-math-fot-6.explainHtml: The negative y-axis corresponds to 270 degrees, which equals 3*pi/2 radians.

tcat-math-fot-7.qHtml: In which quadrant do both conditions sin(theta) < 0 and cos(theta) > 0 simultaneously hold?
tcat-math-fot-7.explainHtml: In Quadrant IV, x-coordinates (cosine) are positive while y-coordinates (sine) are negative.

tcat-math-fot-8.qHtml: If tan(theta) = 3/4 and theta lies in the third quadrant, what is the value of cos(theta)?
tcat-math-fot-8.explainHtml: In Quadrant III, cosine is negative. With opposite = 3 and adjacent = 4, hypotenuse = 5, so cos(theta) = -4/5.

tcat-math-fot-9.qHtml: Find the length of the arc of a circle of radius 6 cm subtended by a central angle of 30 degrees.
tcat-math-fot-9.explainHtml: Convert 30 degrees to radians: θ = 30 * pi/180 = pi/6 rad. Arc length s = r * θ = 6 * (pi/6) = pi cm.

tcat-math-fot-10.qHtml: Simplify the trigonometric expression: (1 - sin2(x)) * (1 + tan2(x)).
optionsHtml: sin2(x)
cos2(x)
tan2(x)
tcat-math-fot-10.explainHtml: 1 - sin2(x) = cos2(x), and 1 + tan2(x) = sec2(x). Their product is cos2(x) * sec2(x) = 1.

tcat-math-ti-6.qHtml: Which of the following is the correct double-angle formula for cos(2*alpha) exclusively in terms of sin(alpha)?
optionsHtml: 1 - 2*sin2(alpha)
2*sin2(alpha) - 1
1 - sin2(alpha)
2*cos2(alpha) - 1
tcat-math-ti-6.explainHtml: cos(2*alpha) = cos2(alpha) - sin2(alpha) = (1 - sin2(alpha)) - sin2(alpha) = 1 - 2*sin2(alpha).

tcat-math-ti-7.qHtml: What is the exact algebraic value of sin(105 degrees)?
optionsHtml: (6​+2​) / 4
(6​−2​) / 4
(3​ + 1) / 2
2​ / 2
tcat-math-ti-7.explainHtml: sin(105) = sin(60 + 45) = sin(60)cos(45) + cos(60)sin(45) = (3​/2)(2​/2) + (1/2)(2​/2) = (6​+2​) / 4.

tcat-math-ti-8.qHtml: Express cos(70∘) - cos(20∘) in product form:
optionsHtml: -2*sin(45∘)*sin(25∘)
2*cos(45∘)*cos(25∘)
2*sin(45∘)*sin(25∘)
-2*cos(45∘)*sin(25∘)
tcat-math-ti-8.explainHtml: Using cos(C) - cos(D) = -2*sin((C + D)/2)*sin((C - D)/2): cos(70∘) - cos(20∘) = -2*sin(45∘)*sin(25∘).

tcat-math-ti-9.explainHtml: Combine over common denominator: [sin(3*theta)cos(theta) - cos(3*theta)sin(theta)] / [sin(theta)cos(theta)] = sin(3*θ - theta) / [(1/2)sin(2*theta)] = sin(2*theta) / [(1/2)sin(2*theta)] = 2.

tcat-math-ti-10.qHtml: If tan(A) = 3/4 and tan(B) = 1/7, what is the value of tan(A + B)?

tcat-math-tfg-6.qHtml: What is the fundamental period of the cotangent function y = cot(x)?
tcat-math-tfg-6.explainHtml: Like the tangent function, cot(x) repeats its values every pi radians.

tcat-math-tfg-7.qHtml: What is the domain of the principal inverse sine function y = arcsin(x)?
tcat-math-tfg-7.explainHtml: Since the sine function maps real numbers to [-1, 1], its inverse arcsin(x) is defined only on the domain [-1, 1].

tcat-math-tfg-8.qHtml: What is the period of the function f(x) = cos(x / 3)?
tcat-math-tfg-8.explainHtml: Period of cos(kx) is 2*pi / k. Here k = 1/3, so period = 2*pi / (1/3) = 6*pi.

tcat-math-tfg-9.qHtml: Evaluate the exact value of the sum: arcsin(1/2) + arccos(1/2).
tcat-math-tfg-9.explainHtml: arcsin(1/2) = pi/6, arccos(1/2) = pi/3. Their sum is pi/6 + pi/3 = pi/2. In general, arcsin(x) + arccos(x) = pi/2 for all x in [-1, 1].

tcat-math-tfg-10.qHtml: Find all solutions to the trigonometric equation sin(x) = 1/2 within the interval [0, 2*pi).
tcat-math-tfg-10.explainHtml: sin(x) is positive in quadrants I and II. In quadrant I, x = pi/6. In quadrant II, x = pi - pi/6 = 5*pi/6.

tcat-math-aot-6.qHtml: If the angle of elevation of the sun is 45∘, what is the length of the shadow cast by a 10-meter vertical pole?
optionsHtml: 10*3​ meters
10/3​ meters
tcat-math-aot-6.explainHtml: tan(45∘) = he / shadow \implies 1 = 10 / shadow \implies shadow = 10 meters.

tcat-math-aot-7.qHtml: In any triangle ABC, the Law of Tangents is expressed as:
optionsHtml: (a - b)/(a + b) = tan((α - beta)/2) / tan((α + beta)/2)
(a + b)/(a - b) = tan((α - beta)/2) / tan((α + beta)/2)
(a - b)/(a + b) = sin((α - beta)/2) / sin((α + beta)/2)
(a - b)/(a + b) = cos((α - beta)/2) / cos((α + beta)/2)
tcat-math-aot-7.explainHtml: By Napier's analogies / Law of Tangents: (a - b)/(a + b) = tan((α - beta)/2) / tan((α + beta)/2).

tcat-math-aot-8.qHtml: In triangle ABC, if side a = 4, side b = 5, and included angle gamma = 60∘, what is the area Delta of the triangle?
optionsHtml: 5*3​ sq units
10*3​ sq units
tcat-math-aot-8.explainHtml: Area δ = (1/2)*a*b*sin(gamma) = (1/2)*(4)*(5)*sin(60∘) = 10*(3​/2) = 5*3​ sq units.

tcat-math-aot-9.qHtml: What is the formula for the radius r1 of the excircle opposite to vertex A in terms of triangle area Delta and semi-perimeter s?
optionsHtml: δ / (s - a)
δ / (s - b)
δ / s
tcat-math-aot-9.explainHtml: The ex-radii are given by r1 = δ / (s - a), r2 = δ / (s - b), and r3 = δ / (s - c).

tcat-math-aot-10.qHtml: In a triangle ABC, if circumradius R = 10 cm and side a = 10 cm, what is the measure of angle alpha opposite to side a?
tcat-math-aot-10.explainHtml: By the extended Law of Sines: a / sin(alpha) = 2R \implies 10 / sin(alpha) = 20 \implies sin(alpha) = 1/2. Hence α=30∘.

tcat-math-fl-7.qHtml: If f(x) = x2 - 4, what is the expanded expression for f(x + 2)?
optionsHtml: x2 + 4x
x2 + 4
x2 - 4x
tcat-math-fl-7.explainHtml: f(x + 2) = (x+2)2 - 4 = x2 + 4x + 4 - 4 = x2 + 4x.

tcat-math-fl-8.explainHtml: Using standard limit lim_{u → 0} (eu - 1)/u = 1 with u = 2x: \$\lim_{x \to 0} 2*(e^{2x} - 1)/(2x) = 2 * 1 = 2.

tcat-math-fl-9.qHtml: What is the natural domain of the real-valued function f(x) = x^{2}- 16?
tcat-math-fl-9.explainHtml: For f(x) to be real, the radicand x2 - 16 \ge 0 \implies (x - 4)(x + 4) \ge 0 \implies x <= -4 or x \ge 4, which is (-infinity, -4] U [4, infinity).

tcat-math-fl-10.qHtml: Evaluate the limit: \limx→0​ [$\sqrt{1 + x} - 1] / x.
tcat-math-fl-10.explainHtml: Rationalize the numerator: [1+x​ - 1][1+x​ + 1] / [x(1+x​ + 1)] = x / [x(1+x​ + 1)] = 1 / (1 + 1) = 1/2.

tcat-math-fl-11.qHtml: For the signum-like function f(x) = ∣x∣ / x (where x \ne 0), what is the r-hand limit \$\lim_{x \to 0^+} f(x)?
tcat-math-fl-11.explainHtml: For x > 0, ∣x∣ = x, so f(x) = x/x = 1. Therefore, \$\lim_{x \to 0^+} f(x) = 1.

tcat-math-diff-7.qHtml: What is the derivative of the exponential function f(x) = ax (where a > 0, a \ne 1) with respect to x?
optionsHtml: ax * ln(a)
ax / ln(a)
tcat-math-diff-7.explainHtml: By the exponential derivative rule, d/dx(ax) = ax * ln(a).

tcat-math-diff-8.qHtml: Find the slope dy/dx of the circle x2+y2 = 25 at the point (3, 4).

tcat-math-diff-9.qHtml: What is the derivative of y = arcsin(2x) with respect to x for |2x| < 1?
optionsHtml: 2 / (1 + 4x2)
tcat-math-diff-9.explainHtml: Using chain rule: dy/dx = [1 / sqrt(1 - (2x)2)] * d/dx(2x) = 2 / 1 -4x^{2}.

tcat-math-diff-10.qHtml: A continuous function f(x) has a point of inflection at x = c if:
optionsHtml: f''(c) = 0 and f''(x) changes sign across x = c
tcat-math-diff-10.explainHtml: A point of inflection occurs where the concavity changes, requiring f''(c) = 0 (or undefined) with f''(x) changing sign across c.

tcat-math-diff-11.qHtml: Find the equation of the normal line to the curve y = x2 at the point (1, 1).
tcat-math-diff-11.explainHtml: dy/dx = 2x \implies slope of tangent at x = 1 is m_t = 2. Slope of normal m_n = -1/2. Equation: y - 1 = -1/2(x - 1) \implies 2y - 2 = -x + 1 \implies x + 2y - 3 = 0.

tcat-math-int-7.qHtml: Evaluate the indefinite integral: integral of e^{3x} dx.
optionsHtml: (1/3)*ex + C
tcat-math-int-7.explainHtml: int e^{ax} dx = (1/a)*e^{ax} + C. Here a = 3, so (1/3)*e^{3x} + C.

tcat-math-int-8.qHtml: Evaluate the integral: integral of 1 / (x2 + 9) dx.
optionsHtml: ln(x2 + 9) + C
tcat-math-int-8.explainHtml: Using standard form int 1 / (x2+a2) dx = (1/a)*arctan(x/a) + C. With a = 3: (1/3)*arctan(x/3) + C.

tcat-math-int-9.qHtml: Evaluate the definite integral: int_0^(pi/4) sec2(x) dx.
tcat-math-int-9.explainHtml: Antiderivative of sec2(x) is tan(x). Evaluating from 0 to pi/4: tan(pi/4) - tan(0) = 1 - 0 = 1.

tcat-math-int-10.qHtml: Using integration by parts, what is the antiderivative of ln(x) dx?
optionsHtml: (lnx)2 / 2 + C
tcat-math-int-10.explainHtml: Let u = ln(x), dv = dx. Then du = 1/x dx, v = x. int ln(x) dx = x*ln(x) - int x*(1/x) dx = x*ln(x) - x + C.

tcat-math-int-11.qHtml: Evaluate the integral: integral of (3x + 2) / (x2 + 1) dx.
optionsHtml: (3/2)*ln(x2 + 1) + 2*arctan(x) + C
3*ln(x2 + 1) + 2*arctan(x) + C
(3/2)*ln(x2 + 1) + arctan(x) + C
3*arctan(x) + 2*ln(x2 + 1) + C
tcat-math-int-11.explainHtml: Split: 3/2 * int (2x)/(x2 + 1) dx + 2 * int 1/(x2 + 1) dx = (3/2)*ln(x2 + 1) + 2*arctan(x) + C.

tcat-math-ag-6.qHtml: What is the midpoint of the line segment connecting P(2, -4) and Q(6, 8)?

tcat-math-ag-7.qHtml: What is the slope of any horizontal line parallel to the x-axis?
tcat-math-ag-7.explainHtml: A line parallel to the x-axis has delta y = 0, so slope m = 0 / delta x = 0.

tcat-math-ag-8.qHtml: Find the acute angle theta between two lines having slopes m1 = 2 and m2 = -3.
tcat-math-ag-8.explainHtml: tan(theta) = |(m2 - m1) / (1 + m1*m2)| = |(-3 - 2) / (1 + (2)(-3))| = |-5 / -5| = 1 \implies θ=45∘.

tcat-math-ag-9.qHtml: What is the equation of the line passing through (2, 3) with a slope of -1?
tcat-math-ag-9.explainHtml: Point-slope form: y - 3 = -1(x - 2) \implies y - 3 = -x + 2 \implies x + y - 5 = 0.

tcat-math-ag-10.qHtml: What is the area of the triangle with vertices at the origin (0, 0), (4, 0), and (0, 6)?
tcat-math-ag-10.explainHtml: Since base is on x-axis (length = 4) and he is on y-axis (length = 6), area = (1/2)*4*6 = 12 sq units.

tcat-math-ag-11.qHtml: What is the necessary and sufficient condition for three stra lines a1*x + b1*y + c1 = 0, a2*x + b2*y + c2 = 0, and a3*x + b3*y + c3 = 0 to be concurrent?
optionsHtml: The 3x3 determinant formed by their coefficients equals 0
The sum of their slopes equals 0
tcat-math-ag-11.explainHtml: Three lines intersect at a common point (are concurrent) if and only if the determinant of the coefficient matrix [[a1, b1, c1], [a2, b2, c2], [a3, b3, c3]] is zero.

tcat-math-lp-6.qHtml: Which geometric half-plane does the origin (0, 0) belong to with respect to the inequality 3x - 4y \le 12?
tcat-math-lp-6.explainHtml: Testing (0, 0): 3(0) - 4(0) = 0 \le 12, which is true. Hence the origin lies in the solution half-plane.

tcat-math-lp-7.qHtml: In linear programming, the linear function of decision variables to be maximized or minimized is called the:
tcat-math-lp-7.explainHtml: The function that expresses the goal (e.g. profit maximization or cost minimization) is the objective function.

tcat-math-lp-8.qHtml: Where does the optimal (maximum or minimum) value of an objective function always occur in a bounded feasible polygon?
optionsHtml: At one of the corner points (vertices)
tcat-math-lp-8.explainHtml: By the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Programming, optimal values of a linear objective function occur at the extreme points (corner points) of the feasible region.

tcat-math-lp-9.qHtml: Maximize Z = 2x + 3y subject to the constraints: x \ge 0, y \ge 0, and x + y \le 4.
tcat-math-lp-9.explainHtml: Corner points are (0, 0), (4, 0), and (0, 4). Evaluating Z: at (0,0) Z=0; at (4,0) Z=8; at (0,4) Z=12. The maximum is 12.

tcat-math-lp-10.qHtml: If a linear programming problem has an unbounded feasible region in the direction of optimization, the problem has:
optionsHtml: Multiple optimal solutions on all boundaries
tcat-math-lp-10.explainHtml: If the feasible region extends indefinitely in the direction that increases the objective function, the maximum value is infinite (unbounded solution).

tcat-math-cs-6.qHtml: What is the locus of a point whose distance from a fixed focus is equal to its distance from a fixed directrix line (eccentricity e = 1)?
tcat-math-cs-6.explainHtml: By geometric definition of conics, e = 1 defines a parabola.

tcat-math-cs-7.qHtml: What are the center coordinates of the circle given by (x−3)2+(y+5)2 = 49?
tcat-math-cs-7.explainHtml: Standard circle equation is (x−h)2+(y−k)2=r2. Here h = 3, k = -5, so center is (3, -5).

tcat-math-cs-8.qHtml: What is the length of the major axis of the ellipse x2/25 + y2/9 = 1?
tcat-math-cs-8.explainHtml: Here a2 = 25 \implies a = 5. The length of the major axis is 2a = 2 * 5 = 10.

tcat-math-cs-9.qHtml: What are the coordinates of the foci of the hyperbola x2/16 - y2/9 = 1?
tcat-math-cs-9.explainHtml: For a horizontal hyperbola, c2=a2 + b2 = 16 + 9 = 25 \implies c = 5. Foci are located at (+-c, 0) = (+-5, 0).

tcat-math-cs-10.qHtml: What is the equation of the directrix of the parabola y2 = 8x?
tcat-math-cs-10.explainHtml: Standard form y2 = 4ax. 4a = 8 \implies a = 2. Directrix of y2 = 4ax is x = -a \implies x = -2.

tcat-math-cs-11.qHtml: What is the condition of tangency for the stra line y = mx + c to touch the circle x2+y2=a2?
optionsHtml: c2=a2 * (1 + m2)
c2=a2 * (1 - m2)
c2=a2 / (1 + m2)
tcat-math-cs-11.explainHtml: The perpendicular distance from center (0, 0) to line mx - y + c = 0 is |c| / 1 +m^{2}. Equating to radius a gives c2=a2*(1 + m2).

tcat-math-vec-6.qHtml: A vector having zero magnitude and an arbitrary, indeterminate direction is known as a:
tcat-math-vec-6.explainHtml: A null or zero vector has magnitude 0 and no specific direction.

tcat-math-vec-7.qHtml: What is the unit vector in the direction of vector v = 3i - 4j?
tcat-math-vec-7.explainHtml: Magnitude ∣v∣ = sqrt(32+(−4)2) = 9+16​ = 5. Unit vector = v / ∣v∣ = (3i - 4j) / 5.

tcat-math-vec-8.qHtml: If two non-zero vectors a and b are parallel or collinear, what is their cross product a x b?
tcat-math-vec-8.explainHtml: a x b = |a||b|sin(theta) n_hat. When parallel, θ = 0 or 180∘, so sin(theta) = 0, giving the zero vector 0.

tcat-math-vec-9.qHtml: Find the work done by a constant force F = 2i + 3j + k acting on a particle moving from the origin to displacement d = 4i - j + 2k.

tcat-math-vec-10.qHtml: What is the numerical value of the scalar triple product [i, j, k]?
tcat-math-vec-10.explainHtml: [i, j, k] = i · (j x k). Since j x k = i, i · i = 1.

tcat-math-sfg-11.qHtml: If a binary operation * on a set S satisfies (a * b) * c = a * (b * c) for all a, b, c in S, the operation is called:
tcat-math-sfg-11.explainHtml: By definition, an operation is associative if grouping does not change the result: (a * b) * c = a * (b * c).

tcat-math-sfg-12.qHtml: What is the identity element in the group (Z, +) of integers under addition?
tcat-math-sfg-12.explainHtml: For any integer a, a + 0 = 0 + a = a. Thus, 0 is the additive identity.

tcat-math-sfg-13.qHtml: A function f: A → B is said to be bijective if and only if it is:
tcat-math-sfg-13.explainHtml: A bijection is a one-to-one correspondence, meaning the mapping is simultaneously injective and surjective.

tcat-math-sfg-14.qHtml: Under the operation of multiplication modulo 5 on the set {1, 2, 3, 4}, what is the inverse of 3?
tcat-math-sfg-14.explainHtml: In multiplication mod 5, 3 * 2 = 6 = 1 (mod 5). Since the product equals the identity 1, the multiplicative inverse of 3 is 2.

tcat-math-sfg-15.qHtml: How many proper non-empty subsets does a finite set S with 5 elements possess?
tcat-math-sfg-15.explainHtml: Total subsets = 25 = 32. Proper subsets exclude the set itself (32 - 1 = 31). Non-empty proper subsets also exclude the empty set (31 - 1 = 30).

tcat-math-sfg-16.qHtml: In any mathematical group (G, *), what is the inverse of the element (a * b)?
optionsHtml: (a∗b)−1 does not exist
tcat-math-sfg-16.explainHtml: By the shoes-and-socks property of groups, (a∗b)−1 = b^{-1} * a^{-1} because (a * b) * (b^{-1} * a^{-1}) = a * (b * b^{-1}) * a^{-1} = a * e * a^{-1} = e.

tcat-math-pf-11.qHtml: A rational fraction P(x) / Q(x) is classified as an improper fraction when:
optionsHtml: Degree of P(x) \ge Degree of Q(x)
Degree of P(x) < Degree of Q(x)
tcat-math-pf-11.explainHtml: A fraction P(x)/Q(x) is improper if the degree of the numerator polynomial P(x) is greater than or equal to the degree of the denominator Q(x).

tcat-math-pf-12.qHtml: For the fraction (2x + 1) / ((x - 2)(x + 3)), how many partial fraction terms are formed?
tcat-math-pf-12.explainHtml: The denominator has 2 distinct linear non-repeated factors, so the decomposition takes the form A/(x - 2) + B/(x + 3), which is 2 terms.

tcat-math-pf-13.qHtml: What is the correct form of the partial fraction decomposition for 1 / (x2 (x + 1))?
optionsHtml: A/x + B/x2 + C/(x + 1)
Ax / x2 + B/(x + 1)
A/x2 + B/(x + 1)
(Ax + B)/x2 + C/(x + 1)
tcat-math-pf-13.explainHtml: For a repeated linear factor x2, the terms must ascend in power: A/x + B/x2, followed by C/(x + 1) for the distinct linear factor.

tcat-math-pf-14.qHtml: In the identity 1 / ((x - 1)(x + 2)) = A / (x - 1) + B / (x + 2), find the value of constant A.
tcat-math-pf-14.explainHtml: Multiplying through by (x - 1)(x + 2) gives 1 = A(x + 2) + B(x - 1). Setting x = 1 yields 1 = A(3) \implies A = 1/3.

tcat-math-pf-15.qHtml: In decomposing (5x2 - 2) / ((x2 + 1)(x - 1)), what is the standard numerator chosen for the irreducible quadratic factor (x2 + 1)?
optionsHtml: Ax2 + B
A / (x2 + 1)
tcat-math-pf-15.explainHtml: For an irreducible non-repeated quadratic factor (x2 + 1) in the denominator, the corresponding partial fraction numerator is linear, namely (Ax + B).

tcat-math-pf-16.qHtml: Convert (x3 + 1) / (x2 - 1) into polynomial quotient plus proper rational fraction before partial fraction resolution:
optionsHtml: x + (x + 1)/(x2 - 1)
x + 1/(x2 - 1)
x2 + 1/(x - 1)
1 + x/(x2 - 1)
tcat-math-pf-16.explainHtml: Dividing x3 + 1 by x2 - 1: x3 = x(x2 - 1) + x, so x3 + 1 = x(x2 - 1) + (x + 1). Hence (x3 + 1)/(x2 - 1) = x + (x + 1)/(x2 - 1).

tcat-math-mibt-11.qHtml: What is the sum of the binomial coefficients in the expansion of (1+x)n?
tcat-math-mibt-11.explainHtml: Putting x = 1 into (1+x)n gives (1+1)n=2n=(0n​)+(1n​) + ... + C(n,n).

tcat-math-mibt-12.qHtml: The formula for the sum of the first n cubes, 13+23 + ... + n3, is equal to:
optionsHtml: n2(n + 1) / 2
tcat-math-mibt-12.explainHtml: By standard mathematical induction, the sum of cubes of first n natural numbers is [n(n + 1)/2]^2, which is the square of the sum of first n numbers.

tcat-math-mibt-13.qHtml: What is the general term Tr+1​ in the binomial expansion of (a+b)n for a positive integer n?
optionsHtml: \binom{n}{r}∗an−r∗b^{r}
(rn​)∗ar * b^{n - r}
(rn​) * a^{n - r - 1} * b^{r+1}
tcat-math-mibt-13.explainHtml: By the Binomial Theorem, the (r + 1)-th term is given by Tr+1​ = (n choose r) * a^{n - r} * br.

tcat-math-mibt-14.qHtml: Find the term independent of x in the expansion of (x+1/x)6.
tcat-math-mibt-14.explainHtml: Tr+1​=(r6​) * x^{6 - r} * (x^{-1})^r = (r6​) * x^{6 - 2r}. For x0, 6 - 2r = 0 \implies r = 3. T4​=(36​) = 6!/(3!3!) = 20.

tcat-math-mibt-15.qHtml: The expansion of (1−x)−2 is valid only when:
optionsHtml: ∣x∣ < 1
∣x∣ \le 1
tcat-math-mibt-15.explainHtml: For any non-positive or fractional exponent, the infinite binomial series (1+y)n converges if and only if ∣y∣ < 1. Here |-x| = ∣x∣ < 1.

tcat-math-mibt-16.qHtml: In the expansion of (1+2x)−1, what is the coefficient of x3?
tcat-math-mibt-16.explainHtml: (1+y)−1 = 1 - y + y2−y3 + ... With y = 2x, the term is -(2x)3 = -8x3. So the coefficient of x3 is -8.

tcat-math-fot-11.qHtml: How many radians are there in a complete revolution of 360 degrees?
tcat-math-fot-11.explainHtml: 180∘ = π radians, therefore a full rotation of 360∘ is equal to 2π radians.

tcat-math-fot-12.qHtml: In which quadrant are both sin(θ) < 0 and cos(θ) < 0?
tcat-math-fot-12.explainHtml: In Quadrant III, both x-coordinate (cosine) and y-coordinate (sine) are negative (tangent is positive).

tcat-math-fot-13.qHtml: Find the length of an arc of a circle of radius 6 cm subtended by a central angle of 2.5 radians.
tcat-math-fot-13.explainHtml: Arc length l = r * θ = 6 cm * 2.5 rad = 15 cm.

tcat-math-fot-14.qHtml: What is the area of a circular sector with radius r = 4 cm and central angle θ = π/4 radians?
tcat-math-fot-14.explainHtml: Area of sector = (1/2) * r2 * θ = (1/2) * (16) * (π/4) = 2π cm2.

tcat-math-fot-15.qHtml: If cot(θ) = 5/12 and the terminal ray of θ lies in Quadrant III, what is the exact value of cosec(θ)?
tcat-math-fot-15.explainHtml: cot(θ) = 5/12 \implies tan(θ) = 12/5. In Q III, both sin and cos are negative. Opp = -12, Adj = -5, Hyp = sqrt((−12)2+(−5)2) = 13. sin(θ) = -12/13, so cosec(θ) = 1/sin(θ) = -13/12.

tcat-math-fot-16.qHtml: The value of the trigonometric ratio sec(-300∘) is equal to:
tcat-math-fot-16.explainHtml: sec(-θ) = sec(θ). sec(300∘) = 1 / cos(300∘). cos(300∘) = cos(360∘−60∘) = cos(60∘) = 1/2. Thus, sec(-300∘) = 1 / (1/2) = 2.

tcat-math-ti-11.qHtml: Which of the following fundamental identities is correct for all real angles θ?
optionsHtml: 1 + tan2(θ) = sec2(θ)
1 - sin2(θ) = -cos2(θ)
1 + cot2(θ) = tan2(θ)
sec2(θ) - cosec2(θ) = 1
tcat-math-ti-11.explainHtml: Dividing sin2(θ) + cos2(θ) = 1 by cos2(θ) gives tan2(θ) + 1 = sec2(θ).

tcat-math-ti-12.qHtml: Express sin(2α) in terms of single-angle functions sin(α) and cos(α):
optionsHtml: sin2(α) - cos2(α)
cos2(α) - sin2(α)
tcat-math-ti-12.explainHtml: The double angle formula for sine is sin(2α) = 2 sin(α) cos(α).

tcat-math-ti-13.qHtml: What is the value of cos(75∘)?
optionsHtml: (6​−2​) / 4
(6​+2​) / 4
(3​ - 1) / 2
(3​ + 1) / 2
tcat-math-ti-13.explainHtml: cos(75∘) = cos(45∘+30∘) = cos(45∘)cos(30∘) - sin(45∘)sin(30∘) = (1/2​)(3​/2) - (1/2​)(1/2) = (6​−2​)/4.

tcat-math-ti-14.qHtml: Convert the product 2 sin(5θ) cos(3θ) into a sum of sines:
tcat-math-ti-14.explainHtml: Using 2 sin(A) cos(B) = sin(A + B) + sin(A - B): 2 sin(5θ) cos(3θ) = sin(5θ + 3θ) + sin(5θ - 3θ) = sin(8θ) + sin(2θ).

tcat-math-ti-15.qHtml: What is the exact value of tan(15∘)?
optionsHtml: 3​ - 1
tcat-math-ti-15.explainHtml: tan(15∘) = tan(45∘−30∘) = (1 - 1/3​) / (1 + 1/3​) = (3​ - 1)/(3​ + 1). Multiplying by (3​ - 1): (4 - 2*3​)/2 = 2 - 3​.

tcat-math-ti-16.qHtml: The expression cos(3θ)+cos(θ)sin(3θ)−sin(θ)​ simplifies to:
tcat-math-ti-16.explainHtml: sin(3θ) - sin(θ) = 2 cos(2θ) sin(θ). cos(3θ) + cos(θ) = 2 cos(2θ) cos(θ). Ratio = [2 cos(2θ) sin(θ)] / [2 cos(2θ) cos(θ)] = sin(θ)/cos(θ) = tan(θ).

tcat-math-tfg-11.qHtml: What is the fundamental period of the tangent function y = tan(x)?
tcat-math-tfg-11.explainHtml: The tangent and cotangent functions have a fundamental period of π radians, whereas sine and cosine have a period of 2π.

tcat-math-tfg-12.qHtml: What is the amplitude of the sinusoidal function f(x) = -4 cos(3x + π/2)?
tcat-math-tfg-12.explainHtml: The amplitude of A cos(kx + φ) is given by the absolute value ∣A∣. Here ∣−4∣ = 4.

tcat-math-tfg-13.qHtml: Find the period of the function f(x) = 3 cos(4x - π).
tcat-math-tfg-13.explainHtml: Period of cos(kx) is 2π / ∣k∣. Here k = 4, so the period is 2π / 4 = π/2.

tcat-math-tfg-14.qHtml: What is the principal range of the inverse cosine function y = arccos(x)?
tcat-math-tfg-14.explainHtml: To make cosine bijective, its domain is restricted to [0, π], which becomes the range of y = arccos(x).

tcat-math-tfg-15.explainHtml: Let θ = arctan(4/3). Then tan(θ) = 4/3 (opposite = 4, adjacent = 3). Hypotenuse = 4^{2} + 3^{2} = 5. Therefore sin(θ) = 4/5.

tcat-math-tfg-16.qHtml: Find the number of solutions of the equation sin(2x) = 1 in the closed interval [0, 2π].
tcat-math-tfg-16.explainHtml: For x in [0, 2π], 2x is in [0, 4π]. sin(2x) = 1 when 2x = π/2 or 2x = 5π/2. Thus x = π/4 and x = 5π/4, giving exactly 2 solutions.

tcat-math-aot-11.qHtml: According to the Law of Sines for any triangle ABC, the ratio a / sin(α) is equal to:
tcat-math-aot-11.explainHtml: By the extended Law of Sines: a/sin(α) = b/sin(β) = c/sin(γ) = 2R, where R is the radius of the circumcircle.

tcat-math-aot-12.qHtml: In a triangle ABC, the formula for inradius r is:
tcat-math-aot-12.explainHtml: The inradius of a triangle is given by r = Δ / s, where Δ is the area and s is the semi-perimeter.

tcat-math-aot-13.qHtml: In a r triangle with hypotenuse 10 m and an acute angle of 30∘, what is the length of the side opposite to the 30∘ angle?
optionsHtml: 5 * 3​ m
10 * 3​ m
tcat-math-aot-13.explainHtml: sin(30∘) = Opposite / Hypotenuse \implies 1/2 = Opp / 10 \implies Opposite = 5 m.

tcat-math-aot-14.qHtml: If the sides of a triangle are a = 5, b = 6, and c = 7, find the semi-perimeter s.

tcat-math-aot-15.qHtml: In triangle ABC, if a = 3, b = 4, and c = 5, what is the radius R of its circumscribed circle?
tcat-math-aot-15.explainHtml: Since 32+42=52, this is a r triangle with hypotenuse c = 5. In any r-angled triangle, the circumcentre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, so R = c / 2 = 5 / 2 = 2.5.

tcat-math-aot-16.qHtml: An observer standing 50 m from the base of a vertical tower notes an angle of elevation of 45∘ to the top. What is the he of the tower?
optionsHtml: 50 * 3​ m
tcat-math-aot-16.explainHtml: tan(45∘) = he / distance \implies 1 = h / 50 \implies h = 50 m.

tcat-math-lilp-11.qHtml: If -3x < 12, what is the resulting inequality after dividing both sides by -3?
tcat-math-lilp-11.explainHtml: Dividing or multiplying an inequality by a negative number reverses the direction of the inequality sign: x > 12 / (-3) \implies x > -4.

tcat-math-lilp-12.qHtml: In linear programming, the non-negativity constraints x \ge 0, y \ge 0 restrict the feasible region to which quadrant?
tcat-math-lilp-12.explainHtml: Both x \ge 0 and y \ge 0 describe the first quadrant of the Cartesian coordinate plane.

tcat-math-lilp-13.qHtml: Does the origin (0, 0) satisfy the linear inequality 2x - 3y \le 6?
tcat-math-lilp-13.explainHtml: Substituting (0, 0): 2(0) - 3(0) = 0 \le 6, which is a true statement; hence the origin lies inside the solution half-plane.

tcat-math-lilp-14.qHtml: A point where two boundary lines of the feasible region intersect is termed a:
tcat-math-lilp-14.explainHtml: The intersection of boundary lines bounding a feasible region is known as a corner point or extreme point.

tcat-math-lilp-15.qHtml: Maximize the objective function f(x, y) = 3x + 2y subject to corner points (0, 0), (4, 0), (2, 3), and (0, 4).

tcat-math-lilp-16.qHtml: According to the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Programming, where does the optimal value of a linear objective function occur?
optionsHtml: At one or more corner points (vertices) of the feasible region
At the geometric center of the feasible region
tcat-math-lilp-16.explainHtml: A linear function defined on a convex polygon achieves its global maximum and minimum at the extreme/corner points of the region.

tcat-math-vec-11.qHtml: What is the magnitude of the 3D position vector r = 2i - 3j + 6k?
tcat-math-vec-11.explainHtml: ∣r∣ = sqrt(22+(−3)2 + 62) = 4+9+36​=49​ = 7.

tcat-math-vec-12.qHtml: What is the unit vector in the direction of the vector v = 3i - 4j?
tcat-math-vec-12.explainHtml: The unit vector is v / ∣v∣. Magnitude ∣v∣ = sqrt(32+(−4)2) = 5. Hence v_hat = (3/5)i - (4/5)j.

tcat-math-vec-13.qHtml: Compute the scalar projection of vector a = 3i + 4j onto vector b = i.
tcat-math-vec-13.explainHtml: Scalar projection of a onto b = (a · b) / ∣b∣ = (3*1 + 4*0) / 1 = 3.

tcat-math-vec-14.qHtml: Evaluate the cross product: k x j.
tcat-math-vec-14.explainHtml: In the r-handed cyclic system, j x k = i, so k x j = -(j x k) = -i.

tcat-math-vec-15.qHtml: What is the area of a parallelogram having adjacent side vectors a = 2i + j - k and b = i - j + 2k?
tcat-math-vec-15.explainHtml: a x b = i(2 - 1) - j(4 - (-1)) + k(-2 - 1) = i - 5j - 3k. Magnitude |a x b| = sqrt(12+(−5)2 + (−3)2) = 1+25+9​=35​.

tcat-math-vec-16.qHtml: If the vectors u = i + j, v = j + k, and w = i + λk are coplanar, find the value of λ.
tcat-math-vec-16.explainHtml: Vectors are coplanar when their scalar triple product is zero: det([[1, 1, 0], [0, 1, 1], [1, 0, λ]]) = 1(λ - 0) - 1(0 - 1) = λ + 1 = 0 => λ = -1.

tcat-math-ns-12.qHtml: The set of rational numbers Q and irrational numbers Q' are:
optionsHtml: Disjoint sets whose union is the set of real numbers R
Intersecting sets with infinite common elements
tcat-math-ns-12.explainHtml: Every real number is either rational or irrational, and no number can be both: Q ∩ Q' = ∅ and Q ∪ Q' = R.

tcat-math-ns-13.qHtml: What is the absolute value (modulus) of the complex number z = -6 + 8i?
tcat-math-ns-13.explainHtml: ∣z∣ = sqrt((−6)2+82) = 36+64​=100​ = 10.

tcat-math-ns-14.qHtml: What is the polar form of the complex number z = 1 - i?
optionsHtml: 2​(cos(7π/4) + i sin(7π/4))
2​(cos(π/4) + i sin(π/4))
tcat-math-ns-14.explainHtml: Modulus r = sqrt(12+(−1)2) = 2​. Since x > 0 and y < 0, z lies in the fourth quadrant. Argument θ = 2π - π/4 = 7π/4. Thus z = 2​(cos(7π/4) + i sin(7π/4)).

tcat-math-ns-15.qHtml: According to De Moivre's Theorem, for any integer n, (cos(θ) + i sin(θ))^n equals:
optionsHtml: cosn(θ) + i sinn(θ)
tcat-math-ns-15.explainHtml: De Moivre's theorem states that (cos(θ) + i sin(θ))^n = cos(nθ) + i sin(nθ) for all rational numbers n.

tcat-math-ns-16.qHtml: If ω is a complex cube root of unity, what is the value of 1 + ω + ω^2?
tcat-math-ns-16.explainHtml: The sum of all three cube roots of unity (1, ω, ω^2) is always equal to 0: 1 + ω + ω^2 = 0.

tcat-math-md-12.qHtml: A square matrix A is classified as symmetric if and only if:
optionsHtml: At = A
At = -A
tcat-math-md-12.explainHtml: A matrix equals its transpose (At = A) if and only if it is a symmetric matrix.

tcat-math-md-13.qHtml: What is the determinant of a 2x2 identity matrix I_2?

tcat-math-md-14.qHtml: If A is a 3x3 matrix and det(A) = 4, what is the value of det(2A)?
tcat-math-md-14.explainHtml: For an n x n matrix, det(k*A) = kn * det(A). For n = 3 and k = 2, det(2A) = 23 * 4 = 8 * 4 = 32.

tcat-math-md-15.qHtml: Find the inverse of the matrix A = [[2, 0], [0, 3]].
tcat-math-md-15.explainHtml: The inverse of a diagonal matrix is formed by taking the reciprocal of each non-zero diagonal entry: diag(1/2, 1/3).

tcat-math-md-16.qHtml: If the determinant of the matrix [[1, x], [4, 8]] is equal to 0, what is the value of x?

tcat-math-qe-12.qHtml: What is the sum of the roots of the quadratic equation 3x2 - 12x + 7 = 0?

tcat-math-qe-13.qHtml: For what value of k does the quadratic equation x2 - 6x + k = 0 have equal (repeated) real roots?
tcat-math-qe-13.explainHtml: Roots are equal when discriminant b2 - 4ac = 0. (−6)2 - 4(1)(k) = 0 \implies 36 - 4k = 0 \implies k = 9.

tcat-math-qe-14.qHtml: If α and β are roots of x2 - 5x + 6 = 0, form the quadratic equation whose roots are 2α and 2β.
optionsHtml: x2 - 10x + 24 = 0
x2 - 10x + 12 = 0
x2 - 5x + 24 = 0
x2 - 20x + 24 = 0
tcat-math-qe-14.explainHtml: New sum S = 2(α + β) = 2(5) = 10. New product P = (2α)(2β) = 4(αβ) = 4(6) = 24. Equation: x2 - Sx + P = x2 - 10x + 24 = 0.

tcat-math-qe-15.qHtml: According to the Remainder Theorem, when polynomial P(x) = 2x3−3x2 + 4x - 5 is divided by (x - 2), what is the remainder?
tcat-math-qe-15.explainHtml: Remainder R = P(2) = 2(2)3 - 3(2)2 + 4(2) - 5 = 2(8) - 3(4) + 8 - 5 = 16 - 12 + 8 - 5 = 7.

tcat-math-qe-16.qHtml: If the roots of ax2 + bx + c = 0 are reciprocal to each other, which condition must hold true?
optionsHtml: b2 = 4ac
tcat-math-qe-16.explainHtml: Product of roots = α * (1/α) = 1. But product = c/a. Hence c/a = 1 \implies a = c.

tcat-math-ss-12.qHtml: What is the 10th term of the arithmetic progression with first term a = 3 and common difference d = 4?
tcat-math-ss-12.explainHtml: an​ = a + (n - 1)d \implies a10​ = 3 + (9)(4) = 3 + 36 = 39.

tcat-math-ss-13.qHtml: What is the sum to infinity of a geometric series with first term a = 4 and common ratio r = 1/2?

tcat-math-ss-14.qHtml: What is the Harmonic Mean (HM) between two positive real numbers a = 2 and b = 6?

tcat-math-ss-15.qHtml: For any two distinct positive real numbers, which inequality relationship strictly holds between AM, GM, and HM?
tcat-math-ss-15.explainHtml: For distinct positive real numbers, the Arithmetic Mean is strictly greater than the Geometric Mean, which is strictly greater than the Harmonic Mean (AM > GM > HM).

tcat-math-ss-16.qHtml: If the n-th term of an arithmetic sequence is an​ = 5n - 3, what is the sum of its first 20 terms?
tcat-math-ss-16.explainHtml: a_{1} = 5(1) - 3 = 2. a20​ = 5(20) - 3 = 97. Sum S_20 = (n/2)(a_{1} + an​) = (20/2)(2 + 97) = 10 * 99 = 990.

tcat-math-pcp-12.qHtml: In how many different orders can 5 distinct books be arranged on a single shelf?
tcat-math-pcp-12.explainHtml: The number of arrangements of 5 distinct items is 5! = 5 * 4 * 3 * 2 * 1 = 120.

tcat-math-pcp-13.qHtml: What is the probability of rolling a prime number on a single fair six-sided die?
tcat-math-pcp-13.explainHtml: Prime outcomes on a standard die are {2, 3, 5} (3 outcomes out of 6). Probability = 3/6 = 1/2.

tcat-math-pcp-14.qHtml: In how many ways can a delegation committee of 3 engineers be selected from a department of 8 engineers?
tcat-math-pcp-14.explainHtml: Selection order does not matter: (38​) = 8! / (3! * 5!) = (8 * 7 * 6) / (3 * 2 * 1) = 56.

tcat-math-pcp-15.qHtml: If two fair coins are tossed simultaneously, what is the probability of obtaining at least one Head?
tcat-math-pcp-15.explainHtml: Sample space = {HH, HT, TH, TT} (4 outcomes). Outcomes with at least one head = {HH, HT, TH} (3 outcomes). P = 3/4.

tcat-math-pcp-16.qHtml: For two independent events A and B with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.5, what is the probability of their union P(A ∪ B)?
tcat-math-pcp-16.explainHtml: For independent events, P(A ∩ B) = P(A) * P(B) = 0.4 * 0.5 = 0.20. Then P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B) = 0.4 + 0.5 - 0.2 = 0.7.

tcat-math-fl-12.qHtml: A real function f(x) is classified as an even function if for all x in its domain:
tcat-math-fl-12.explainHtml: By definition, f(x) is an even function if f(-x) = f(x) for all x in the domain.

tcat-math-fl-14.qHtml: Evaluate the limit: lim_(x → ∞) [(3x2 + 5x) / (2x2 - 7)].
tcat-math-fl-14.explainHtml: Dividing numerator and denominator by highest power x2 gives (3 + 5/x)/(2 - 7/x2) → 3/2 as x → ∞.

tcat-math-fl-15.qHtml: What is the domain of the real-valued function f(x) = 16 -x^{2}?
tcat-math-fl-15.explainHtml: For real values, the radicand must be non-negative: 16 - x2 \ge 0 \implies x2 \le 16 => -4 \le x \le 4.

tcat-math-fl-16.qHtml: Evaluate the limit: lim_(n → ∞) (1+1/n)3n.
tcat-math-fl-16.explainHtml: Using the fundamental definition lim_(n → ∞) (1+1/n)n = e, we have [(1+1/n)n]^3 → e3.

tcat-math-diff-12.qHtml: What is the derivative with respect to x of y = e^{4x}?
tcat-math-diff-12.explainHtml: By chain rule, d/dx [e^{kx}] = k * e^{kx}. Here k = 4, giving 4 e^{4x}.

tcat-math-diff-13.qHtml: Find the derivative of y = ln(sec(x)).

tcat-math-diff-14.qHtml: At what point does the function f(x) = x3 - 3x have a local maximum?
tcat-math-diff-14.explainHtml: f'(x) = 3x2 - 3 = 0 \implies x = ±1. f''(x) = 6x. For x = -1, f''(-1) = -6 < 0 (local maximum). For x = 1, f''(1) = 6 > 0 (local minimum).

tcat-math-diff-15.qHtml: According to Maclaurin's series expansion, what is the coefficient of x2 for f(x) = cos(x)?
tcat-math-diff-15.explainHtml: cos(x) = 1 - x2/2! + x4/4! - ... The coefficient of x2 is -1/2! = -1/2.

tcat-math-int-12.qHtml: What is the indefinite integral ∫ sec2(x) dx?
tcat-math-int-12.explainHtml: Since d/dx [tan(x)] = sec2(x), the anti-derivative ∫ sec2(x) dx is tan(x) + C.

tcat-math-int-13.qHtml: Evaluate the definite integral ∫ from 0 to π/2 of cos(x) dx.
tcat-math-int-13.explainHtml: ∫ cos(x) dx = [sin(x)] from 0 to π/2 = sin(π/2) - sin(0) = 1 - 0 = 1.

tcat-math-int-14.qHtml: Evaluate the indefinite integral: ∫ x * ex dx.
optionsHtml: (x - 1) ex + C
(x + 1) ex + C
x2ex / 2 + C
x ex + C
tcat-math-int-14.explainHtml: Using integration by parts ∫ u v' dx = u v - ∫ u' v dx with u = x, v' = ex: x ex - ∫ ex dx = x ex−ex + C = (x - 1)ex + C.

tcat-math-int-15.qHtml: Evaluate the definite integral: ∫ from 0 to 1 of 1 / (1 + x2) dx.
tcat-math-int-15.explainHtml: ∫ 1/(1 + x2) dx = [arctan(x)] from 0 to 1 = arctan(1) - arctan(0) = π/4 - 0 = π/4.

tcat-math-iag-12.qHtml: What is the slope of the stra line 4x - 2y + 7 = 0?
tcat-math-iag-12.explainHtml: Rewriting in slope-intercept form: 2y = 4x + 7 \implies y = 2x + 7/2. The slope m is 2.

tcat-math-iag-13.qHtml: What is the perpendicular distance from the origin (0, 0) to the line 3x + 4y - 15 = 0?
tcat-math-iag-13.explainHtml: Distance d = |a*x0 + b*y0 + c| / a^{2} + b^{2}= |0 + 0 - 15| /3^{2}+4^{2} = 15 / 5 = 3.

tcat-math-iag-14.qHtml: Find the equation of the line passing through (1, 2) with slope m = 3.
tcat-math-iag-14.explainHtml: y - y1 = m(x - x1) \implies y - 2 = 3(x - 1) \implies y - 2 = 3x - 3 \implies 3x - y - 1 = 0.

tcat-math-iag-15.qHtml: Two lines with slopes m1 and m2 are perpendicular if and only if:
tcat-math-iag-15.explainHtml: Condition for perpendicularity of two non-vertical lines is m1 * m2 = -1 (product of slopes equals -1).

tcat-math-cs-12.qHtml: What is the eccentricity e of any parabola?
tcat-math-cs-12.explainHtml: By geometric definition, a parabola is the locus of a point whose distance from the focus equals its distance from the directrix, giving an eccentricity e = 1.

tcat-math-cs-13.qHtml: What is the coordinates of the focus of the standard parabola y2 = 12x?
tcat-math-cs-13.explainHtml: Comparing with y2 = 4ax: 4a = 12 \implies a = 3. The focus lies at (a, 0) = (3, 0).

tcat-math-cs-14.qHtml: Find the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse x2/25 + y2/9 = 1.
tcat-math-cs-14.explainHtml: Here a2 = 25 (a = 5) and b2 = 9. The length of the latus rectum is 2b2 / a = 2(9) / 5 = 18/5.

tcat-math-cs-15.qHtml: What type of conic section is represented by the general equation x2/16 - y2/9 = 1?
tcat-math-cs-15.explainHtml: An equation of the form x2/a2 - y2/b2 = 1 represents a horizontal hyperbola with eccentricity e > 1.

tcat-math-cs-16.qHtml: What is the length of the latus rectum of the parabola y2 = 16x?
tcat-math-cs-16.explainHtml: For the standard parabola y2 = 4ax, the length of the latus rectum is 4a. Here 4a = 16.

tcat-math-cs-17.qHtml: The eccentricity e of a rectangular hyperbola is always equal to:
tcat-math-cs-17.explainHtml: For an equilateral (rectangular) hyperbola, a = b. Thus e = 1 +b^{2} / a^{2}= √(1 + 1) = √(2).

tcat-math-cs-18.qHtml: What are the coordinates of the foci of the ellipse x2/25 + y2/9 = 1?
tcat-math-cs-18.explainHtml: Here a2 = 25, b2 = 9. c2=a2 - b2 = 25 - 9 = 16 \implies c = 4. Since the major axis is along the x-axis, foci are (±c, 0) = (±4, 0).

tcat-math-cs-19.qHtml: What is the equation of the directrix of the parabola x2 = -12y?
tcat-math-cs-19.explainHtml: Comparing with x2 = -4ay: 4a = 12 \implies a = 3. The focus is at (0, -3) and the directrix is y = a, so y = 3.

tcat-math-cs-20.qHtml: What is the condition for the line y = mx + c to be tangent to the ellipse x2/a2 + y2/b2 = 1?
optionsHtml: c^{2} = a^{2}m^{2}+b^{2}
c^{2} = a^{2}m^{2}−b^{2}
c^{2} = a^{2}−b^{2}m^{2}
tcat-math-cs-20.explainHtml: The condition of tangency for the line y = mx + c to an ellipse x2/a2 + y2/b2 = 1 is c2=a2m2 + b2.

tcat-math-cs-21.qHtml: What are the equations of the asymptotes of the hyperbola x2/16 - y2/9 = 1?
tcat-math-cs-21.explainHtml: For hyperbola x2/a2 - y2/b2 = 1, asymptotes are y = ±(b/a)x. Here a = 4, b = 3, so y = ±(3/4)x.

tcat-math-diff-16.qHtml: What is the derivative of f(x) = ln(sec(x) + tan(x)) with respect to x?
optionsHtml: sec2(x)
tcat-math-diff-16.explainHtml: d/dx [ln(sec(x) + tan(x))] = (sec(x)tan(x) + sec2(x)) / (sec(x) + tan(x)) = sec(x)(tan(x) + sec(x)) / (sec(x) + tan(x)) = sec(x).

tcat-math-diff-17.qHtml: What is the derivative of e^{5x} at x = 0?
tcat-math-diff-17.explainHtml: d/dx [e^{5x}] = 5 e^{5x}. At x = 0, 5 e0 = 5.

tcat-math-diff-18.qHtml: If y = arctan((2x) / (1 - x2)), what is dy/dx for ∣x∣ < 1?
optionsHtml: 2 / (1 + x2)
1 / (1 + x2)
2x / (1 + x2)
-2 / (1 + x2)
