tcat-cs-297.explainHtml: K-map axes use Gray code ordering (00, 01, 11, 10) so that adjacent cells differ in exactly one variable, facilitating visual algebraic grouping.

tcat-cs-298.qHtml: How many 2-to-1 Multiplexers (MUX) are required to construct a complete 8-to-1 Multiplexer tree?
tcat-cs-298.explainHtml: To build an 8-to-1 MUX using 2-to-1 MUXes: Stage 1 requires 4 MUXes, Stage 2 requires 2 MUXes, Stage 3 requires 1 MUX. Total = 4 + 2 + 1 = 7 MUXes.

tcat-cs-299.qHtml: What is the characteristic equation of an edge-triggered J-K Flip-Flop denoting next state Q(t+1)?
tcat-cs-299.explainHtml: The characteristic equation for a J-K flip-flop derived from its truth table is Q(next) = J·Q' + K'·Q.

tcat-cs-300.qHtml: In synchronous sequential circuits, what causes a race condition (static hazard) in combinational logic during input transitions?
optionsHtml: Unequal propagation delays across convergent signal paths resulting in momentary spurious output glitches
Insufficient clock frequency from the quartz crystal oscillator
Excessive fan-out overloading gate voltage thresholds
Inversion of ground and supply voltages
tcat-cs-300.explainHtml: Static hazards occur when differential propagation delays along divergent physical paths cause a transient spike (glitch) before stabilizing to the steady-state Boolean value.

tcat-cs-301.qHtml: Simplify the 4-variable minterm function F(A,B,C,D) = Σm(0, 2, 8, 10) into its minimal Sum-of-Products (SOP) form:
tcat-cs-301.explainHtml: Minterms in binary: m0 (0000), m2 (0010), m8 (1000), m10 (1010). A is 0 or 1, C is 0 or 1, while B is consistently 0 (B') and D is consistently 0 (D'). The four-corner grouping simplifies to B'D'.

tcat-cs-302.qHtml: How many layers are formally defined in the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) OSI Reference Model?
tcat-cs-302.explainHtml: The OSI model defines 7 distinct layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, and Application.

tcat-cs-303.qHtml: What network topology connects all client nodes to a single centralized hardware switch or hub?
tcat-cs-303.explainHtml: In a Star topology, each network host features a dedicated point-to-point link directly to a central hub or switch.

tcat-cs-304.qHtml: What protocol resolves human-readable domain names (e.g., www.example.com) into numerical IP addresses?
tcat-cs-304.explainHtml: DNS translates hierarchical host domain names into machine-routable numerical IP addresses.

tcat-cs-305.qHtml: What is the length of an IPv4 address in bits versus an IPv6 address?
optionsHtml: IPv4 is 32 bits, IPv6 is 128 bits
IPv4 is 16 bits, IPv6 is 64 bits
IPv4 is 64 bits, IPv6 is 256 bits
tcat-cs-305.explainHtml: An IPv4 address consists of 32 bits (4 octets), whereas an IPv6 address consists of 128 bits (16 octets).

tcat-cs-306.qHtml: At which layer of the OSI model does an IP router primarily inspect packets and make forwarding decisions?
tcat-cs-306.explainHtml: Routers operate at Layer 3 (Network Layer), inspecting logical IP headers and using routing tables to forward packets across subnets.

tcat-cs-307.qHtml: What is the standard subnet mask for a default Class C IPv4 network address in dot-decimal notation?
tcat-cs-307.explainHtml: A default Class C network assigns 24 bits to the network prefix (/24), yielding the standard subnet mask 255.255.255.0.

tcat-cs-308.qHtml: How does the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) establish a reliable connection before transmitting application data?
optionsHtml: Via a three-way handshake using SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK control packets
By broadcasting UDP datagrams over the local Ethernet subnet
By requesting an IP lease from a local DHCP server
Via an ICMP echo request and echo reply ping sequence
tcat-cs-308.explainHtml: TCP initiates reliable sessions via the classic 3-way handshake: Client sends SYN, Server replies with SYN-ACK, and Client confirms with ACK.

tcat-cs-309.qHtml: What protocol translates logical Layer 3 IP addresses into physical Layer 2 MAC hardware addresses on a local Ethernet subnet?
tcat-cs-309.explainHtml: ARP broadcasts a request onto the local network segment querying which host owns a target IP address, obtaining its 48-bit MAC address.

tcat-cs-310.qHtml: In the IPv4 network 192.168.10.0/27, what is the maximum number of usable host IP addresses and what is the broadcast address?
tcat-cs-310.explainHtml: A /27 subnet leaves 32 - 27 = 5 host bits. Total addresses = 25 = 32 (indices 0 to 31). Subtracting network (0) and broadcast (31) leaves 32 - 2 = 30 usable hosts.

tcat-cs-311.qHtml: How does TCP Reno handle network congestion when experiencing packet loss detected by three duplicate acknowledgments (triple-duplicate ACK)?
optionsHtml: Halves the congestion window (ssthresh = cwnd / 2), sets cwnd to ssthresh + 3, and performs Fast Retransmit / Fast Recovery without dropping to slow-start
Resets cwnd to 1 MSS immediately and restarts slow-start
tcat-cs-311.explainHtml: Upon receiving 3 duplicate ACKs, TCP Reno executes Fast Retransmit and Fast Recovery: it halves cwnd, sets slow-start threshold ssthresh = cwnd / 2, and recovers without resetting to 1.

tcat-cs-312.qHtml: What is the count-to-infinity problem in Distance Vector routing protocols (e.g., RIP), and what mechanism mitigates it?
optionsHtml: Routing loops causing routing metrics to increment indefinitely; mitigated by Split Horizon and Poison Reverse techniques
Buffer overflows in switches; mitigated by CSMA/CD
Exhaustion of IPv4 addresses; mitigated by NAT
DNS query amplification; mitigated by DNSSEC
tcat-cs-312.explainHtml: In Distance Vector routing, link failure information propagates slowly, causing adjacent nodes to bounce metric updates until reaching infinity (16 in RIP); Split Horizon prevents advertising routes back.

tcat-cs-313.qHtml: In symmetric vs asymmetric cryptography, how does the Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange protocol allow two parties to negotiate a secret session key over an insecure channel?
optionsHtml: By exploiting the computational intractability of the discrete logarithm problem over finite cyclic groups without transmitting the secret exponents
By transmitting public keys encoded in plain text alongside private keys
By using symmetric block ciphers with pre-shared master passwords
By encrypting data through hash digests generated by MD5
tcat-cs-313.explainHtml: Diffie-Hellman relies on the difficulty of computing discrete logarithms in a finite field: Alice and Bob share g and p, compute ga mod p and gb mod p, and combine them into g^{ab} mod p without exposing secrets a or b.

tcat-cs-314.qHtml: In relational database terminology, what is a single row in a table formally called?
tcat-cs-314.explainHtml: In relational database theory, a row is formally referred to as a tuple (or record), while a column represents an attribute.

tcat-cs-315.qHtml: Which SQL command is used to extract data rows from one or more database tables?
tcat-cs-315.explainHtml: The SQL SELECT statement queries and retrieves specified data records from database relations.

tcat-cs-316.qHtml: What type of database key uniquely identifies each distinct record in a relational table and cannot contain NULL values?
tcat-cs-316.explainHtml: A Primary Key is a minimal candidate key that uniquely identifies each tuple in a table; entity integrity dictates it cannot be NULL.

tcat-cs-317.qHtml: Which clause in an SQL SELECT query filters rows based on a specified boolean search condition?
tcat-cs-317.explainHtml: The WHERE clause specifies search predicates to filter tuples returned by an SQL query before aggregation.

tcat-cs-318.qHtml: What constraint in relational database management ensures that a Foreign Key value must correspond to a valid Primary Key in the referenced parent table?
tcat-cs-318.explainHtml: Referential integrity mandates that every non-null foreign key attribute must match an existing primary key value in the related target relation.

tcat-cs-319.qHtml: What relational normalization requirement elevates a relational table from First Normal Form (1NF) to Second Normal Form (2NF)?
optionsHtml: Elimination of all partial functional dependencies on any composite candidate key
Removal of repeating groups and ensuring atomic attribute values
Ensuring every determinant is a superkey
tcat-cs-319.explainHtml: Second Normal Form (2NF) requires 1NF plus the complete absence of partial functional dependencies (non-prime attributes must depend on the whole candidate key).

tcat-cs-320.qHtml: What is the key functional difference between the WHERE clause and the HAVING clause in an SQL query?
optionsHtml: WHERE filters individual rows prior to grouping, while HAVING filters aggregated group results after GROUP BY
WHERE can only be used with numeric datatypes
HAVING is applied before table joins
Both clauses are completely interchangeable synonyms in standard SQL
tcat-cs-320.explainHtml: WHERE acts on individual tuples prior to aggregation; HAVING acts on grouped summaries produced by aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG) after GROUP BY.

tcat-cs-321.qHtml: In the ACID properties of database transactions, what does the "A" (Atomicity) guarantee?
optionsHtml: All operations within the transaction succeed completely, or the entire transaction is rolled back with zero modifications
Transactions execute in complete isolation from concurrent transactions
Committed data persists permanently even after power failure
Data strictly satisfies all integrity schema constraints
tcat-cs-321.explainHtml: Atomicity ensures that a transaction is an indivisible "all-or-nothing" unit of work: if any sub-operation fails, the entire transaction is aborted and rolled back.

tcat-cs-322.qHtml: In relational algebra, what is the result of applying the natural join (⋈) between relations R(A, B) and S(B, C)?
optionsHtml: A relation T(A, B, C) formed by equi-joining R and S on their common attribute B and projecting out duplicate B columns
The Cartesian product of R and S without any equality match
The union of rows present in R or S
The set difference containing tuples in R but not in S
tcat-cs-322.explainHtml: A natural join performs an equi-join on all identically named common attributes (here attribute B) and automatically eliminates the redundant duplicate column.

tcat-cs-323.qHtml: What condition defines Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) strictly beyond Third Normal Form (3NF)?
optionsHtml: For every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y, the determinant X must be a superkey
Every attribute must be part of a candidate key
No multi-valued dependencies may exist in any relation
All join dependencies must be implied by candidate keys
tcat-cs-323.explainHtml: BCNF is a stricter version of 3NF: for every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y, X must strictly be a superkey (eliminates candidate key overlaps).

tcat-cs-324.qHtml: In database indexing, why are B+ Trees preferred over standard Binary Search Trees for disk-based relational database indices?
optionsHtml: High fan-out (branching factor) minimizes disk I/O seek operations, and leaf nodes are linked sequentially for efficient range scans
B+ Trees occupy zero memory in RAM
B+ Trees store full table records inside all interior routing nodes
B+ Trees eliminate the need for write-ahead logging
tcat-cs-324.explainHtml: B+ Trees have a high branching factor, keeping tree he low (typically 3-4 levels) to minimize costly disk block seeks, and their leaf chain allows rapid linear range scans.

tcat-cs-325.qHtml: How does Strict Two-Phase Locking (Strict 2PL) prevent cascading transaction rollbacks (cascading aborts) in concurrent DBMS execution?
optionsHtml: By holding all exclusive write locks until the transaction explicitly commits or aborts
By acquiring locks only after releasing previous shared locks
By executing all transactions in strict single-threaded serial order
By automatically converting write locks to shared locks during the shrinking phase
tcat-cs-325.explainHtml: Strict 2PL mandates that all exclusive (write) locks acquired during the growing phase must be retained until final commit or rollback, preventing other transactions from reading uncommitted dirty data.

tcat-cs-326.qHtml: How many distinct states or values can be represented by an 8-bit unsigned byte?
tcat-cs-326.explainHtml: An n-bit binary sequence represents 2n unique values. For 8 bits, 28 = 256 unique combinations, ranging from 0 to 255.

tcat-cs-327.qHtml: What is the hexadecimal representation of the decimal integer 255?
tcat-cs-327.explainHtml: 255 in binary is 1111 1111_2. Each group of 4 bits corresponds to F in hexadecimal, yielding 0xFF.

tcat-cs-328.qHtml: Which component of the Central Processing Unit directs the flow of signals and coordinates hardware operations according to program instructions?
tcat-cs-328.explainHtml: The Control Unit fetches, decodes, and orchestrates the execution of instructions, routing control signals across the CPU datapath.

tcat-cs-329.qHtml: Which computer storage medium retains its stored data even when external electric power is disconnected?
tcat-cs-329.explainHtml: ROM is non-volatile solid-state memory that preserves its firmware/bootloader instructions in the absence of power.

tcat-cs-330.qHtml: What standard character encoding system originally utilized 7 bits to encode 128 characters including English letters and control codes?
tcat-cs-330.explainHtml: Standard ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange) uses 7 bits per character, supporting 27 = 128 codes.

tcat-cs-331.qHtml: In two's complement binary arithmetic with an 8-bit signed integer representation, what is the binary code for decimal -1?
tcat-cs-331.explainHtml: +1 is 00000001. Inverting all bits gives 11111110; adding 1 yields 11111111, which equals -1 in two's complement.

tcat-cs-332.qHtml: What is the principal operational distinction between Static RAM (SRAM) and Dynamic RAM (DRAM)?
optionsHtml: SRAM utilizes flip-flop latches and requires no periodic refreshing, whereas DRAM utilizes capacitive charges requiring periodic refresh cycles
DRAM is significantly faster than SRAM
SRAM is non-volatile while DRAM is volatile
DRAM is utilized for L1 processor cache while SRAM is used for main memory
tcat-cs-332.explainHtml: SRAM stores bits using transistor flip-flops (faster, no refresh), while DRAM stores bits in tiny capacitors that leak charge and require periodic refreshing.

tcat-cs-333.qHtml: During the instruction machine cycle, what specific hardware register holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched?
tcat-cs-333.explainHtml: The Program Counter (PC) stores the sequential memory address of the next instruction to be fetched from memory into the CPU.

tcat-cs-334.qHtml: In the IEEE 754 single-precision (32-bit) floating-point format, how are the 32 bits allocated across sign, exponent, and fraction?
optionsHtml: 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits, 23 fraction (mantissa) bits
1 sign bit, 11 exponent bits, 20 fraction bits
2 sign bits, 6 exponent bits, 24 fraction bits
1 sign bit, 7 exponent bits, 24 fraction bits
tcat-cs-334.explainHtml: IEEE 754 standard 32-bit float allocates bit 31 to sign, bits 30-23 (8 bits) to biased exponent, and bits 22-0 (23 bits) to mantissa/fraction.

tcat-cs-335.qHtml: What structural feature fundamentally distinguishes Harvard computer architecture from von Neumann architecture?
optionsHtml: Harvard architecture maintains physically segregated memory and bus pathways for instructions and data, preventing von Neumann bottlenecks
Von Neumann architecture uses separate instruction and data buses
Harvard architecture does not possess an ALU
Von Neumann architecture cannot execute conditional jumps
tcat-cs-335.explainHtml: Harvard architecture features separate address/data buses for instruction code and data memory, permitting simultaneous instruction fetching and data access.

tcat-cs-336.qHtml: How does a direct-mapped cache determine whether a requested memory address results in a cache hit or cache miss?
optionsHtml: Extracts the index bits to locate the cache line, then compares the address tag with the stored tag bit in that line alongside the valid bit
Searches all cache lines simultaneously using parallel associative comparisons
Performs a binary search through RAM
Executes a software interrupt to poll the BIOS
tcat-cs-336.explainHtml: In direct-mapped cache, the memory address is split into Tag, Index, and Offset. The index indexes the unique line, and if Valid==1 and Tag matches, a hit occurs.

tcat-cs-337.qHtml: What is the purpose of the Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) in modern virtual memory management units (MMU)?
optionsHtml: Acts as a high-speed hardware associative cache for recent virtual-to-physical page table address translations, mitigating page table walk latency
Buffers disk writes before committing to mechanical sectors
Translates source code directly into machine binary at runtime
Manages interrupt priorities between USB and Ethernet controllers
tcat-cs-337.explainHtml: The TLB caches recent virtual page number to physical frame number mappings, avoiding multi-level page table traversals in main memory on every memory access.

tcat-cs-338.qHtml: In superscalar pipelined processors, how does out-of-order execution with Tomasulo's algorithm eliminate write-after-write (WAW) and write-after-read (WAR) false data hazards?
optionsHtml: By register renaming using reservation stations and reorder buffers
By inserting stall bubbles until all previous instructions retire
By flushing the entire instruction pipeline upon every branch
tcat-cs-338.explainHtml: Tomasulo's algorithm employs dynamic register renaming via reservation stations and tags, converting architectural registers to temporary tags to dissolve WAR and WAW false dependencies.

tcat-cs-339.qHtml: In C++, which keyword is used to declare a variable whose value cannot be modified after initial assignment?
tcat-cs-339.explainHtml: The `const` qualifier enforces read-only immutability on a variable after initialization, causing compiler errors if modified.

tcat-cs-340.qHtml: Which C++ header file must be included to use standard input and output streams like std::cin and std::cout?
tcat-cs-340.explainHtml: <iostream> contains declarations for the standard basic I/O stream objects including cin, cout, cerr, and clog.

tcat-cs-341.qHtml: Which loop construct in C++ is guaranteed to execute its block of code at least once before testing the loop termination condition?
tcat-cs-341.explainHtml: A `do-while` loop evaluates its condition at the bottom of the loop body, guaranteeing at least one execution.

tcat-cs-342.qHtml: In C++, what operator is used to obtain the memory address of an existing variable?
tcat-cs-342.explainHtml: The unary ampersand `&` is the address-of operator, returning the memory address where the operand resides.

tcat-cs-343.explainHtml: The prefix increment `++x` increments x from 5 to 6 before evaluation; then 6 * 2 = 12.

tcat-cs-344.qHtml: In C++ Object-Oriented Programming, what mechanism enables a derived class to provide a specific implementation of a method declared in its base class?
tcat-cs-344.explainHtml: Declaring a method as `virtual` in a base class allows a derived class to override it, enabling dynamic polymorphism via base class pointers.

tcat-cs-345.qHtml: What happens when dynamic memory allocated with `new int[50]` in C++ is deallocated using `delete p` instead of `delete[] p`?
optionsHtml: Undefined behavior and potential memory leaks or heap corruption occur
The compiler automatically detects it and frees the full array
A compile-time syntax error is thrown
Only the last element is deleted safely
tcat-cs-345.explainHtml: Mismatched deallocation (`delete` on an array allocated with `new[]`) results in undefined behavior and fails to invoke destructors on array elements.

tcat-cs-346.qHtml: In C++, what is the difference between passing an argument by value versus passing by reference (`int& x`)?
optionsHtml: Pass by value creates a local copy, whereas pass by reference allows direct modification of the original argument without copying
Pass by reference makes a deep copy of the variable
Pass by value is strictly faster for large user-defined structs
Pass by reference allocates new memory on the heap
tcat-cs-346.explainHtml: Pass-by-value duplicates data in the function frame; pass-by-reference binds an alias to the caller's object, avoiding copy overhead and allowing in-place edits.

tcat-cs-347.qHtml: What is the function of a destructor in a C++ class, and how is it named?
optionsHtml: Cleans up resources upon object destruction; named with a tilde followed by the class name (~ClassName)
Allocates dynamic memory; named with an exclamation mark (!ClassName)
tcat-cs-347.explainHtml: A destructor is invoked when an object goes out of scope or is deleted, releasing allocated resources; its identifier is `~ClassName()`.

tcat-cs-348.qHtml: What is the purpose of the "vptr" and "vtable" in C++ implementations of runtime polymorphism?
optionsHtml: The vtable is an array of function pointers per polymorphic class, and each object contains a vptr pointing to its class's vtable for dynamic dispatch
They manage garbage collection in heap memory
They convert virtual member functions into inline assembly
They prevent classes from being inherited by subclasses
tcat-cs-348.explainHtml: When virtual functions are used, the compiler generates a virtual method table (vtable) and injects a hidden pointer (vptr) in each object instance for late binding at runtime.

tcat-cs-349.qHtml: What fundamental design principle does the RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) idiom embody in modern C++?
optionsHtml: Resource lifetime is bound to the deterministic scope lifetime of stack-allocated objects whose destructors guarantee automatic resource release
All variables must be allocated dynamically using raw pointers
Constructors must never throw exceptions under any condition
Classes must always inherit from an abstract base interface
tcat-cs-349.explainHtml: RAII binds resource management (memory, file handles, mutex locks) to object lifetime, ensuring deterministic destruction and exception-safe cleanup when the stack frame unwinds.

tcat-cs-350.qHtml: What distinguishes `std::unique_ptr` from `std::shared_ptr` in modern C++ smart pointer management?
optionsHtml: unique_ptr maintains exclusive single ownership with zero reference counting overhead, whereas shared_ptr uses reference counting for shared ownership
unique_ptr allows multiple aliases while shared_ptr does not
shared_ptr cannot be used with custom deleters
unique_ptr stores objects on the stack while shared_ptr allocates them on disk
tcat-cs-350.explainHtml: `std::unique_ptr` owns and manages another object through a pointer and disposes of that object when the unique_ptr goes out of scope (move-only, non-copyable).

tcat-cs-351.qHtml: In C++, why must a base class have a `virtual` destructor if derived class objects are deleted through a base class pointer?
optionsHtml: To ensure the derived class destructor is invoked, preventing memory leaks and incomplete object destruction
To allow the base class to be instantiated as an abstract class
To prevent the derived class from defining its own destructor
To speed up compile times during static linking
tcat-cs-351.explainHtml: Deleting a derived instance through a base pointer without a virtual destructor causes undefined behavior; the derived destructor is never invoked.

tcat-cs-352.qHtml: Which linear data structure operates strictly on a Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) order of element retrieval?
tcat-cs-352.explainHtml: A stack follows the LIFO principle: the most recently pushed element is the first one popped.

tcat-cs-353.qHtml: What is the time complexity of accessing an arbitrary element in a contiguous 1D array given its integer index?
optionsHtml: O(n2) quadratic time
tcat-cs-353.explainHtml: Array elements reside in contiguous memory; accessing index `i` is computed via `base_address + i * element_size` in O(1) time.

tcat-cs-354.qHtml: Which data structure operates on a First-In, First-Out (FIFO) principle, where elements are enqueued at the rear and dequeued from the front?
tcat-cs-354.explainHtml: A queue enforces First-In, First-Out (FIFO) ordering for processing items in chronological arrival order.

tcat-cs-355.qHtml: What is the prerequisite condition for executing a Binary Search algorithm on a 1D array?
optionsHtml: The array elements must be sorted
The array size must be a power of two
All elements must be positive integers
The array must be implemented as a linked list
tcat-cs-355.explainHtml: Binary search repeatedly divides the search interval in half, requiring that elements are sorted in monotonic order.

tcat-cs-356.qHtml: What is the primary operational advantage of a singly linked list over a standard static array?
optionsHtml: Dynamic size and efficient O(1) insertion/deletion at known node positions without shifting trailing elements
Constant-time random access to any element by index
Lower memory usage per element than arrays
Better cache spatial locality during sequential scans
tcat-cs-356.explainHtml: Linked lists allow nodes to be allocated dynamically anywhere in memory, permitting insertion/removal without reallocating or shifting neighboring data.

tcat-cs-357.qHtml: In a complete binary tree containing n nodes, what is the theoretical maximum he (number of levels) of the tree?
tcat-cs-357.explainHtml: Because a complete binary tree fills every level except possibly the last, its he is tightly bounded by floor(log2(n)).

tcat-cs-358.qHtml: What is the average-case time complexity of the QuickSort algorithm when sorting an array of n distinct elements?
optionsHtml: O(n2)
tcat-cs-358.explainHtml: QuickSort divides the problem into balanced subproblems around a pivot on average, achieving an average runtime of O(n log n).

tcat-cs-359.qHtml: What tree traversal order visits nodes in the sequence: Left Subtree → Root Node → R Subtree?
tcat-cs-359.explainHtml: In-order traversal visits the left subtree, processes the root, and then visits the r subtree, producing sorted output in a Binary Search Tree.

tcat-cs-360.qHtml: What self-balancing invariant must be satisfied by every node in an AVL tree to maintain O(log n) search time complexity?
optionsHtml: The absolute difference between the heights of the left and r subtrees (balance factor) cannot exceed 1
Every node must be colored either red or black
The left child must always hold an even key and the r child an odd key
Every leaf node must reside at the exact same depth
tcat-cs-360.explainHtml: An AVL tree enforces that for every node, Balance Factor = |he(left) - he(r)| <= 1; any violation triggers tree rotations.

tcat-cs-361.qHtml: How does open addressing with quadratic probing resolve hash collisions in a hash table?
optionsHtml: Probes subsequent indices using a quadratic polynomial function of the attempt number: h(k, i) = (h(k) + c1*i + c2*i2) mod m
Chains colliding keys into a linked list at the same bucket index
Discards the old key and overwrites it with the new key
Allocates a second separate hash table on disk
tcat-cs-361.explainHtml: Quadratic probing calculates probe locations via a quadratic function of the probe count i, reducing the primary clustering seen in linear probing.

tcat-cs-362.qHtml: In a standard Min-Heap priority queue implemented via a 0-indexed array, what is the array index of the parent of a node located at index i (where i > 0)?
tcat-cs-362.explainHtml: For a 0-indexed binary heap array: parent(i) = floor((i - 1) / 2), left_child(i) = 2i + 1, and right_child(i) = 2i + 2.

tcat-cs-363.qHtml: What is the worst-case time complexity of searching for a key in an unbalanced Binary Search Tree (BST) containing n nodes?
tcat-cs-363.explainHtml: If keys are inserted in monotonic sorted order, an unbalanced BST degenerates into a linear linked list of he n, making search O(n).

tcat-cs-364.qHtml: How does Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm efficiently select the next unvisited vertex with minimal tentative distance?
optionsHtml: By utilizing a min-priority queue (min-heap) to extract the minimum distance vertex in O(log V) time
By performing a depth-first search across all possible graph paths
By computing the matrix inverse of the adjacency matrix
By sorting all graph edges globally using Kruskal's rule
tcat-cs-364.explainHtml: Using a min-heap allows Dijkstra's algorithm to extract the unvisited vertex with the smallest distance in O(log V), yielding O((V + E) log V) total time.

tcat-cs-365.qHtml: Which two-input logic gate produces a HIGH (1) output ONLY when BOTH of its inputs are HIGH (1)?
tcat-cs-365.explainHtml: An AND gate outputs 1 if and only if all of its inputs are 1; otherwise its output is 0.

tcat-cs-366.qHtml: What is the output of an inverter (NOT gate) when its digital input is 0?
tcat-cs-366.explainHtml: A NOT gate performs logical negation, inverting input 0 into output 1.

tcat-cs-367.qHtml: According to Boolean algebra laws, what does the expression `A + 0` simplify to?
tcat-cs-367.explainHtml: Under the Identity Law of Boolean OR operations, A + 0 = A.

tcat-cs-368.qHtml: Which pair of logic gates are classified as "Universal Gates" because any Boolean logic circuit can be constructed solely from them?
tcat-cs-368.explainHtml: NAND and NOR gates are universal gates; any arbitrary combinational logic circuit can be synthesized using either gate alone.

tcat-cs-369.qHtml: State De Morgan's First Theorem in Boolean algebra:
tcat-cs-369.explainHtml: De Morgan's theorem states that the complement of a product is equal to the sum of the complements: (A . B)' = A' + B'.

tcat-cs-370.qHtml: What is the Boolean expression for the output of an Exclusive-OR (XOR) gate with inputs A and B?
tcat-cs-370.explainHtml: The XOR function outputs 1 when the inputs differ, expressed in sum-of-products as A'B + AB'.

tcat-cs-371.qHtml: Simplify the Boolean expression `A + A'B` using Boolean algebraic theorems:
tcat-cs-371.explainHtml: By the absorption/distributive law: A + A'B = (A + A')(A + B) = (1)(A + B) = A + B.

tcat-cs-372.qHtml: In digital arithmetic circuits, how many half-adders and OR gates are required to construct a single 1-bit Full-Adder?
optionsHtml: Two half-adders and one OR gate
One half-adder and two OR gates
Three half-adders and zero OR gates
Four half-adders and one AND gate
tcat-cs-372.explainHtml: A full-adder sums three 1-bit inputs (A, B, Cin) using 2 half-adders and 1 OR gate to combine the carry-out signals.

tcat-cs-373.qHtml: In a 4-variable Karnaugh Map (K-map), how many adjacent minterm cells must be grouped together to eliminate three Boolean variables from a product term?
tcat-cs-373.explainHtml: In a K-map, grouping 2k adjacent cells eliminates k variables. To eliminate 3 variables, 23 = 8 cells (an octet) must be combined.

tcat-cs-374.qHtml: What is the characteristic equation of an edge-triggered J-K Flip-Flop describing its next state Q(next)?
tcat-cs-374.explainHtml: The next-state equation for a J-K flip-flop is Q(next) = J Q' + K' Q. When J=K=1, Q(next) toggles to Q'.

tcat-cs-375.qHtml: What operational feature distinguishes a Mealy finite state machine (FSM) from a Moore machine in sequential circuit design?
optionsHtml: In a Mealy machine, outputs depend on both the current state and current inputs; in a Moore machine, outputs depend solely on the current state
In a Moore machine, outputs depend on both inputs and state
Mealy machines require no clock signal
Moore machines cannot be synthesized with flip-flops
tcat-cs-375.explainHtml: A Mealy machine's outputs are functions of current state AND primary inputs, often reacting a cycle faster than a Moore machine whose outputs depend solely on state.

tcat-cs-376.qHtml: How does a Carry-Lookahead Adder (CLA) overcome the latency limitations of a standard ripple-carry adder?
optionsHtml: Generates carry signals in parallel using Generate (G = A.B) and Propagate (P = A⊕B) logic functions, eliminating serial carry ripple delays
Uses software prediction to guess carry bits
Converts binary numbers into analog voltages
Discards the carry bit on all odd clock cycles
tcat-cs-376.explainHtml: CLA calculates carries ahead of time using Pi and Gi signals across all stages in O(1) logic depth, bypassing O(n) ripple propagation.

tcat-cs-377.qHtml: What transmission medium uses pulses of l guided through thin silica glass fibers to achieve high-bandwidth data transmission?
tcat-cs-377.explainHtml: Fiber optic cables transmit digital data signals as l pulses through core glass or plastic filaments using total internal reflection.

tcat-cs-378.qHtml: Which networking topology connects all host nodes to a single central hub or switch via dedicated point-to-point links?
tcat-cs-378.explainHtml: In a star topology, each network device connects via a dedicated point-to-point link directly to a central multiport switch or hub.

tcat-cs-379.qHtml: What network protocol dynamically translates human-readable domain names (e.g., www.google.com) into numerical IP addresses?
tcat-cs-379.explainHtml: DNS translates human-friendly domain names into machine-routable numerical IP addresses.

tcat-cs-380.qHtml: What is the length of an IPv4 address in bits and how is it typically formatted?
optionsHtml: 32 bits formatted as 4 decimal octets separated by dots
tcat-cs-380.explainHtml: IPv4 addresses are 32-bit integers written in dotted-decimal notation as four 8-bit octets (e.g., 192.168.1.1).

tcat-cs-381.qHtml: What is the primary operational distinction between TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) and UDP (User Datagram Protocol)?
optionsHtml: TCP is connection-oriented, reliable, and provides flow/congestion control; UDP is connectionless, lightwe, and does not guarantee packet delivery
UDP is connection-oriented while TCP is connectionless
TCP operates at the Network layer while UDP operates at the Transport layer
UDP encrypts all payload packets natively while TCP transmits plaintext
tcat-cs-381.explainHtml: TCP provides reliable, ordered, error-checked stream delivery with three-way handshaking; UDP is a lightwe, connectionless protocol with minimal overhead for real-time traffic.

tcat-cs-382.qHtml: What protocol is responsible for mapping a known Network Layer IP address to a physical Data Link Layer MAC address on a local area network?
tcat-cs-382.explainHtml: ARP broadcasts on the local subnet to resolve a known logical IP address into the physical hardware MAC address of the destination interface.

tcat-cs-383.qHtml: In classless inter-domain routing (CIDR) notation, how many usable host IP addresses are available on a `/26` subnet?
tcat-cs-383.explainHtml: A /26 subnet has 32 - 26 = 6 host bits. Total addresses = 26 = 64. Subtracting 2 (network and broadcast addresses) leaves 62 usable host addresses.

tcat-cs-384.qHtml: At which layer of the OSI model do network routers primarily operate to inspect packet headers and make forwarding decisions?
tcat-cs-384.explainHtml: Routers operate at Layer 3 (Network Layer), inspecting destination IP addresses to route packets across disparate networks.

tcat-cs-385.qHtml: What is the sequence of flag packets exchanged during the standard TCP Three-Way Handshake to establish a connection?
tcat-cs-385.explainHtml: TCP connection establishment: Client sends SYN, Server replies with SYN-ACK, and Client completes connection with ACK.

tcat-cs-386.qHtml: How does the TCP congestion control mechanism respond to packet loss detected via three duplicate ACKs under TCP Reno?
optionsHtml: Executes Fast Retransmit, cuts Congestion Window (cwnd) in half, and enters Fast Recovery without resetting cwnd to 1 MSS
Resets cwnd immediately to 1 MSS and restarts Slow Start
Increases cwnd exponentially to saturate the buffer
tcat-cs-386.explainHtml: Three duplicate ACKs trigger Fast Retransmit and Fast Recovery: cwnd is halved (ssthresh = cwnd / 2), avoiding the drastic reset to 1 MSS seen on timeout.

tcat-cs-387.qHtml: What routing metric and algorithm are employed by the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routing protocol?
optionsHtml: Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm operating on link-state cost metrics based on interface bandwidth
Bellman-Ford algorithm operating on hop count
Spanning Tree Protocol operating on MAC addresses
tcat-cs-387.explainHtml: OSPF is an Interior Gateway link-state protocol that builds a complete network topology map and executes Dijkstra's SPF algorithm using interface bandwidth cost.

tcat-cs-388.qHtml: In asymmetric public-key cryptography (e.g., RSA), which key is used to encrypt a message so that only the designated recipient can decrypt it?
optionsHtml: The recipient's public key is used to encrypt, and the recipient's private key decrypts
The sender's private key encrypts, and recipient's public key decrypts
The sender's public key encrypts, and recipient's private key decrypts
A shared symmetric session key generated by the ISP
tcat-cs-388.explainHtml: Confidentiality in public key cryptography: Sender encrypts with Recipient's Public Key; only the Recipient's private key can invert the trapdoor permutation to decrypt.

tcat-cs-389.qHtml: What type of database key uniquely identifies each record/tuple in a relational database table and cannot contain null values?
tcat-cs-389.explainHtml: A Primary Key is a minimal candidate key selected to uniquely identify each row in a relation; entity integrity mandates it cannot be NULL.

tcat-cs-390.qHtml: Which standard SQL command is used to retrieve data from one or more database tables?
tcat-cs-390.explainHtml: The `SELECT` statement is the fundamental DML query command in SQL used to fetch rows and columns from tables.

tcat-cs-391.qHtml: What type of key establishes a relational link between two database tables by referencing the primary key of another table?
tcat-cs-391.explainHtml: A Foreign Key is a field in one table that refers to the Primary Key in another table, enforcing referential integrity.

tcat-cs-392.qHtml: Which SQL clause is used to filter query results based on specific conditional criteria?
tcat-cs-392.explainHtml: The `WHERE` clause filters rows before aggregation, returning only records that satisfy the specified condition.

tcat-cs-393.qHtml: What is the primary goal of Database Normalization in relational database design?
optionsHtml: Eliminate data redundancy and prevent update, insertion, and deletion anomalies
Maximize disk space utilization by compressing strings
Combine all application tables into a single large flat file
Automatically create clustered B-tree indexes for all attributes
tcat-cs-393.explainHtml: Normalization decomposes relations to minimize data duplication, prevent update/insert/delete anomalies, and ensure data integrity.

tcat-cs-394.qHtml: A relational table is in First Normal Form (1NF) if and only if:
optionsHtml: All attributes contain only atomic (indivisible) scalar values and there are no repeating groups
Every non-key attribute is fully functionally dependent on the primary key
It has no foreign key references
tcat-cs-394.explainHtml: 1NF mandates that each column contains only atomic values and there are no multivalued attributes or repeating groups.

tcat-cs-395.qHtml: What is the operational difference between the SQL `WHERE` clause and the `HAVING` clause?
optionsHtml: WHERE filters individual rows prior to grouping, whereas HAVING filters aggregated groups after GROUP BY
HAVING filters individual rows prior to grouping
WHERE can only be used with numeric data types
HAVING cannot be used alongside GROUP BY
tcat-cs-395.explainHtml: `WHERE` applies row-level filters before aggregation; `HAVING` applies filtering conditions to group summaries produced by `GROUP BY`.

tcat-cs-396.qHtml: What type of SQL JOIN returns all matching rows from both tables, plus all unmatched rows from the left table with NULLs filled in for r table attributes?
tcat-cs-396.explainHtml: A `LEFT OUTER JOIN` retains all tuples from the left relation, matching them with r table tuples where the predicate holds or outputting NULLs where no match exists.

tcat-cs-397.qHtml: In the ACID transaction properties of database management systems, what does "Isolation" guarantee?
optionsHtml: Concurrent execution of transactions results in a system state that would be obtained if transactions were executed serially
All or none of the operations in a transaction are committed
Database integrity constraints are never violated
Committed updates survive power outages and system crashes
tcat-cs-397.explainHtml: Isolation ensures that concurrently running transactions cannot see or interfere with each other's intermediate uncommitted states (serializability).

tcat-cs-398.qHtml: What condition defines Third Normal Form (3NF) for a relation already conforming to 2NF?
optionsHtml: Every non-prime attribute is non-transitively dependent on every candidate key (no non-key determines another non-key)
Every determinant is a candidate key (BCNF condition)
No partial functional dependencies exist on a composite key
tcat-cs-398.explainHtml: 3NF requires that the relation is in 2NF and contains no transitive dependencies: for every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y, either X is a superkey or Y is a prime attribute.

tcat-cs-399.qHtml: How does Two-Phase Locking (2PL) guarantee conflict serializability in database concurrency control?
optionsHtml: Transactions must acquire all needed locks during an expanding Growing Phase and may not acquire new locks once any lock is released in the Shrinking Phase
Locks are acquired and released randomly based on CPU availability
Transactions never lock rows, relying entirely on timestamps
Write locks are converted into read locks after every commit
tcat-cs-399.explainHtml: Under 2PL, a transaction cannot request any lock once it has released any lock (Phase 1: Growing/acquiring; Phase 2: Shrinking/releasing), mathematically guaranteeing conflict serializability.

tcat-cs-400.qHtml: What structural property makes a B+ Tree index superior to a standard binary search tree for relational database index storage on block storage devices?
optionsHtml: High fan-out yields a shallow tree depth, minimizing disk I/O, and leaf nodes are linked sequentially for efficient range scans
Binary search trees have higher branching factors
B+ trees store all data records in internal nodes
B+ trees do not require any memory buffering
tcat-cs-400.explainHtml: B+ trees have high branching factor (fanout of hundreds), meaning he is typically 3-4, requiring few disk seeks. Leaves form a linked list, enabling fast sequential range queries.

tcat-cs-401.qHtml: Which component of the Central Processing Unit (CPU) coordinates and synchronizes all hardware operations via control signals?
tcat-cs-401.explainHtml: The Control Unit (CU) directs system operations by decoding instructions and generating control timing signals to the ALU, registers, and memory bus.

tcat-cs-402.qHtml: What is the 8-bit two's complement binary representation of the negative decimal integer -43?
tcat-cs-402.explainHtml: +43 in 8-bit binary is 00101011. One's complement (invert bits) is 11010100. Adding 1 gives the two's complement: 11010101.

tcat-cs-403.qHtml: In the memory hierarchy, which type of semiconductor memory provides the fastest access latency for the processor core?
tcat-cs-403.explainHtml: L1 CPU Cache implemented with static RAM (SRAM) integrated directly onto the processor die exhibits single-cycle access latency (~1 ns).

tcat-cs-404.qHtml: What is the primary function of the Program Counter (PC) register in von Neumann architecture?
optionsHtml: To hold the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched and executed
To store the mathematical output of the ALU
To buffer data read directly from secondary storage
To count the total number of instructions executed since boot
tcat-cs-404.explainHtml: The Program Counter (PC) register stores the memory address of the upcoming instruction in the instruction fetch-decode-execute cycle.

tcat-cs-405.qHtml: Which hardware mechanism allows high-speed peripheral input/output controllers to transfer data blocks directly to and from main RAM without continuous CPU intervention?
tcat-cs-405.explainHtml: DMA bypasses the CPU for bulk memory transfers, allowing disk and network controllers to read or write RAM directly, freeing CPU cycles.

tcat-cs-406.qHtml: In C/C++, what is the value stored in variable x after executing: int x = 17 % 5; ?
tcat-cs-406.explainHtml: The modulus operator (%) computes the integer remainder of division: 17 = 3 * 5 + 2, so 17 % 5 = 2.

tcat-cs-407.qHtml: Which iterative loop construct is guaranteed to execute its code block at least once regardless of whether the loop condition initially evaluates to true or false?
tcat-cs-407.explainHtml: A do-while loop evaluates its exit test condition at the end of the iteration, guaranteeing at least one execution pass.

tcat-cs-408.qHtml: Consider the recursive C function: int f(int n) { if(n \le 1) return 1; return n * f(n - 1); }. What does this function compute for any positive integer n?
optionsHtml: Sum of integers up to n
tcat-cs-408.explainHtml: The recurrence relation f(n) = n * f(n - 1) with base case f(1) = 1 defines the factorial mathematical function n!.

tcat-cs-409.qHtml: What occurs when a recursive function lacks a well-defined terminating base case or the base condition is unreachable?
tcat-cs-409.explainHtml: Unbounded recursion continuously pushes activation stack frames onto the thread runtime call stack until memory is exhausted, throwing a Stack Overflow.

tcat-cs-410.qHtml: What is the runtime output in C when dereferencing an uninitialized dangling pointer pointing to deallocated memory?
optionsHtml: Undefined behavior (potential segmentation fault or memory corruption)
tcat-cs-410.explainHtml: Dereferencing a dangling or uninitialized pointer accesses invalid address space, causing undefined behavior or an immediate SIGSEGV signal.

tcat-cs-411.qHtml: Which abstract data structure operates strictly under the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) access discipline?
tcat-cs-411.explainHtml: A stack restricts insertion and deletion to one end (the top), adhering strictly to Last-In, First-Out (LIFO).

tcat-cs-412.qHtml: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search when executed on a sorted array containing n elements?
tcat-cs-412.explainHtml: Binary search halves the search interval in every iteration, executing in O(log n) comparisons in both average and worst cases.

tcat-cs-413.qHtml: What is the primary advantage of a singly linked list over a contiguous static array?
optionsHtml: Dynamic size with O(1) constant-time insertion at the head without reallocation
Instantaneous O(1) random index access to arbitrary elements
Zero auxiliary memory overhead for pointer metadata
Superior hardware CPU cache locality during sequential scans
tcat-cs-413.explainHtml: Linked lists allow nodes to be allocated dynamically anywhere in heap memory, enabling O(1) insertion at the front without shifting elements.

tcat-cs-414.qHtml: In a complete binary max-heap implemented as an array where the root is at index 0, what is the array index of the left child of a node stored at index i?
tcat-cs-414.explainHtml: For zero-based array representation of a binary heap, the left child of node i is at 2*i + 1, and the r child is at 2*i + 2.

tcat-cs-415.qHtml: What is the average-case and worst-case time complexity of standard Quicksort algorithm using a naive fixed pivot strategy?
optionsHtml: Average O(n log n), Worst-case O(n2)
Average O(n), Worst-case O(n log n)
Average O(n log n), Worst-case O(n log n)
Average O(n2), Worst-case O(n3)
tcat-cs-415.explainHtml: Quicksort divides elements around a pivot; balanced partitions yield O(n log n) average time, but already sorted data with a fixed endpoint pivot degrades to O(n2).

tcat-cs-416.qHtml: Which basic digital logic gate outputs logic 1 (HIGH) if and only if all of its input terminals are at logic 1?
tcat-cs-416.explainHtml: An AND gate produces a HIGH output solely when every input is asserted HIGH (1).

tcat-cs-417.qHtml: According to Boolean algebra laws, what is the simplified form of the expression A + A'*B ?
tcat-cs-417.explainHtml: By the absorption/redundancy law: A + A'*B = (A + A')(A + B) = (1)(A + B) = A + B.

tcat-cs-418.qHtml: According to De Morgan's second theorem, the complement of a sum of variables (A + B)' is algebraically equivalent to:
tcat-cs-418.explainHtml: De Morgan's Law states that the NOR operation is dual to AND with inverted inputs: (A + B)' = A' * B'.

tcat-cs-419.qHtml: Which two logic gates are classified as "Universal Gates" because any Boolean logic circuit can be synthesized exclusively using either one?
tcat-cs-419.explainHtml: NAND and NOR are universal gates capable of implementing NOT, AND, OR, XOR, and all combinational logic functions without other gate types.

tcat-cs-420.qHtml: How many 2-to-1 multiplexers (MUX) are required to construct a 4-to-1 multiplexer circuit?
tcat-cs-420.explainHtml: Two 2-to-1 MUXes select between four inputs in the first stage using select line s0, and one 2-to-1 MUX in the second stage selects between their outputs using select line s1, requiring 3 total.

tcat-cs-421.qHtml: What is the length in bits of a standard IPv4 network address?
tcat-cs-421.explainHtml: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long (4 octets), whereas IPv6 addresses are 128 bits in length.

tcat-cs-422.qHtml: Which protocol translates human-readable domain names (such as uettaxila.edu.pk) into numerical IP addresses?
tcat-cs-422.explainHtml: DNS (Domain Name System) operates as the Internet's directory, resolving alphanumeric domain names into IP addresses.

tcat-cs-423.qHtml: At which layer of the OSI 7-layer reference model do network routers operate to determine optimal packet forwarding paths?
tcat-cs-423.explainHtml: Routers operate at the Network Layer (Layer 3), using logical IP addressing and routing protocols to route packets across subnets.

tcat-cs-424.qHtml: Which transmission protocol guarantees reliable, ordered, and error-checked delivery of a stream of octets between networked applications?
tcat-cs-424.explainHtml: TCP establishes connection-oriented sessions with three-way handshakes, sequence tracking, acknowledgments, and retransmissions, ensuring reliable delivery.

tcat-cs-425.qHtml: In the TCP three-way handshake connection establishment, what is the exact sequence of control flag packets transmitted between client and server?
tcat-cs-425.explainHtml: TCP initiates connection by client sending SYN, server responding with SYN-ACK, and client concluding setup with ACK.

tcat-cs-426.qHtml: Which SQL statement is used to retrieve data records from a relational database table?
tcat-cs-426.explainHtml: The SQL SELECT statement queries and retrieves specified columns or rows from database tables.

tcat-cs-427.qHtml: An attribute or minimal set of attributes that uniquely identifies every tuple (record) within a relational table is called the:
tcat-cs-427.explainHtml: A primary key uniquely identifies each entity instance or tuple in a relation, enforcing entity integrity (no nulls and no duplicate keys).

tcat-cs-428.qHtml: In relational database theory, Second Normal Form (2NF) mandates that the table is in 1NF and that:
optionsHtml: Every non-key attribute is fully functionally dependent on the entire primary key (no partial dependencies)
There are no transitive dependencies between non-key attributes
All attributes contain multi-valued repeating groups
Foreign keys must reference unique candidate keys in different databases
tcat-cs-428.explainHtml: 2NF eliminates partial functional dependencies; every non-prime attribute must depend on the whole candidate key, not a proper subset.

tcat-cs-429.qHtml: What is the function of a FOREIGN KEY constraint in a relational database management system?
optionsHtml: To enforce referential integrity between two associated tables
To accelerate indexing of non-unique strings
To prevent the table from exceeding physical disk storage limits
To automatically encrypt sensitive biometric data
tcat-cs-429.explainHtml: A foreign key references the primary key of another table, ensuring referential integrity by preventing orphaned rows and invalid cross-references.

tcat-cs-430.qHtml: In the ACID transaction processing model, which property ensures that once a database transaction commits, its state changes survive system crashes or power failures?
tcat-cs-430.explainHtml: Durability guarantees that committed transaction modifications are recorded permanently in non-volatile write-ahead logging storage and persist across system failures.

tcat-bio-1.qHtml: Which organelle is universally referred to as the "powerhouse of the cell" due to ATP generation via oxidative phosphorylation?
tcat-bio-1.explainHtml: Mitochondria produce the bulk of cellular ATP through the citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation on the inner mitochondrial cristae.

tcat-bio-2.qHtml: In plant cells, where do the l-dependent reactions of photosynthesis specifically take place?
tcat-bio-2.explainHtml: L-dependent reactions occur across the thylakoid membranes where chlorophyll pigments, photosystems I and II, and ATP synthase reside.

tcat-bio-3.qHtml: What is the net yield of ATP molecules generated per molecule of glucose during anaerobic glycolysis in the cytoplasm?
tcat-bio-3.explainHtml: Glycolysis consumes 2 ATP and produces 4 ATP, yielding a net gain of exactly 2 ATP molecules per glucose.

tcat-bio-4.qHtml: Which organelle contains acid hydrolases responsible for intracellular digestion and autolysis of worn-out organelles?
tcat-bio-4.explainHtml: Lysosomes contain acidic hydrolytic enzymes (optimal pH ~4.5-5.0) for degrading biological polymers and cellular debris.

tcat-bio-5.qHtml: What is the primary enzyme responsible for carbon fixation in the stroma during the Calvin Cycle (l-independent reactions)?
tcat-bio-5.explainHtml: RuBisCO catalyzes the addition of CO2 to ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP) to form two molecules of 3-phosphoglycerate (3-PGA).

tcat-bio-6.qHtml: How does a competitive enzyme inhibitor alter the kinetic parameters Vmax and Km of an enzymatic reaction?
optionsHtml: Km increases while Vmax remains unchanged
Vmax decreases while Km remains unchanged
Both Vmax and Km decrease proportionally
tcat-bio-6.explainHtml: Competitive inhibitors bind to the active site; adding excess substrate overcomes the inhibitor (Vmax unchanged), but requires higher substrate concentration (Km increases).

tcat-bio-7.qHtml: During the mitochondrial electron transport chain, what serves as the ultimate terminal electron acceptor?
tcat-bio-7.explainHtml: Electrons flowing through complex IV are transferred to molecular oxygen (O2), which combines with protons to form water.

tcat-bio-8.qHtml: What mechanism drives the transport of sodium and potassium ions across the plasma membrane via the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase pump?
optionsHtml: Primary active transport pumping 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in against their electrochemical gradients using 1 ATP
Facilitated diffusion moving 2 Na⁺ out and 3 K⁺ in down their gradients
Secondary active symport moving Na⁺ and K⁺ in the same direction
Passive osmosis governed by extracellular osmolarity
tcat-bio-8.explainHtml: The Na+/K \pm ATPase uses 1 ATP molecule to export 3 Na+ ions and import 2 K+ ions against their concentration gradients.

tcat-bio-9.qHtml: Peter Mitchell's chemiosmotic hypothesis explains ATP synthesis by demonstrating that:
optionsHtml: Proton pumping across the inner mitochondrial membrane establishes an electrochemical proton gradient (pmf) that drives ATP synthase
Substrate-level phosphorylation directly transfers high-energy phosphate from acetyl-CoA
Electron transfer complexes mechanically twist the mitochondrial matrix proteins
Water splitting in the matrix generates pressurized molecular hydrogen
tcat-bio-9.explainHtml: Mitchell's chemiosmotic hypothesis demonstrated that the proton motive force across the inner membrane powers rotational catalysis in ATP synthase (F₀F₁).

tcat-bio-10.qHtml: How many turns of the Calvin cycle, and how many net molecules of CO₂, ATP, and NADPH are required to synthesize one net molecule of Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆)?
tcat-bio-10.explainHtml: Synthesizing one glucose requires fixing 6 CO2 molecules over 6 turns, consuming 18 ATP and 12 NADPH.

tcat-bio-11.qHtml: Which mitochondrial matrix intermediate combines with oxaloacetate (4C) to initiate the Krebs citric acid cycle?
tcat-bio-11.explainHtml: Citrate synthase condenses 2-carbon Acetyl-CoA with 4-carbon Oxaloacetate to produce 6-carbon Citric Acid (Citrate).

tcat-bio-12.qHtml: In cyclic photophosphorylation in chloroplasts, which photosystem operates independently and what product is uniquely synthesized without NADPH production?
optionsHtml: Photosystem I (P700) alone operates, synthesizing exclusively ATP
Photosystem II (P680) alone operates, synthesizing exclusively NADPH
Both PSI and PSII operate together, synthesizing ATP and O₂
Photosystem II operates, synthesizing Glucose directly
tcat-bio-12.explainHtml: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves only PSI (P700); excited electrons return via ferredoxin and cytochrome b6f to PSI, generating ATP without reducing NADP+.

tcat-bio-13.qHtml: Which covalent linkage joins individual amino acid monomers together to form a polypeptide chain?
tcat-bio-13.explainHtml: A peptide bond forms between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another via a condensation (dehydration) reaction.

tcat-bio-14.qHtml: Which nitrogenous base is present in RNA nucleotides but replaced by Thymine in DNA?
tcat-bio-14.explainHtml: RNA contains Uracil (U) instead of Thymine (T); both base-pair with Adenine (A).

tcat-bio-15.qHtml: What is the primary storage polysaccharide found in animal liver and skeletal muscle cells?
tcat-bio-15.explainHtml: Glycogen is a highly branched polymer of glucose used by animals for rapid energy storage and glucose mobilization.

tcat-bio-16.qHtml: What chemical components combine to form a single triglyceride lipid molecule?
optionsHtml: One glycerol molecule and three fatty acid chains
Three glycerol molecules and one fatty acid chain
One sphingosine and two phosphate groups
One glucose and three amino acid residues
tcat-bio-16.explainHtml: A triglyceride consists of a 3-carbon glycerol backbone esterified to three fatty acid tails.

tcat-bio-17.qHtml: What type of chemical bond stabilizes the secondary structure of proteins (such as α-helices and β-pleated sheets)?
optionsHtml: Hydrogen bonds between backbone carbonyl oxygens and amide hydrogens
Disulfide bridges between cysteine side chains
Hydrophobic interactions between non-polar aliphatic groups
Ionic salt bridges between aspartate and lysine
tcat-bio-17.explainHtml: Secondary structure (α-helix and β-sheet) is maintained strictly by repetitive hydrogen bonding along the peptide backbone.

tcat-bio-18.qHtml: Which pair of nitrogenous bases are two-ringed Purines?
tcat-bio-18.explainHtml: Adenine (A) and Guanine (G) are purines with a double-ring structure (pyrimidine fused to imidazole).

tcat-bio-19.qHtml: Why cannot human digestive enzymes hydrolyze dietary cellulose, despite it being composed entirely of glucose subunits?
optionsHtml: Cellulose contains β-1,4-glycosidic linkages which humans lack cellulase enzymes to cleave
Cellulose contains α-1,4-glycosidic bonds that are shielded by lipids
Cellulose is composed of L-glucose stereoisomers rather than D-glucose
Cellulose has branched peptide cross-links that inactivate salivary amylase
tcat-bio-19.explainHtml: Human amylase only breaks α-1,4 linkages (starch/glycogen); human bodies lack cellulase to hydrolyze β-1,4 glycosidic bonds in cellulose.

tcat-bio-20.qHtml: What structural property makes phospholipids amphipathic molecules capable of forming cell membrane bilayers?
optionsHtml: A hydrophilic polar phosphate head group combined with two hydrophobic non-polar fatty acid tails
Two hydrophilic glycerol backbones linked to a non-polar peptide chain
Equal numbers of positively charged amino and negatively charged carboxyl groups
A cholesterol ring fused covalently to three phosphate ions
tcat-bio-20.explainHtml: Phospholipids have a hydrophilic polar head (phosphate + glycerol) and hydrophobic nonpolar tails, spontaneously forming bilayers in water.

tcat-bio-21.qHtml: In the tertiary structure of globular proteins, which covalent interaction forms the strongest bond between distant amino acid residues?
optionsHtml: Disulfide bond (-S-S-) between two cysteine residues
Hydrogen bond between serine and threonine
Electrostatic interaction between glutamate and arginine
Van der Waals attraction between leucine residues
tcat-bio-21.explainHtml: Disulfide bridges are true covalent bonds formed by oxidation of thiol (-SH) groups on cysteine residues, providing strong structural stability.

tcat-bio-22.qHtml: What is the structural distinction between DNA and RNA pentose sugars at the 2' carbon position?
optionsHtml: Deoxyribose has an -H atom at C-2', while Ribose has an -OH hydroxyl group at C-2'
Ribose lacks an oxygen atom at C-2', while Deoxyribose possesses two -OH groups
Deoxyribose contains 6 carbons (hexose), whereas Ribose contains 5 carbons (pentose)
Ribose has a nitrogenous base attached directly to C-2'
tcat-bio-22.explainHtml: Deoxyribose is 'de-oxygenated' at the 2' position (bearing -H instead of -OH), making DNA chemically less prone to alkaline hydrolysis than RNA.

tcat-bio-23.qHtml: According to Chargaff's rules for double-stranded DNA, if a genomic sample contains 28% Cytosine, what percentage of Adenine does it contain?
tcat-bio-23.explainHtml: In dsDNA, C = G = 28%, so C + G = 56%. The remaining 44% is divided equally between A and T (A = T = 44% / 2 = 22%).

tcat-bio-24.qHtml: What is the characteristic prosthetic group present in Hemoglobin and Myoglobin that binds reversible molecular oxygen?
optionsHtml: Iron-containing Protoporphyrin IX (Heme group with Fe2⁺)
tcat-bio-24.explainHtml: Hemoglobin contains four heme prosthetic groups (iron protoporphyrin IX with Fe2⁺), each capable of binding one O₂ molecule reversibly.

tcat-bio-25.qHtml: Which human heart chamber pumps oxygenated blood directly into the systemic circulation via the Aorta?
tcat-bio-25.explainHtml: The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall and generates high pressure to pump oxygenated blood through the aortic valve into the aorta.

tcat-bio-26.qHtml: What is the functional microscopic filtration unit of the human kidney?
tcat-bio-26.explainHtml: The nephron is the basic structural and functional unit of the kidney, consisting of a renal corpuscle and renal tubule system.

tcat-bio-27.qHtml: Which proteolytic enzyme is secreted by stomach gastric chief cells in an inactive zymogen form and activated by hydrochloric acid (HCl)?
tcat-bio-27.explainHtml: Chief cells secrete inactive pepsinogen, which is converted to active pepsin in the acidic environment (pH 1.5-2.0) created by parietal cell HCl.

tcat-bio-28.qHtml: Which blood type is considered the "Universal Red Blood Cell Donor" because its erythrocytes lack both A and B surface antigens?
tcat-bio-28.explainHtml: Type O negative blood has neither A nor B antigens nor the Rh (D) antigen on RBC membranes, minimizing hemolytic transfusion reaction risks.

tcat-bio-29.qHtml: What physiological event causes the characteristic "lub" (first heart sound, S1)?
optionsHtml: Closure of the atrioventricular (Tricuspid and Mitral/Bicuspid) valves at the onset of ventricular systole
Closure of the semilunar (Aortic and Pulmonary) valves at the end of systole
Rapid passive filling of the ventricles during diastole
Contraction of the papillary muscles during atrial systole
tcat-bio-29.explainHtml: The first heart sound (S1, "lub") is caused by the sudden closure and vibration of the AV valves (mitral and tricuspid) as ventricles contract.

tcat-bio-30.qHtml: What does the Bohr effect describe regarding hemoglobin-oxygen affinity in actively respiring tissues?
optionsHtml: Elevated CO₂ and decreased pH (increased H⁺) reduce hemoglobin's affinity for O₂, promoting oxygen unloading
Increased oxygen partial pressure drives carbon dioxide release from carbamino compounds
Decreased temperature shifts the oxygen dissociation curve to the r
High concentrations of carbon monoxide lock hemoglobin in the relaxed R-state
tcat-bio-30.explainHtml: The Bohr effect explains that lower pH and higher CO2 in metabolically active tissues decrease hemoglobin affinity for O2, releasing oxygen where needed.

tcat-bio-31.qHtml: In the nephron, which segment is primarily responsible for the reabsorption of approximately 65-70% of filtered water, sodium, and 100% of filtered glucose and amino acids?
tcat-bio-31.explainHtml: The PCT has extensive microvilli (brush border) and mitochondria, actively reabsorbing glucose, amino acids, and most electrolytes and water.

tcat-bio-32.qHtml: How is the major fraction (~70%) of carbon dioxide transported in human systemic venous blood?
optionsHtml: As dissolved bicarbonate ions (HCO₃⁻) in blood plasma
Bound directly to hemoglobin as carbaminohemoglobin
As dissolved CO₂ gas bubbles in blood serum
Bound covalently to plasma albumin proteins
tcat-bio-32.explainHtml: Carbonic anhydrase inside RBCs converts CO2 to H2CO3, which dissociates into H+ and HCO3-; HCO3- is then transported in plasma via chloride shift.

tcat-bio-33.qHtml: How does the countercurrent multiplier mechanism in the Loop of Henle establish a hypertonic medullary osmotic gradient?
optionsHtml: The descending limb is permeable to water but impermeable to solutes; the ascending limb actively pumps NaCl out while being impermeable to water
The ascending limb allows water to leave by osmosis; the descending limb actively absorbs urea
Both limbs actively pump glucose and sodium ions simultaneously into the renal cortex
Vasa recta capillaries pump potassium ions into the collecting tubules against concentration gradients
tcat-bio-33.explainHtml: Descending limb loses water (concentrating tubular fluid); ascending limb actively pumps NaCl into the interstitium without water following, creating a gradient up to 1200 mOsm/L.

tcat-bio-34.qHtml: What is the role of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH / Vasopressin) in regulating renal water excretion?
optionsHtml: It stimulates insertion of Aquaporin-2 water channels into the apical membranes of collecting duct principal cells, increasing water reabsorption
It inhibits sodium reabsorption in the ascending loop of Henle, causing diuresis
It constricts the afferent glomerular arteriole to lower GFR to zero
It activates aldosterone secretion directly from the juxtaglomerular apparatus
tcat-bio-34.explainHtml: ADH binds V2 receptors in collecting duct cells, triggering exocytosis of Aquaporin-2 channels to reabsorb water and produce concentrated urine.

tcat-bio-35.qHtml: On a standard clinical Electrocardiogram (ECG/EKG), what electrical event is represented by the QRS complex?
optionsHtml: Atrial repolarization masking the T wave
tcat-bio-35.explainHtml: The QRS complex corresponds to rapid ventricular depolarization; atrial repolarization also occurs simultaneously but is hidden by the large QRS amplitude.

tcat-bio-36.qHtml: Which digestive hormone stimulates the gall bladder to contract and expels pancreatic digestive enzymes into the duodenum in response to fatty chyme?
tcat-bio-36.explainHtml: CCK is secreted by enteroendocrine I cells in the duodenum; it stimulates gallbladder contraction (bile release) and pancreatic acinar enzyme secretion.

tcat-bio-37.qHtml: What phenotypic ratio is expected in the F2 generation of a classic Mendelian monohybrid cross between two heterozygous parents (Aa × Aa) with complete dominance?
tcat-bio-37.explainHtml: In a monohybrid cross (Aa × Aa), genotypes are 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa, producing a 3 dominant : 1 recessive phenotypic ratio.

tcat-bio-38.qHtml: Which enzyme is responsible for synthesizing a complementary messenger RNA (mRNA) transcript from a DNA template during transcription?
tcat-bio-38.explainHtml: RNA Polymerase binds to the promoter sequence and adds complementary ribonucleotides to build the pre-mRNA transcript in the 5' to 3' direction.

tcat-bio-39.qHtml: What laboratory technique is used to amplify millions of copies of a specific targeted DNA sequence in vitro?
tcat-bio-39.explainHtml: PCR (using Taq polymerase, primers, and thermal cycling) exponentially amplifies targeted DNA fragments in vitro.

tcat-bio-40.qHtml: How many nucleotide bases constitute a single genetic codon that specifies an amino acid in the genetic code?
tcat-bio-40.explainHtml: The genetic code is a triplet code where three consecutive mRNA bases form a codon specifying one amino acid or a termination signal.

tcat-bio-41.qHtml: What cross is used to determine whether an individual displaying a dominant phenotype is homozygous dominant or heterozygous?
optionsHtml: Test Cross (crossing the individual with a homozygous recessive individual)
Backcross with a homozygous dominant parent
tcat-bio-41.explainHtml: A test cross with a homozygous recessive (aa) reveals the genotype: if 100% dominant, parent was AA; if 50% dominant / 50% recessive, parent was Aa.

tcat-bio-42.qHtml: Why are X-linked recessive disorders such as Hemophilia and Red-Green Color Blindness observed significantly more frequently in biological males than females?
optionsHtml: Males are hemizygous (XY), possessing only one X chromosome; a single recessive allele on the X is expressed
Females inactivate both X chromosomes in somatic tissues
The Y chromosome actively represses the clotting factor genes
Males produce testosterone which accelerates mutation rates on the X chromosome
tcat-bio-42.explainHtml: Males have XY chromosomes; since there is no homologous counterpart on the Y chromosome, any recessive allele on the single X chromosome is automatically expressed.

tcat-bio-43.qHtml: Which enzyme seals nicks in the phosphodiester backbone by joining Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand during DNA replication?
tcat-bio-43.explainHtml: DNA ligase catalyzes formation of phosphodiester bonds between the 3'-OH of one Okazaki fragment and 5'-phosphate of the next fragment.

tcat-bio-44.qHtml: In agarose gel electrophoresis, how do DNA fragments migrate under an applied electric field?
optionsHtml: Negatively charged DNA fragments migrate toward the positive anode; smaller fragments move faster through the gel pores
Positively charged DNA fragments migrate toward the negative cathode; larger fragments move faster
Neutral DNA molecules separate based strictly on nucleotide base composition
DNA fragments remain stationary until cleaved by ultraviolet l
tcat-bio-44.explainHtml: DNA's phosphate backbone carries negative charges, driving migration toward the positive electrode; smaller fragments experience less matrix resistance and travel farther.

tcat-bio-45.qHtml: What are the three sequential thermal phases of a standard Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) cycle?
tcat-bio-45.explainHtml: PCR cycles: 94-96°C denatures dsDNA into single strands; 50-65°C anneals primers; 72°C enables thermostable Taq polymerase extension.

tcat-bio-46.qHtml: What is the function of Restriction Endonucleases (e.g., EcoRI) in recombinant DNA technology?
optionsHtml: They recognize specific palindromic DNA sequences and cleave phosphodiester bonds, generating sticky or blunt ends
They synthesize complementary DNA (cDNA) from mature mRNA transcripts
They add poly-A tails to the 3' ends of eukaryotic pre-mRNAs
They protect bacterial host ribosomes from viral bacteriophage infection
tcat-bio-46.explainHtml: Restriction enzymes recognize specific palindromic sequences (e.g. 5'-GAATTC-3') and produce cohesive ("sticky") or blunt overhangs suitable for recombinant insertion.

tcat-bio-47.qHtml: In eukaryotic mRNA post-transcriptional processing, what modifications must occur before mature mRNA exports from the nucleus?
optionsHtml: Addition of a 7-methylguanosine cap at the 5' end, a poly-A tail at the 3' end, and spliceosomal excision of non-coding introns
Removal of exons and joining of introns via reverse transcriptase
Phosphorylation of serine residues along the transcript backbone
Attachment of transfer RNA molecules directly to the promoter region
tcat-bio-47.explainHtml: Eukaryotic pre-mRNA undergoes 5' 7-methylguanosine capping, 3' polyadenylation (poly-A tail), and splicing out of introns by spliceosomes.

tcat-bio-48.qHtml: What is the molecular cause of Sickle Cell Anemia at the genetic and polypeptide level?
optionsHtml: A point mutation (GAG to GTG transversion) substituting Valine for Glutamic acid at position 6 of the β-globin chain
A frameshift deletion eliminating phenylalanine at position 508
A nonsense mutation terminating the α-globin chain prematurely
A chromosomal trisomy of chromosome 21 leading to defective heme synthesis
tcat-bio-48.explainHtml: Sickle cell is caused by a missense mutation in the β-globin gene (GAG to GTG), substituting hydrophilic Glutamic acid with hydrophobic Valine at residue 6.

tcat-bio-49.qHtml: How many total bones comprise the adult human skeletal system?
tcat-bio-49.explainHtml: The adult human skeleton consists of exactly 206 bones (80 axial and 126 appendicular).

tcat-bio-50.qHtml: Which type of joint provides the greatest range of movement in multiple planes, such as at the shoulder and hip joints?
tcat-bio-50.explainHtml: Ball-and-socket joints (glenohumeral and acetabulofemoral) allow multiaxial movement: flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, rotation, and circumduction.

tcat-bio-51.qHtml: What tough fibrous connective tissue bands connect skeletal muscles to bones?
tcat-bio-51.explainHtml: Tendons attach muscles to bones, while ligaments connect bones to other bones across joints.

tcat-bio-52.qHtml: What is the basic functional contractile unit of a skeletal muscle myofibril, bounded by two Z-discs?
tcat-bio-52.explainHtml: The sarcomere is the segment between two adjacent Z-lines and forms the repeating contractile unit of striated muscle.

tcat-bio-53.qHtml: According to the Sliding Filament Theory of muscle contraction, what happens to the sarcomere banding during active contraction?
optionsHtml: The H-zone and I-band narrow/disappear while the A-band length remains constant
The A-band shortens while the I-band length remains unchanged
Both the A-band and actin filaments lengthen
The Z-discs move farther apart as myosin filaments compress
tcat-bio-53.explainHtml: During contraction, actin filaments slide over myosin; the A-band (myosin length) stays constant while the I-band and H-zone shorten.

tcat-bio-54.qHtml: Which regulatory ion is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum to trigger cross-bridge cycling in skeletal muscle fibers?
optionsHtml: Calcium ions (Ca2⁺)
Magnesium ions (Mg2⁺)
tcat-bio-54.explainHtml: Action potentials traversing T-tubules cause terminal cisternae of the sarcoplasmic reticulum to release Ca2⁺ into the sarcoplasm.

tcat-bio-55.qHtml: What is the role of Troponin-C when calcium ions bind to it during muscle activation?
optionsHtml: It induces a conformational change that shifts Tropomyosin away from the myosin-binding sites on actin
It hydrolyzes ATP to ADP and inorganic phosphate on the myosin tail
It directly polymerizes G-actin into F-actin microfilaments
It pumps calcium back into the terminal cisternae
tcat-bio-55.explainHtml: Ca2⁺ binding to Troponin-C causes tropomyosin to move away from actin's myosin-binding sites, allowing myosin heads to form cross-bridges.

tcat-bio-56.qHtml: Which bone cell type is actively responsible for bone resorption and mineral matrix demineralization?
tcat-bio-56.explainHtml: Osteoclasts are multinucleated cells derived from monocyte lineage that secrete acids and enzymes to resorb bone matrix.

tcat-bio-57.qHtml: What causes the stiffening of muscles known as Rigor Mortis following death?
optionsHtml: Complete depletion of cellular ATP prevents the detachment of myosin heads from actin filaments
Excessive synthesis of lactic acid crystallizes the sarcoplasm
Spontaneous hyperpolarization of the motor neuron axon terminals
Uncontrolled degradation of troponin by lysosomal enzymes
tcat-bio-57.explainHtml: ATP binding is required to detach the myosin head from actin. After death, ATP depletion locks cross-bridges in place, causing rigor mortis.

tcat-bio-58.qHtml: In the microscopic architecture of compact bone, what structure occupies the central canal (Haversian canal) of each Osteon?
optionsHtml: Blood vessels (arterioles and venules) and nerve fibers
tcat-bio-58.explainHtml: Each Haversian canal contains blood vessels that nourish osteocytes in surrounding concentric lamellae, and associated nerve fibers.

tcat-bio-59.qHtml: What step during the cross-bridge cycle directly produces the "power stroke" that pulls actin toward the M-line?
optionsHtml: The release of inorganic phosphate (Pi) and ADP from the energized myosin head
The hydrolysis of ATP into ADP and Pi by myosin ATPase
The binding of a brand-new ATP molecule to the myosin active site
The influx of potassium ions through voltage-gated sarcolemma channels
tcat-bio-59.explainHtml: Release of Pi initiates the power stroke as the myosin head pivots ~45∘; ADP release follows, pulling the actin filament toward the center of the sarcomere.

tcat-bio-60.qHtml: How many pairs of ribs are classified as "True Ribs" (vertebrosternal ribs) because their costal cartilages attach directly to the sternum?
tcat-bio-60.explainHtml: Ribs 1-7 attach directly to the sternum via individual costal cartilages and are termed true (vertebrosternal) ribs.

tcat-bio-61.qHtml: What is the normal resting membrane potential of a typical mammalian neuron?
tcat-bio-61.explainHtml: The typical resting membrane potential of a resting neuron is approximately -70 millivolts, polarized negatively on the inside.

tcat-bio-62.qHtml: Which hormone is secreted by pancreatic β-cells in response to elevated blood glucose concentrations?
tcat-bio-62.explainHtml: Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans secrete insulin, promoting glucose uptake into tissues and glycogenesis.

tcat-bio-63.qHtml: What fatty insulating layer wraps around neuronal axons in the peripheral nervous system to accelerate nerve impulse conduction?
optionsHtml: Myelin sheath produced by Schwann cells
tcat-bio-63.explainHtml: Schwann cells wrap around PNS axons to form the myelin sheath, insulating the axon and enabling rapid saltatory conduction.

tcat-bio-64.qHtml: Which endocrine gland is historically called the "Master Gland" because its tropic hormones regulate other endocrine organs?
tcat-bio-64.explainHtml: The anterior pituitary secretes trophic hormones (TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH) regulating target endocrine glands throughout the body.

tcat-bio-65.qHtml: What ion movement causes the rapid depolarization phase of a neuronal action potential once the threshold voltage (-55 mV) is reached?
optionsHtml: Rapid influx of Na⁺ through voltage-gated sodium channels
Efflux of K⁺ through voltage-gated potassium channels
Influx of Cl⁻ through ligand-gated chloride channels
Active export of Ca2⁺ via plasma membrane calcium pumps
tcat-bio-65.explainHtml: Depolarization above threshold opens voltage-gated Na+ channels; Na+ rushes inward down its electrical and chemical gradient, reversing membrane potential toward +30 mV.

tcat-bio-66.qHtml: What is the physiological role of the Nodes of Ranvier along a myelinated nerve axon?
